words.en: Downtime is a period of time when a machine, system, or factory is not working, especially because it is broken or being repaired.

words.ex: The new machine improves the efficiency of production.
words.ex_cn: 这台新机器提高了生产的效率。
words.en: Efficiency is the ability to do something or produce something without wasting materials, time, or energy.

words.ex: The diamond is encased in glass.
words.ex_cn: 钻石被包裹在玻璃里。
words.en: To encase something means to cover or surround it completely in a case or close-fitting covering.

words.ex: The cows graze in the enclosure.
words.ex_cn: 奶牛在围场里吃草。
words.en: An enclosure is an area that is surrounded by a barrier or fence, often used to keep animals in or to protect something.

words.ex: He put the letter in an envelope.
words.ex_cn: 他把信装进了一个信封。
words.en: An envelope is a flat, usually rectangular or square, paper container for a letter, which you seal before you send it by post.

words.tr: v. 作…的摘要；成为…的缩影；概括；集中体现
words.ex: This painting epitomizes the beauty of nature.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画概括了自然的美。
words.en: If you say that something or someone epitomizes a particular thing, you mean that they are a perfect example of it.

words.tr: n. 均等；相等；相当；等价
words.ex: The equivalence of the two weights was proven by the scale.
words.ex_cn: 天平证明了这两个重量的均等。
words.en: Equivalence is the condition of being equal or equivalent in value, worth, function, etc.

words.tr: v. 举例说明；例证；例示
words.ex: This example exemplifies the rule clearly.
words.ex_cn: 这个例子清楚地说明了这条规则。
words.en: To exemplify means to be a typical example of something or to give an example of something.

words.tr: n. 专门知识；专门技能；
words.ex: His expertise in computers helps the team solve problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在计算机方面的专门知识帮助团队解决问题。
words.en: Expertise is special skill or knowledge that is acquired by training, study, or practice.

words.ex: The expiry of the contract will be next month.
words.ex_cn: 合同的满期将在下个月。
words.en: The end of the period for which something is valid.

words.tr: v. 删去（书籍中不合适之处）
words.ex: The teacher expurgated the old book to remove bad words.
words.ex_cn: 老师删改了这本旧书，去掉了不好的词语。
words.en: To remove material that is considered improper or offensive from (a book, movie, etc.).

words.tr: n. 扩展；延长期；延伸；电话分机；
words.ex: The company added an extension to its office building.
words.ex_cn: 公司为办公楼加了一个扩建部分。
words.en: An extension is a part that is added to something to make it longer or larger, or the act of adding this part.

words.ex: He won the game with great finesse.
words.ex_cn: 他以高超的技巧赢得了比赛。
words.en: If you finesse something, you handle it in a skillful and often slightly deceptive way.

words.ex: This lock is foolproof and easy to use.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁是万无一失的，而且容易使用。
words.en: A foolproof plan, system, or method is so well designed that it cannot go wrong or be used wrongly.

words.ex: The framework of the house is made of wood.
words.ex_cn: 房子的骨架是木制的。
words.en: A framework is a particular set of rules, ideas, or beliefs which you use in order to deal with problems or to decide what to do.

words.ex: He tried to gild the old box with gold paint.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用金漆把旧盒子镀金。
words.en: To cover something with a thin layer of gold or to make something seem more attractive or valuable than it really is.

words.ex: He hastened to finish his homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他赶紧在晚饭前写完作业。
words.en: If you hasten to do something, you quickly do it or quickly go somewhere.

words.ex: The rain was a hindrance to the game.
words.ex_cn: 雨水对比赛造成了妨碍。
words.en: A hindrance is a person or thing that makes it difficult for you to do something.

words.tr: v. 列出清单；逐条列记
words.ex: He will itemize his expenses on the form.
words.ex_cn: 他将在表格上逐项列出他的开支。
words.en: To itemize means to list things separately, often including details about each one.

words.tr: n. 管理不善；处理不当；弊政
words.ex: The town suffered from maladministration by its leaders.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇因领导者的管理不善而受苦。
words.en: Maladministration is the inefficient or dishonest management of an organization or government department.

words.ex: The weight of the box is measurable.
words.ex_cn: 这个箱子的重量是可以测量的。
words.en: If something is measurable, it can be measured or quantified.

words.ex: The mechanical toy moves with batteries.
words.ex_cn: 这个机械玩具用电池驱动。
words.en: Relating to machines or machinery; operated by or involving a machine or machines.

words.ex: He wrote a memorandum about the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一份关于会议的备忘录。
words.en: A memorandum is a written proposal or reminder, especially in a business context.

words.ex: I misplace my keys every morning.
words.ex_cn: 我每天早上都把钥匙弄丢。
words.en: If you misplace something, you lose it, usually only temporarily.

words.ex: The government will mobilize troops to help after the earthquake.
words.ex_cn: 政府将调动军队在地震后提供帮助。
words.en: If you mobilize a group of people, or if they mobilize, they prepare to take action, especially in a military context.

words.ex: The scientist observe the birds every morning.
words.ex_cn: 科学家每天早上观察鸟类。
words.en: If you observe a person or thing, you watch them carefully, especially in order to learn something about them.

words.ex: The big rock was an obstacle on the road.
words.ex_cn: 那块大石头是路上的障碍。
words.en: An obstacle is something which makes it difficult for you to go forward or to achieve something.

words.ex: I need a photocopy of my passport.
words.ex_cn: 我需要一份护照的影印本。
words.en: A photocopy is a copy of a document made by a photocopier.

words.tr: n. 陷阱；隐患；想不到的困难；
words.ex: Don't ignore the pitfall of skipping homework.
words.ex_cn: 不要忽视不做作业这个陷阱。
words.en: A pitfall is a likely mistake or problem in a situation.

words.ex: He has great proficiency in English.
words.ex_cn: 他的英语水平很高。
words.en: If you show proficiency in something, you show ability or skill at it.

words.ex: He will proofread the letter before sending it.
words.ex_cn: 他在发送这封信之前会校对。
words.en: To read and mark corrections on a text before it is published.

words.ex: The rectification of the error took only one day.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误的纠正只花了一天时间。
words.en: Rectification refers to the act of correcting something that is wrong or the process of converting alternating current to direct current in electrical engineering.

words.tr: v. 重新分配；再分配；重分配；
words.ex: The government will redistribute the money to poor families.
words.ex_cn: 政府将把钱重新分配给贫困家庭。
words.en: To redistribute something means to distribute it in a different way, so that it is shared more fairly or equally.

words.tr:
n. 申斥；谴责
v. 斥责；训斥
words.ex: The teacher gave him a reprimand for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他上课讲话而训斥了他。
words.en: A reprimand is a formal or official expression of disapproval, typically by a person in authority.

words.ex: The tree produces a sticky resin.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树会分泌一种粘稠的树脂。
words.en: A sticky substance secreted by some trees, used in varnishes, adhesives, and plastics.

words.tr: adj. 树脂的；树脂质的；树脂制的；
words.ex: The tree exudes a resinous sap.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树流出一种树脂状的树液。
words.en: A resinous substance contains resin or is similar to resin.

words.tr: n. 恢复；重新开始；继续进行
words.ex: The resumption of classes was delayed by one week.
words.ex_cn: 课程的恢复被推迟了一周。
words.en: The act of starting something again after a pause or interruption.

words.ex: After a long day at work, he treated himself to a rubdown.
words.ex_cn: 工作了一整天后，他给自己做了一次按摩。
words.en: A rubdown is a massage, especially one given to an athlete after exercise.

words.ex: The child developed a schema for sorting toys by color.
words.ex_cn: 孩子发展出了一种按颜色分类玩具的图式。
words.en: A schema is a representation of a plan or theory in the form of an outline or model.

words.tr: v.  系统化；图形化；扼要表示
words.ex: The professor tried to schematize the complex process for his students.
words.ex_cn: 教授试图为学生们系统化复杂的流程。
words.en: To arrange or represent something according to a plan, system, or scheme.

words.tr: v. 详细检查；仔细察看
words.ex: The teacher scrutinizes every student's homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师仔细检查每位学生的作业。
words.en: If you scrutinize something, you examine it very carefully, often to find out some information from it or about it.

words.tr:
n. （船舷上的）排水孔
v. 故意沉船；破坏计划
words.ex: The sailor cleaned the scupper to let water drain out of the boat.
words.ex_cn: 水手清理了排水孔，让水从船上流出去。
words.en: To scupper something means to cause it to fail or to be ruined, especially a plan or a project. As a noun, it refers to an opening in the side of a ship at deck level that allows water to run off.

words.ex: The contract stipulates that payments must be made monthly.
words.ex_cn: 合同规定付款必须按月进行。
words.en: If you stipulate a condition or stipulate that something must be done, you say clearly that it must be done.

words.tr: v. （使）变直；（使）变平；（使）变整齐；
words.ex: He straightened the crooked picture on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 他把墙上歪斜的画扶直了。
words.en: To make something straight or to put something in order.

words.ex: The two companies made a tie-up to share resources.
words.ex_cn: 两家公司达成了合作以共享资源。
words.en: A tie-up is a connection or association between two or more things, especially a business partnership or collaboration.

chapters.name: 工作学习 职场风云 重点词

words.tr: adj. 负有责任的；应作解释的
words.ex: He is accountable for his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他要为自己的错误负责。
words.en: If you are accountable to someone for something that you do, you are responsible for it and must be prepared to justify your actions to that person.

words.ex: He is adept at solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长解决数学问题。
words.en: Someone who is adept at something is very skilled at it.

words.tr: adj. 可容许的；可接纳的
words.ex: The evidence is admissible in court.
words.ex_cn: 这些证据在法庭上是可接受的。
words.en: If something is admissible, it is allowed or acceptable, especially in a court of law.

words.ex: My parents give me a weekly allowance.
words.ex_cn: 我父母每周给我零用钱。
words.en: An allowance is money that is given regularly, usually to a child, by their parents, or by the government to someone who is unemployed or ill.

words.tr:
adj. 交替的；轮流的；间隔的；
v. （使）交替；（使）轮流；
words.ex: We take alternate days off work.
words.ex_cn: 我们隔天休息一次。
words.en: If something alternates between two things, it repeatedly changes from one to the other and back again.

words.ex: He submitted his application for the job last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周提交了那份工作申请。
words.en: An application is a formal request, often written, for something such as a job, a place at a university, or permission to do something. It can also refer to the act of putting something to a special use or purpose, or a program or piece of software designed to perform a specific function.

words.ex: He wants to apply for a job at the bank.
words.ex_cn: 他想申请银行的工作。
words.en: To make a formal request, usually in writing, for something such as a job, a place at a university, or permission to do something.

words.tr:
n. 奖品；裁定；
v. 授予；
words.ex: He received an award for best student.
words.ex_cn: 他获得了最佳学生奖。
words.en: An award is a prize or other mark of recognition given in honor of an achievement.

words.ex: The heavy workload became a burden for her.
words.ex_cn: 繁重的工作量成了她的负担。
words.en: A burden is a heavy load that is difficult to carry, or a duty or responsibility that is hard to bear.

words.ex: He has the capacity to solve hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有能力解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: The capacity of a place or container is the amount of things or people that it can hold.

words.ex: He is a competent teacher who helps students easily.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有能力的老师，能轻松帮助学生。
words.en: If you are competent to do something, you have the skills, abilities, or experience necessary to do it well.

words.tr:
v. 补充；与…相辅相成；
n. 补足物；补语；余角；
words.ex: The red scarf complements her blue coat.
words.ex_cn: 这条红围巾补充了她的蓝外套。
words.en: To complement something means to make it complete or perfect by adding something to it.

words.ex: The hotel gave us complimentary breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 酒店免费赠送了我们早餐。
words.en: If something is complimentary, it is given or done free of charge. It can also mean expressing a compliment; praising or approving.

words.ex: He is conversant with basic math.
words.ex_cn: 他熟悉基础数学。
words.en: If you are conversant with something, you are familiar with it and able to deal with it.

words.ex: He wore a decent shirt to the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一件像样的衬衫去面试。
words.en: Decent is used to describe something which is considered to be of an acceptable standard or quality.

words.ex: The teacher designated him as the group leader.
words.ex_cn: 老师指派他为组长。
words.en: If you designate someone or something as a particular thing, you formally give them that description or name.

words.ex: The power will devolve to the local government.
words.ex_cn: 权力将下放给地方政府。
words.en: If you devolve power, authority, or responsibility to a less powerful person or group, or if it devolves upon them, it is transferred to them.

words.ex: He dismissed her advice and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他不理会她的建议，走开了。
words.en: If you dismiss someone, you send them away or allow them to leave.

words.tr: v. 取代；迫使…离开家园；
words.ex: The new robot will displace the workers on the assembly line.
words.ex_cn: 这个新机器人将取代装配线上的工人。
words.en: To displace something or someone means to take their place or to force them to leave their usual place or role.

words.ex: The division of the cake was fair.
words.ex_cn: 蛋糕的划分是公平的。
words.en: The act or process of dividing something into parts or the state of being divided.

words.tr:
v. 使降低；使降级
n. 下坡路
words.ex: The company decided to downgrade the software version.
words.ex_cn: 公司决定将软件版本降级。
words.en: To downgrade something means to reduce its quality, value, or status.

words.ex: The efficacy of the medicine is clear.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物的效果是明显的。
words.en: The ability to produce a desired or intended result.

words.ex: He uses an efficient way to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种高效的方法解决数学问题。
words.en: If something or someone is efficient, they are able to do tasks successfully, without wasting time or energy.

words.ex: Exercise can elevate your mood.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提升你的情绪。
words.en: To elevate something means to raise it to a higher position or level, either physically or in terms of its status or importance.

words.tr: adj. 有资格的；合格的；合意的；
words.ex: He is eligible to vote because he is 18 years old.
words.ex_cn: 他年满18岁，有资格投票。
words.en: Someone who is eligible for something is qualified or allowed to do it.

words.ex: The new tool enables him to finish work faster.
words.ex_cn: 这个新工具使他能够更快地完成工作。
words.en: If someone or something enables you to do a particular thing, they give you the opportunity or means to do it.

words.tr: v. 参与；从事；吸引；与…建立密切关系；
words.ex: He engages in community volunteer work.
words.ex_cn: 他参与社区志愿工作。
words.en: To engage means to occupy, attract, or involve someone or oneself in a particular activity or situation.

words.tr: v. （使）参与；从事于；雇佣；“engage”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 忙着的；
words.ex: The teacher engaged the students in a group discussion.
words.ex_cn: 老师让学生们参与了一次小组讨论。
words.en: If you are engaged in an activity, you are doing it or involved in it. If you are engaged to someone, you have agreed to marry them.

words.ex: The computer will execute the program quickly.
words.ex_cn: 计算机将快速执行该程序。
words.en: To execute means to carry out or put into effect a plan, order, or course of action. It can also refer to the act of legally killing someone as a punishment.

words.tr:
n. 决策人；行政官；管理人员；
adj. 行政的；决策的；
words.ex: The executive decided to launch the new product.
words.ex_cn: 这位决策人决定推出新产品。
words.en: An executive is a person who has a senior management position in a business or other organization.

words.tr:
adj. 就职的；开幕的；创立的
n. 就职演说
words.ex: He gave his inaugural speech last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚发表了就职演讲。
words.en: An inaugural event or speech is the first in a series planned to celebrate or introduce something.

words.tr: adj. 即将开始的；新任的；
words.ex: The incoming class will start next week.
words.ex_cn: 即将开始的班级将在下周开课。
words.en: An incoming thing or person is arriving or being received.

words.ex: Water is indispensable for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必不可少的。
words.en: Absolutely necessary or essential.

words.tr: v. 使正式就任；给予职位
words.ex: They inducted the new mayor with a ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过一场仪式使新市长正式就任。
words.en: To induct someone into a position or organization means to formally install them in that position or officially introduce them into that organization.

words.tr: adj. 无能的；不起作用的
words.ex: His attempts to solve the problem were ineffectual.
words.ex_cn: 他试图解决问题的尝试是无效的。
words.en: If someone or something is ineffectual, they lack the ability or power to achieve something.

words.tr: adj. 不适当的；无能的；笨拙的
words.ex: His inept reply made the situation worse.
words.ex_cn: 他不适当的回答让情况变得更糟。
words.en: If you say that someone is inept, you are criticizing them because they do something with a complete lack of skill.

words.ex: He inferred that she was tired from her yawns.
words.ex_cn: 他从她的哈欠推断出她很累。
words.en: If you infer that something is the case, you decide that it is true on the basis of information that you already have.

words.ex: This product is inferior to the other one.
words.ex_cn: 这个产品比另一个差。
words.en: If one person or thing is inferior to another, they are not as good, important, or valuable as the other person or thing.

words.ex: He will initiate a new project next week.
words.ex_cn: 他将在下周发起一个新项目。
words.en: To initiate something means to start it or cause it to happen.

words.tr: n. 倡议；主动权；自发性；措施；
words.ex: The school launched an initiative to reduce plastic use.
words.ex_cn: 学校发起了一项减少塑料使用的倡议。
words.en: An initiative is an important act or statement that is intended to solve a problem.

words.ex: His insight helped the team solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他的洞察力帮助团队解决了问题。
words.en: If you gain insight or an insight into a complex situation or problem, you gain an accurate and deep understanding of it.

words.ex: Her story inspires me to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 她的故事激励我更加努力。
words.en: If someone or something inspires you to do something new or unusual, they make you want to do it.

words.ex: The water supply is insufficient for the whole village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对整个村庄来说是不充分的。
words.en: If something is insufficient, it is not enough for a particular purpose.

words.tr:
adj. （职位或等级）较低的；年幼的；（高中、大学的）三年级学生；
n. 年幼者；
words.ex: He is a junior employee in the company.
words.ex_cn: 他是公司里职位较低的员工。
words.en: A junior person is younger or has a lower position than another person.

words.ex: He has a knack for fixing bikes.
words.ex_cn: 他有修自行车的技巧。
words.en: A knack is a special skill or ability that someone has, especially one that is hard to explain or teach.

words.tr: n. 实际知识；技术；窍门
words.ex: He has the know-how to fix the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他有修理这台机器的诀窍。
words.en: Practical knowledge or expertise in a particular field or area.

words.ex: The car made a lateral move to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 汽车横向移动以避开狗。
words.en: Relating to the side or sides; situated at or extending to the side.

words.tr: n. 解雇；活动停止期间
words.ex: He got a layoff last month.
words.ex_cn: 他上个月被裁员了。
words.en: A layoff is the termination of employment of an employee or, more commonly, a group of employees for business reasons, such as the decision of the company to downsize its operations.

words.tr: adj. 权宜的；临时凑合的；
words.ex: He used a makeshift table made of boxes and a board.
words.ex_cn: 他用箱子和木板做了一个权宜的桌子。
words.en: A makeshift object or arrangement is one that is made or done quickly and without much skill, using whatever is available at the time.

words.tr: adj. 可管理的；可应付的；可处理的；
words.ex: The project is manageable if we work together.
words.ex_cn: 如果我们一起合作，这个项目是可以管理的。
words.en: If you describe something as manageable, you mean that it is easy to control or deal with.

words.tr:
adj. 手工的；体力的；
n. 说明书；
words.ex: He made a manual copy of the letter.
words.ex_cn: 他手工抄写了一封信。
words.en: A manual is a book which tells you how to do something or how a piece of machinery works.

words.ex: The norm in this school is to arrive on time.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校的准则就是准时到校。
words.en: A norm is an official standard or level that organizations are expected to reach.

words.ex: He is a novice at playing the guitar.
words.ex_cn: 他是个吉他新手。
words.en: A novice is someone who has just started learning or doing something and does not have much experience.

words.ex: The cat occupies the sofa all day.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫整天占据着沙发。
words.en: If people or things occupy a place, they are in it or fill it.

words.tr: n. 几率；不利条件；不平等；
words.ex: The odds of winning the lottery are very low.
words.ex_cn: 中彩票的几率非常低。
words.en: The odds are the chances that a particular thing will happen.

words.ex: He opted to stay home instead of going out.
words.ex_cn: 他选择待在家里而不是出去。
words.en: If you opt for something, or opt to do something, you choose it or decide to do it in preference to anything else.

words.ex: Free lunch is a perk of this job.
words.ex_cn: 免费午餐是这份工作的一个额外补贴。
words.en: If someone perks up or if something perks them up, they become more cheerful or lively.

words.ex: His answer was pertinent to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答与问题相关。
words.en: Something that is pertinent is relevant to a particular subject.

words.ex: He showed his portfolio to the art teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他向美术老师展示了他作品集。
words.en: A portfolio is a set of pictures by someone, or photographs of examples of their work, which they use when entering competitions or applying for work.

words.tr: n. 额外费用；保险费；溢价；
words.ex: You need to pay a premium for faster delivery.
words.ex_cn: 你需要支付额外费用才能享受更快的配送。
words.en: A premium is an amount of money that you pay regularly to an insurance company for an insurance policy, or an amount of money that is more than usual for a product or service because it is of higher quality.

words.ex: His profession is a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他的职业是教师。
words.en: A profession is a type of job that requires advanced education or training.

words.ex: He is proficient in playing the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他弹钢琴很熟练。
words.en: If you are proficient in something, you can do it well because you have learned how to do it.

words.tr: adj. 有希望的；有前途的； v. 承诺；答应；“promise”的现在分词；
words.ex: The young boy is a promising student.
words.ex_cn: 这个小男孩是个有希望的学生。
words.en: Showing signs of future success or achievement.

words.tr: v. 促进；推动；宣传；推销；
words.ex: Exercise can promote good health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进健康。
words.en: To promote means to help something to happen, develop, or increase, or to raise someone to a higher position or rank.

words.ex: The prospect of a better job makes him happy.
words.ex_cn: 更好工作的前景让他感到高兴。
words.en: A prospect is the possibility that something will happen, or a view of a wide area.

words.ex: He is a prospective student at Harvard.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的预期学生。
words.en: Prospective is used to describe someone or something that is expected or likely to happen or be in the future.

words.ex: He took a provisional job until he found a better one.
words.ex_cn: 他在找到更好的工作之前做了一份临时工作。
words.en: Something that is provisional is temporary and likely to be changed or replaced in the future.

words.tr: v. 使合格；使具有资格；
words.ex: He studied hard to qualify for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习以获得这份工作的资格。
words.en: To qualify means to meet the necessary conditions or standards to be eligible for something or to perform a particular role.

words.tr: v.  合理化； 使合理
words.ex: He tries to rationalize his bad choices.
words.ex_cn: 他试图为自己的错误选择找借口。
words.en: To rationalize something means to try to find reasons to explain or justify it, often when these reasons are not really good ones.

words.ex: The government must redress the unfair law.
words.ex_cn: 政府必须纠正这部不公平的法律。
words.en: If you redress something such as a wrong or a complaint, you do something to correct it or to improve things for the person who has been wronged.

words.ex: The extra chair is redundant because we have enough seats.
words.ex_cn: 这把额外的椅子是多余的，因为我们已经有足够的座位了。
words.en: If you are made redundant, your employer tells you to leave because your job is no longer necessary or because there is no more work for you.

words.tr:
v. 倒退；退步；退化
n. 倒退；退步；退化
words.ex: The patient regressed to a childlike state after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后，病人退回到了孩童般的状态。
words.en: If you regress, you return to a previous and less advanced stage of development.

words.ex: The regression of the society was caused by war and poverty.
words.ex_cn: 社会的倒退是由战争和贫困造成的。
words.en: Regression is a statistical method used to examine the relationship between two or more variables. In a broader sense, it refers to the process of returning to a former or less developed state.

words.ex: The regularity of his daily routine helps him stay focused.
words.ex_cn: 他日常作息的规律性帮助他保持专注。
words.en: The quality or state of being regular; the condition of being governed by or according to rules, principles, or established customs.

words.ex: The company will reinstate his job next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将恢复他的工作。
words.en: If you reinstate someone, you give them back a job or position which had been taken away from them.

words.ex: The team was relegated to the second division after losing all their games.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在输掉所有比赛后被降级到第二级别联赛。
words.en: If you relegate someone or something to a less important position, you give them this position.

words.ex: The company will remunerate you for your extra work.
words.ex_cn: 公司会为你的额外工作支付报酬。
words.en: To remunerate someone means to pay them for work that they have done.

words.tr: v. 重新定位；使适应；改变方针；调整
words.ex: He had to reorient his goals after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他在失业后不得不重新调整自己的目标。
words.en: To change the focus or direction of something.

words.tr: v. 重塑；改造；给…以新形态
words.ex: He wants to reshape his life after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他想在事故后重新塑造自己的生活。
words.en: To reshape something means to change its form or structure, often in order to improve it.

words.tr: v. 辞职；使…顺从于（做）某事；
words.ex: He decided to resign from his job.
words.ex_cn: 他决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you resign from a job or position, you formally announce that you are leaving it.

words.ex: After a short break, he resumed his work.
words.ex_cn: 短暂休息后，他继续工作。
words.en: If you resume an activity or if it resumes, it begins again or continues after an interruption.

words.ex: He went back to retrieve his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他回去取回他的钥匙。
words.en: To retrieve something means to get it back from somewhere, especially after it has been lost or taken away.

words.tr: adj. 严格的；缜密的；严密的；
words.ex: The teacher is rigorous about homework deadlines.
words.ex_cn: 老师对作业截止日期要求严格。
words.en: If you are rigorous in something, you are very thorough and strict in the way you do it.

words.ex: The selection of books was very good.
words.ex_cn: 书籍的选择非常好。
words.en: The act of carefully choosing someone or something as the best or most suitable.

words.tr: adj. 选择性的；精挑细选的；
words.ex: He is selective about what he eats.
words.ex_cn: 他对吃的东西很挑剔。
words.en: If you are selective, you choose things carefully, for example, the things that you buy or do.

words.ex: The staff at the hotel are very friendly.
words.ex_cn: 酒店的职员非常友好。
words.en: The people who work for a particular organization or company, or a group of officers assisting a commanding officer.

words.tr:
n. (从事某项活动的)规定期限
v. 吝惜；节省
words.ex: He did a short stint as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他短暂地当过一段时间老师。
words.en: A stint is a fixed period of time during which someone does a particular job or activity.

words.ex: His submission to the boss ended the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 他对老板的屈服结束了这场冲突。
words.en: The act of submitting something to someone for their decision or consideration; the state of being submissive or obedient.

words.ex: He will submit his homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会提交他的作业。
words.en: To yield or surrender (oneself) to the will or authority of another.

words.ex: His opinion is subordinate to the manager's.
words.ex_cn: 他的意见比经理的次要。
words.en: If someone is your subordinate, they have a less important position than you in the organization that you both work for.

words.ex: The big company owns a subsidiary that makes phones.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司拥有一家生产手机的附属公司。
words.en: A subsidiary is a company which is part of a larger and more important company.

words.ex: The succession of rain made the ground wet.
words.ex_cn: 连续的雨水使地面变湿了。
words.en: A succession of things of the same kind is a number of them that exist or happen one after the other.

words.ex: He won three successive championships.
words.ex_cn: 他连续赢得了三届冠军。
words.en: Following one after the other without interruption.

words.ex: This phone is superior to the old one.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机比旧的更好。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as superior, you mean that they are better than other people or things.

words.ex: He took a temporary job during summer.
words.ex_cn: 他在暑假期间做了一份短暂的工作。
words.en: Something that is temporary lasts for only a limited time.

words.ex: The teacher will terminate the class at 5 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 老师将在下午5点结束课程。
words.en: To terminate something means to bring it to an end or to stop it from continuing.

words.tr: adj. 易驾驭的；温顺的；易处理的
words.ex: The dog is so tractable that it follows commands effortlessly.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗非常驯良，能轻松地服从命令。
words.en: If you say that a person, problem, or device is tractable, you mean that they can be easily controlled or dealt with.

words.tr:
v. 转移；转让；调任；
n. 转移；转让；调任；
words.ex: He will transfer the money to his bank account.
words.ex_cn: 他将把钱转到他的银行账户。
words.en: If you transfer something or someone from one place to another, or they transfer from one place to another, they go from the first place to the second.

words.ex: The joy was transient, like a brief smile.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是短暂的，像一个短暂的微笑。
words.en: If you describe something as transient, you mean that it lasts only for a short time.

words.tr: n. 参与人（数）；装束；产量；清理
words.ex: The turnout for the election was very high.
words.ex_cn: 这次选举的投票率很高。
words.en: The number of people attending or participating in an event, especially a political meeting or election.

words.tr: n. 优势；有利条件；好处；
words.ex: His height gives him an advantage in basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他的身高在篮球中给了他优势。
words.en: An advantage is a factor or circumstance that puts you in a favorable or superior position.

words.ex: He enjoyed the adventure through vicarious experiences in books.
words.ex_cn: 他通过书中的间接体验享受了冒险。
words.en: Experienced or felt by watching, hearing about, or reading about someone else rather than by doing something yourself.

chapters.name: 工作学习 职场风云 认知词

words.tr: phrase. 临时的；特别的；专为特定目的而设的
words.ex: They made an ad hoc decision to cancel the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他们临时决定取消会议。
words.en: Created or done for a particular purpose as necessary.

words.ex: Children are often adaptable to new environments.
words.ex_cn: 孩子通常能适应新环境。
words.en: If someone or something is adaptable, they are able to change their ideas or behaviour in order to deal with new situations.

words.ex: The meeting will adjourn at 5 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 会议将在下午5点休会。
words.en: If a meeting or trial is adjourned, or if it adjourns, it is stopped for a short time.

words.ex: He works on an advisory committee.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个顾问委员会工作。
words.en: An advisory is a report or announcement that gives advice or information about a particular subject.

words.tr: n. 年金；养老金；年金保险
words.ex: He receives an annuity every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每个月领取一笔年金。
words.en: An annuity is a fixed sum of money paid to someone each year, typically for the rest of their life.

words.tr: adj. 可觉察的；很可观的
words.ex: There is an appreciable difference in his grades.
words.ex_cn: 他的成绩有明显的差异。
words.en: If something is appreciable, it is large enough to be noticed or considered important.

words.ex: He is an apprentice in a car repair shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是汽车修理店的一名学徒。
words.en: An apprentice is a young person who works for someone in order to learn their skill.

words.ex: He has a natural aptitude for math.
words.ex_cn: 他天生有数学天赋。
words.en: An aptitude is a natural ability to do something.

words.tr: n. 奖金；红利；额外津贴；
words.ex: He received a bonus for working overtime.
words.ex_cn: 他因加班获得了奖金。
words.en: A bonus is an extra amount of money that is added to someone's pay, usually because they have worked very hard.

words.ex: His bounty helped the poor family survive winter.
words.ex_cn: 他的慷慨帮助这个贫困家庭度过了冬天。
words.en: If you say that someone is bountiful or does something in a bountiful way, you mean that they are very generous or that they give a lot of something.

words.tr: n. 公告；布告；公报；新闻简报；
words.ex: The school posted a bulletin about the holiday schedule.
words.ex_cn: 学校张贴了一份关于假期安排的公告。
words.en: A bulletin is a short news report on the radio or television. A bulletin is also a short printed newspaper or leaflet that gives information about a particular group or organization.

words.tr: n. 清洁女工；（按日雇用的）女佣
words.ex: The charwoman cleans the office every night.
words.ex_cn: 女清洁工每天晚上打扫办公室。
words.en: A charwoman is a woman who is employed to clean houses or offices, typically on a part-time basis.

words.ex: My colleague helped me with the report.
words.ex_cn: 我的同事帮我完成了报告。
words.en: A colleague is someone you work with, especially in a professional job.

words.ex: His salary is commensurate with his experience.
words.ex_cn: 他的薪水与他的经验相称。
words.en: If the level of one thing is commensurate with another, the first level is in proportion to the second.

words.tr: n. 关键点；最难点；症结
words.ex: The crux of the problem is money.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题的关键是钱。
words.en: The most important or difficult part of a problem or issue.

words.ex: The curator arranged the paintings in the museum.
words.ex_cn: 馆长在博物馆里布置了这些画作。
words.en: A curator is someone who is in charge of the objects or works of art in a museum or art gallery.

words.ex: The manager decided to demote him for poor performance.
words.ex_cn: 经理因他表现不佳决定降职他。
words.en: If someone is demoted, they are given a lower rank or a less important position than they had before.

words.tr: v. 罢免；废黜；宣誓证明
words.ex: The people deposed the corrupt leader.
words.ex_cn: 人民推翻了腐败的领导人。
words.en: To depose someone means to remove them from a position of power or authority, especially a monarch or political leader.

words.tr: n. 沉积（物）；革职；宣誓证词；作证书
words.ex: Sediment deposition forms layers on the riverbed.
words.ex_cn: 沉积物在河床上形成层状结构。
words.en: The act of depositing something, especially a layer of a substance formed by natural processes, or the giving of testimony under oath.

words.ex: The deputation met the mayor to ask for help.
words.ex_cn: 代表团会见了市长，请求帮助。
words.en: A deputation is a group of people appointed to represent others, especially in a formal meeting or negotiation.

words.ex: The deputy signed the document for the manager.
words.ex_cn: 代理人替经理签署了文件。
words.en: A deputy is a person who is appointed to act as a substitute for another, especially in a position of authority.

words.ex: I looked up his phone number in the directory.
words.ex_cn: 我在姓名地址录里查了他的电话号码。
words.en: A directory is a book or list which gives names, addresses, and other information about people or organizations.

words.ex: The old bridge began disintegration after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥在风暴后开始崩解。
words.en: The process of breaking into small parts or pieces and losing strength or effectiveness.

words.ex: His dismissal made him very sad.
words.ex_cn: 他的被解雇让他非常难过。
words.en: The act of officially removing someone from their job, or the act of sending someone away or allowing them to leave.

words.tr: n. 工装裤；粗布工作服；粗棉布裤子
words.ex: He wears blue dungarees to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿蓝色工装裤去上班。
words.en: Dungarees are a type of clothing consisting of trousers with a bib held up by straps over the shoulders, often made of denim or heavy cotton.

words.tr:
n. 社论；
adj. 编辑的；
words.ex: The newspaper published an editorial about climate change.
words.ex_cn: 报纸发表了一篇关于气候变化的社论。
words.en: An editorial is an article in a newspaper which gives the opinion of the editor or publisher on a topic or item of news.

words.ex: The elite of the city often meet at private clubs.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的精英经常在私人俱乐部会面。
words.en: You can refer to the most powerful, rich, or talented people within a particular group, place, or society as the elite.

words.ex: He found employment after graduating from university.
words.ex_cn: 他大学毕业后找到了工作。
words.en: the condition of having paid work

words.ex: He went on an errand to buy milk.
words.ex_cn: 他去买牛奶了。
words.en: An errand is a short journey that you make in order to do a job for someone, for example when you go to a shop to buy something for them.

words.ex: The book contains esoteric ideas that only experts understand.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了只有专家才能理解的深奥思想。
words.en: Intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with a specialized knowledge or interest.

words.ex: He bought apples, oranges, etceteras.
words.ex_cn: 他买了苹果、橙子和其他东西。
words.en: Used at the end of a list to indicate that further, similar items are included.

words.tr:
n. 旗；旗帜；信号旗；
v. 用旗标记；
words.ex: The flag waves in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 旗帜在风中飘扬。
words.en: A flag is a piece of cloth with a special design or colors that is used as a symbol, or to give a signal.

words.tr: n. 安排者（尤指用不正当手段来操办事情的人）
words.ex: He was known as a political fixer who could smooth over any scandal.
words.ex_cn: 他被称为能平息任何丑闻的政治操盘手。
words.en: A fixer is someone who arranges things or solves problems for other people, especially in a way that may not be completely honest or legal.

words.ex: The company values flexibility in work hours.
words.ex_cn: 公司重视工作时间的灵活性。
words.en: Flexibility refers to the quality of bending easily without breaking, or the ability to be easily modified to respond to altered circumstances or conditions.

words.ex: He works on flexitime so he can leave early on Fridays.
words.ex_cn: 他实行弹性工作时间，所以周五可以早点下班。
words.en: Flexitime is a system of working a set number of hours with the starting and finishing times chosen within agreed limits by the employee.

words.ex: He put the papers in a red folder.
words.ex_cn: 他把文件放进了一个红色的活页夹。
words.en: A folder is a thin piece of cardboard or plastic in which you can keep loose papers.

words.ex: The forester walks through the forest to check the trees.
words.ex_cn: 林务员在森林中行走以检查树木。
words.en: A forester is a person who is in charge of the management and conservation of a forest.

words.tr: n. 取得成果；实现；完成
words.ex: The project finally came to fruition after years of hard work.
words.ex_cn: 经过多年的努力，这个项目终于完成了。
words.en: The realization or fulfillment of a plan or project.

words.tr: n. 手巧的人；杂工；能工巧匠
words.ex: The handyman fixed the broken chair.
words.ex_cn: 技工修好了坏掉的椅子。
words.en: A handyman is a person who is skilled at a wide range of repairs, typically around the home. These tasks include trade skills, repair work, maintenance work, are both interior and exterior, and are sometimes described as 'side work', 'odd jobs' or 'fix-up tasks'. Specifically, these jobs could be light plumbing jobs, light electrical jobs, or work that could be described as 'handyman' tasks.

words.ex: She practices housewifery every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天都在做家务。
words.en: The management of a household; the duties and activities associated with running a home.

words.ex: He is an illustrator who draws pictures for children's books.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位为儿童书籍画画的插画师。
words.en: An illustrator is an artist who draws pictures, especially for books.

words.tr: adj. 在职的；负有义务的；
words.ex: The incumbent mayor won the election again.
words.ex_cn: 现任市长再次赢得了选举。
words.en: An incumbent is someone who currently holds a particular office or position, especially in politics. It can also refer to something that is necessary as a duty or responsibility.

words.ex: The induction of the new mayor will be held next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 新市长的就职典礼将在下周一举行。
words.en: Induction is the process or action of inducting someone to a position or organization, or the process of reasoning from specific cases to general rules.

words.ex: He is inquiring about the train schedule.
words.ex_cn: 他正在询问火车时刻表。
words.en: If someone has an inquiring mind, they are interested in learning about many different things.

words.tr: adj. 无法解决的；不能溶解的
words.ex: The problem is insoluble with the current tools.
words.ex_cn: 用当前的工具无法解决这个问题。
words.en: If a problem or mystery is insoluble, it is impossible to solve or explain.

words.tr: adj. 无法克服的；难以解决的；不可逾越的
words.ex: The problem seemed insurmountable.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题似乎无法克服。
words.en: If you describe something as insurmountable, you mean that it is so great or severe that it cannot be dealt with.

words.ex: She will lengthen the dress for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她会把裙子改长一点去参加派对。
words.en: To make something longer, or to become longer.

words.ex: The company improved its logistics to deliver packages faster.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司改进了物流，以更快地配送包裹。
words.en: Logistics refers to the detailed organization and implementation of a complex operation.

words.ex: He has a managerial role in the company.
words.ex_cn: 他在公司中担任管理职务。
words.en: relating to the job of a manager

words.ex: The mode of transportation is a bike.
words.ex_cn: 出行的方式是骑自行车。
words.en: A mode is a particular way or style in which something is done or experienced.

words.ex: The furniture is modular, so you can change its shape.
words.ex_cn: 这套家具是组合式的，你可以改变它的形状。
words.en: A modular system or method is one in which the parts can be separated and recombined easily, often used to describe furniture, software, or buildings that are made up of separate components.

words.ex: He chose an occupational therapy course.
words.ex_cn: 他选择了一门职业治疗课程。
words.en: Relating to a job or profession.

words.ex: We optimize the route to save time.
words.ex_cn: 我们优化路线以节省时间。
words.en: To optimize something means to make it as good or as effective as possible.

words.tr: n. 严酷的考验；痛苦的经历；煎熬
words.ex: He went through a long ordeal before he found peace.
words.ex_cn: 他在找到平静之前经历了一段漫长的磨难。
words.en: An ordeal is a very unpleasant and prolonged experience.

words.ex: The classroom is orderly and clean.
words.ex_cn: 教室整洁有序。
words.en: If something is done in an orderly fashion or manner, it is done in a well-organized and controlled way.

words.ex: His painting shows great originality.
words.ex_cn: 他的画作展现了极大的独创性。
words.en: The quality of being new and original in a way that is not derived from something else.

words.ex: The outcome of the game was a tie.
words.ex_cn: 比赛的结果是平局。
words.en: The outcome of an activity, process, or situation is the situation that exists at the end of it.

words.ex: His oversight caused the project to fail.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致项目失败。
words.en: An oversight is a mistake that is made by not noticing something or by forgetting to do something.

words.ex: The company updated the payroll last Friday.
words.ex_cn: 公司上星期五更新了职工工资册。
words.en: A payroll is a list of employees and the amount of money they are to be paid, or the total amount of money paid to the employees of a company.

words.tr:
n. 尖木桩；警戒哨；纠察队（队员）
v. 进行罢工纠察
words.ex: The fence has wooden pickets to keep animals out.
words.ex_cn: 这个围栏有木制尖木桩，用来防止动物进入。
words.en: A picket is a person or group of people who stand outside a place of work or other venue to protest or to try to persuade others not to enter during a strike. It can also refer to a pointed stake or post driven into the ground, typically to form a fence or to tether a horse.

words.tr:
n. 枢；中心；旋转
v. 在枢轴上转动；以…为中心
words.ex: The door pivots on a hinge.
words.ex_cn: 门围绕一个铰链旋转。
words.en: A pivot is the central point, pin, or shaft on which a mechanism turns or oscillates. It can also refer to the central or most important person or thing in a situation.

words.ex: This decision is pivotal for the company's future.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对公司未来至关重要。
words.en: Of crucial importance in relation to the development or success of something else.

words.ex: The practicality of this tool makes it popular among workers.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具的实用性使它在工人中很受欢迎。
words.en: The quality of being suitable for a particular purpose or situation; the ability to be put to practical use.

words.tr: n. 前任；前辈；原有事物
words.ex: He became the new manager, replacing his predecessor.
words.ex_cn: 他成为了新经理，接替了他的前任。
words.en: A predecessor is someone who had a job or a position before someone else, or something that comes before another thing in time or in a series.

words.ex: He took a preparatory course before starting university.
words.ex_cn: 他在上大学之前参加了一个预备课程。
words.en: Preparatory means relating to or done in preparation for something.

words.ex: He is a pro player in esports.
words.ex_cn: 他是电子竞技的专业选手。
words.en: A pro is someone who is professional in a particular activity or sport, or someone who supports a particular idea or course of action.

words.ex: The new policy is problematic for small businesses.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策对小企业来说成问题。
words.en: If something is problematic, it involves problems and is difficult to deal with or solve.

words.ex: She is the quintessence of grace.
words.ex_cn: 她是优雅的典范。
words.en: The quintessence of something is the most perfect or typical example of it.

words.tr: n. 轻易放弃的人；半途而废者
words.ex: He was labeled a quitter after he dropped out of the marathon.
words.ex_cn: 他在马拉松比赛中途退出后，被贴上了半途而废者的标签。
words.en: A quitter is someone who gives up easily and does not finish something they have started.

words.tr: v. 重新排列；重新安排
words.ex: He rearranged the books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他把书架上的书重新排列了。
words.en: If you rearrange the objects in a place, you change the way in which they are organized or positioned.

words.tr:
v. 补偿；赔偿；报酬
n. 报偿；回礼；赔偿
words.ex: The company recompense the worker for the lost time.
words.ex_cn: 公司补偿了工人损失的时间。
words.en: If you are given something, usually money, in recompense, you are given it as a reward or because you have suffered.

words.ex: The company announced redundancy due to low profits.
words.ex_cn: 公司因利润低下宣布裁员。
words.en: Redundancy refers to the state of being not or no longer needed or useful; the inclusion of extra components which are not strictly necessary to functioning, in case of failure in other components; or the dismissal of employees from work for being no longer necessary.

words.ex: He received fair remuneration for his work.
words.ex_cn: 他因工作获得了公平的报酬。
words.en: Remuneration refers to the money that is paid to someone for the work that they have done.

words.ex: The teacher checked the rota to see who is on duty today.
words.ex_cn: 老师检查了花名册，看看今天谁值日。
words.en: A rota is a list that shows who is supposed to do a particular job or duty on a particular day.

words.ex: He has a sartorial style that impresses everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种令人印象深刻的服装风格。
words.en: Sartorial relates to tailoring, clothes, or style of dress.

words.ex: The secession of the southern states led to the Civil War.
words.ex_cn: 南方各州的脱离导致了内战。
words.en: The action of withdrawing formally from membership of a federation or body, especially a political state.

words.ex: His main shortcoming is being late often.
words.ex_cn: 他的主要缺点是经常迟到。
words.en: A shortcoming is a fault or a failure to meet a certain standard, which means a person or thing is not as good as they should be.

words.ex: He signed his name with a clear signature.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的签名签了名字。
words.en: A signature is a person's name written in a distinctive way as a form of identification in authorizing a document or letter.

words.ex: He used his signet to seal the document.
words.ex_cn: 他用他的印章密封了文件。
words.en: A signet is a small seal, especially one set in a ring, used historically to authenticate documents by pressing it into wax or another soft material.

words.tr: n. 纺纱机；纺纱工；转盘
words.ex: The spinner turned wool into thread.
words.ex_cn: 这台纺纱机将羊毛纺成线。
words.en: A spinner is a person or machine that spins wool, cotton, or other material into thread or yarn.

words.tr:
n. 赞助商；
v. 赞助；
words.ex: The company is a sponsor of the football match.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是这场足球赛的赞助商。
words.en: A sponsor is a person or organization that pays for or contributes to the costs involved in staging a sporting or artistic event in return for advertising. A sponsor can also be someone who introduces and supports a proposal for a new law.

words.ex: The class analyzed statistical data from the survey.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级分析了调查的统计数据。
words.en: Relating to the use of statistics or statistical methods.

words.ex: The statistics show a rise in sales last year.
words.ex_cn: 这些统计数字显示去年销售额有所上升。
words.en: Statistics is a branch of mathematics dealing with the collection, analysis, interpretation, presentation, and organization of data.

words.ex: He receives a small stipend for his internship.
words.ex_cn: 他因实习获得少量薪金。
words.en: A stipend is a sum of money paid regularly as a salary or allowance.

words.ex: The strike caused a stoppage of the train service.
words.ex_cn: 罢工导致了列车服务的停止。
words.en: A stoppage is an instance of stopping or the state of being stopped, especially in a work context.

words.ex: The government gives a subsidy to farmers.
words.ex_cn: 政府向农民提供补贴。
words.en: A subsidy is money that is paid by a government or other authority in order to help an industry or business, or to pay for a public service.

words.tr: v. 监督；管理；主管；指挥
words.ex: He superintends the construction site every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天监督建筑工地。
words.en: To be in charge of something and make sure that it is working as it should.

words.ex: The superintendent of the school is very strict.
words.ex_cn: 学校的主管非常严格。
words.en: A superintendent is a person who is in charge of a particular department or activity, especially within a school, housing project, or police force.

words.ex: The new law will supersede the old one.
words.ex_cn: 新法律将取代旧法律。
words.en: If something is superseded by something newer, it is replaced because it has become old-fashioned or unacceptable.

words.ex: He follows a systematic approach to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种系统的方法来解决数学问题。
words.en: A systematic approach or method is one that is done according to a fixed plan, in a thorough and efficient way.

words.tr: v. 使系统化；使成体系；使条理化
words.ex: He tries to systematize his notes before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前试图系统化他的笔记。
words.en: To systematize means to arrange according to an organized system; make systematic.

words.ex: He works as a tanner in a small town.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个小镇上做皮革工。
words.en: A tanner is a person whose job is to tan animal hides to make leather.

words.ex: The tattooist drew a dragon on his arm.
words.ex_cn: 纹身师在他手臂上画了一条龙。
words.en: A tattooist is a person who tattoos, that is, makes permanent designs on the skin with ink.

words.ex: The teacher has a long tenure at the school.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师在学校有很长的任期。
words.en: The period during which an office is held; the status of holding one's position on a permanent basis.

words.tr: v. 使掉换顺序；使转移；使换位
words.ex: You need to transpose the elements to solve the equation.
words.ex_cn: 你需要调换元素来解这个方程。
words.en: To transpose something means to change its order, position, or nature, especially in mathematics or music.

words.tr: n. 调换；变换；转位；转座
words.ex: The error was caused by a simple transposition of digits.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误是由于简单的数字调换造成的。
words.en: The act of changing the order or position of something.

words.ex: He will try out for the soccer team tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天将参加足球队的选拔。
words.en: A tryout is an opportunity to show that you are suitable for a particular job or activity, especially in sports or acting.

words.ex: The turner fixed the metal part on the lathe.
words.ex_cn: 车床工人把金属零件固定在车床上。
words.en: A turner is someone who operates a lathe or is skilled in turning wood or metal on a lathe.

words.ex: The manager yelled at his underling for making a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 经理因为下属犯了错误而对他大喊大叫。
words.en: An underling is a person who is lower in rank or position than someone else, especially in a work environment.

words.tr: adj. 实用的；功利主义的；
words.ex: The chair is utilitarian and comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子实用又舒适。
words.en: Utilitarian means relating to or adhering to the belief that the value of a thing or an action is determined by its utility.

words.ex: Please vacate the room by noon.
words.ex_cn: 请在中午前腾出房间。
words.en: To vacate a place or position means to leave it or give it up, making it available for other people.

words.ex: They vie for the top prize.
words.ex_cn: 他们争夺最高奖项。
words.en: To compete eagerly with someone in order to do or achieve something.

chapters.name: 多彩生活 人脉沟通 重点词

words.ex: His rude behavior alienated his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的行为使朋友们疏远了他。
words.en: To cause someone to feel isolated or estranged; to transfer the ownership of property to another.

words.tr:
v. 把…联系在一起；
adj. 副的；
n. 同事；伙伴；
words.ex: He associates happiness with family time.
words.ex_cn: 他把幸福与家庭时光联系在一起。
words.en: If you associate someone or something with a particular quality or idea, or if they are associated with it, you connect them in your mind with that quality or idea.

words.ex: He turned his head to avert the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他转过头去避免了事故。
words.en: If you avert something unpleasant, you prevent it from happening.

words.ex: He avoids eating sugar to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他避免吃糖以保持健康。
words.en: If you avoid something, you take action in order to prevent it from happening to you.

words.ex: He is aware of the danger.
words.ex_cn: 他意识到危险。
words.en: If you are aware of something, you know about it.

words.tr: v. 招手示意；举手召唤；引诱
words.ex: He beckoned to the boy to come closer.
words.ex_cn: 他向那个男孩招手示意过来。
words.en: If you beckon to someone, you signal to them to come to you, usually by a gesture of your hand.

words.tr: v. 诱骗；消遣；迷住；消磨
words.ex: He beguiles her with sweet words.
words.ex_cn: 他用甜言蜜语哄骗她。
words.en: If someone beguiles you, they charm you in a way that makes you trust them or like them, often so that they can deceive you.

words.ex: His smile belieed his true feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑掩饰了他真实的情感。
words.en: If one thing belies another, it hides the true situation and so creates a false idea or image of someone or something.

words.ex: Beware of the dog.
words.ex_cn: 当心那只狗。
words.en: to be cautious and alert to the dangers of.

words.tr: adj. 随意的；非正式的；偶然的；
words.ex: He wore casual clothes to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了随意的衣服去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude or behavior as casual, you mean they are not very concerned about what they are doing or what is happening around them, or they are not taking it seriously.

words.tr:
n. 小心；警告；注意；
v. 警告；劝...小心；
words.ex: He drove with caution on the icy road.
words.ex_cn: 他在结冰的道路上小心驾驶。
words.en: Caution is care that you take in order to avoid possible danger or trouble.

words.tr: v. 绕行；设法避开；智胜；围住
words.ex: He circumvented the traffic by taking a small road.
words.ex_cn: 他通过走一条小路绕过了交通拥堵。
words.en: If someone circumvents a rule or restriction, they avoid having to obey it, usually in a clever and dishonest way.

words.tr:
n. 钩；扣；紧握；紧抱
v. 抱紧；握紧；扣紧
words.ex: The necklace has a gold clasp.
words.ex_cn: 这条项链有一个金色的钩。
words.en: A clasp is a small device that fastens something, or the act of holding someone or something tightly.

words.ex: The child clings to his mother's leg.
words.ex_cn: 孩子紧贴着妈妈的腿。
words.en: If you cling to someone or something, you hold onto them tightly.

words.ex: They tried to coerce him into signing the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图强迫他签署那份文件。
words.en: If you coerce someone into doing something, you make them do it, even though they do not want to.

words.ex: It's a coincidence that we both wore blue today.
words.ex_cn: 我们今天都穿了蓝色，真是巧合。
words.en: A coincidence is when two or more similar or related events occur at the same time by chance and without any planning.

words.ex: They collaborate to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他们合作完成这个项目。
words.en: to work jointly with others or together especially in an intellectual endeavor

words.tr: n. 交流；共享；圣餐仪式
words.ex: The two friends had a deep communion after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 两位朋友在晚餐后进行了深入的交流。
words.en: Communion is a feeling of fellowship with others, as a result of sharing common attitudes, interests, or goals.

words.tr: adj. 兼容的；可和谐共存的；
words.ex: This printer is compatible with my computer.
words.ex_cn: 这个打印机与我的电脑兼容。
words.en: If things, for example, systems, ideas, and beliefs, are compatible, they work well together or can exist together successfully.

words.ex: The two countries reached a concord on trade.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家在贸易上达成了一致。
words.en: Concord is a state of agreement or harmony between people or groups.

words.ex: The weather was congenial for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常适合野餐。
words.en: A congenial person, place, or environment is pleasant because it suits your character or nature.

words.ex: He is a conscientious student who always finishes his homework on time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个尽责的学生，总是按时完成作业。
words.en: Someone who is conscientious is very careful to do their work properly.

words.ex: The team reached a consensus on the project plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队就项目计划达成了共识。
words.en: A consensus is general agreement among a group of people.

words.tr:
n. 接触；联系；
v. 接触；联系；
words.ex: The two balls made contact when they collided.
words.ex_cn: 两个球在碰撞时发生了接触。
words.en: Contact refers to the act of communicating with someone, especially regularly, or the state of touching something.

words.tr: v. 考虑；深思；凝视；思考…的可能性
words.ex: He contemplates quitting his job.
words.ex_cn: 他正在考虑辞去工作。
words.en: If you contemplate an action, you think about whether to do it or not.

words.tr: v. 贡献；促成；捐献；投稿；
words.ex: He contributes money to the charity.
words.ex_cn: 他向慈善机构捐款。
words.en: If you contribute to something, you help to cause it or make it happen.

words.ex: The data points correlate with each other.
words.ex_cn: 这些数据点相互关联。
words.en: If one thing correlates with another, there is a close similarity or connection between them, often because one thing causes the other.

words.ex: The number of apples corresponds to the number of oranges.
words.ex_cn: 苹果的数量与橙子的数量相对应。
words.en: If one thing corresponds to another, there is a close similarity or connection between them, often because one is the cause or the result of the other.

words.ex: They maintain correspondence through letters.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过信件保持通信联系。
words.en: Communication by exchanging letters with someone; a close similarity, connection, or equivalence.

words.tr:
adj. 秘密的；隐蔽的
n. （动物可藏身的）小树丛
words.ex: He made a covert plan to leave without telling anyone.
words.ex_cn: 他秘密制定了一个不告诉任何人就离开的计划。
words.en: Covert activities or situations are secret or hidden.

words.ex: She cuddles her baby every night.
words.ex_cn: 她每天晚上都拥抱她的宝宝。
words.en: To hold someone or something close in your arms as a way of showing love or affection.

words.ex: Many people decry the use of plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 许多人公开反对使用塑料袋。
words.en: If you decry something, you criticize it as being wrong or harmful.

words.ex: The soil degrades over time without proper care.
words.ex_cn: 如果没有适当照料，土壤会逐渐退化。
words.en: If something degrades or is degraded, it becomes worse in quality, or weaker in power or status.

words.ex: The delivery of the package took three days.
words.ex_cn: 这个包裹的交付花了三天时间。
words.en: The act of delivering letters, parcels, or goods.

words.ex: He tries not to demean his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他尽量不贬低他的同学。
words.en: To demean someone or something means to cause them to lose their dignity or respect.

words.tr:
adj. 依靠的；依赖的；
n. 受赡养者；
words.ex: The child is dependent on his parents for food.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子依靠父母提供食物。
words.en: A dependent person or thing is one that needs the support of another person or thing in order to exist or be successful.

words.tr: v. 使有尊严；使崇高；使显贵
words.ex: He tried to dignify his actions with excuses.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用借口来美化自己的行为。
words.en: To dignify something means to make it seem important and worthy of respect, often by treating it in a serious or formal way.

words.ex: He kept his dignity even when he was poor.
words.ex_cn: 即使他很穷，他依然保持尊严。
words.en: Dignity is the quality of being worthy of honor or respect.

words.tr:
n. 不信任；名誉丧失；信誉丧失
v. 不信；败坏名声；使丢脸
words.ex: His lies brought discredit to the company.
words.ex_cn: 他的谎言使公司失去了信任。
words.en: To discredit someone or something means to cause them to lose people's respect or trust.

words.ex: He donate money to the poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他向贫困儿童捐赠钱。
words.en: To donate means to give something, especially money, to a person or organization that needs help.

words.ex: She dotes on her little grandson.
words.ex_cn: 她非常疼爱她的孙子。
words.en: If you say that someone dotes on a person or a thing, you mean that they love or care about them very much and spend a lot of time with them.

words.tr:
n. 被愚弄的人；容易受骗的人
v. 欺骗；诈骗；愚弄
words.ex: He was duped into buying a fake watch.
words.ex_cn: 他被骗去买了一块假手表。
words.en: A dupe is someone who is easily deceived or cheated, often because they are too trusting. As a verb, to dupe means to deceive or trick someone into believing something that is not true.

words.ex: The tricky question eluded even the best students.
words.ex_cn: 这道难题难倒了即使是最优秀的学生。
words.en: If something that you want eludes you, you fail to obtain it. If you elude someone or something, you avoid them or escape from them.

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；不易被抓获（觉察、理解或记忆）的；
words.ex: The truth remained elusive.
words.ex_cn: 真相难以捉摸。
words.en: Difficult to find, catch, or achieve; difficult to remember or understand.

words.ex: He finally embraced the new idea.
words.ex_cn: 他最终接受了这个新想法。
words.en: To take someone into your arms as a sign of love or affection, or to accept something enthusiastically.

words.ex: They established a new school in the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们在村里建立了一所新学校。
words.en: To set up or create something, such as an organization or a system, on a firm or permanent basis.

words.ex: He estranged his brother with harsh words.
words.ex_cn: 他用刻薄的话与兄弟疏远了。
words.en: If you estrange someone, especially a member of your family, you cause them to stop being friendly or close to you.

words.ex: He exaggerates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸张自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you exaggerate, you indicate that something is, for example, worse or more important than it really is.

words.tr:
v. 奉承；讨好
adj. 更平坦的；更扁平的；“flat”的比较级
adv. 更平直地；更直截了当地；“flat”的比较级
words.ex: He flatters his boss to get a raise.
words.ex_cn: 他奉承老板以获得加薪。
words.en: If someone flatters you, they praise you in an exaggerated way that may be sincere or may be intended to persuade you to do something.

words.tr: adj. 强制的；强迫的；强有力的
words.ex: The police used forcible entry to get inside.
words.ex_cn: 警察强行进入里面。
words.en: Forcible is used to describe something that is done using physical force or violence, or something that is done in a strong and effective way.

words.tr:
v. 急促而含混不清地说
n. 急促不清的话
words.ex: The children gabble when they are excited.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们兴奋时会叽叽喳喳地说个不停。
words.en: If you gabble, you say things so quickly that it is difficult for people to understand you.

words.ex: He gave a generous donation to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他慷慨地捐钱给穷人。
words.en: A generous person gives more of something, especially money, than is usual or expected.

words.ex: I am grateful for your help.
words.ex_cn: 我感激你的帮助。
words.en: If you are grateful for something that someone has given you or done for you, you have warm, friendly feelings towards them and wish to thank them.

words.ex: He hesitates to ask for help.
words.ex_cn: 他犹豫着是否要寻求帮助。
words.en: If you hesitate, you pause slightly while you are doing something or just before you do it, usually because you are uncertain, embarrassed, or worried.

words.ex: He hobnobs with famous actors at parties.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上与著名演员亲近交往。
words.en: To associate familiarly or socially; to drink together.

words.ex: He tried to hoodwink her with a fake story.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一个虚假的故事欺骗她。
words.en: To deceive or trick someone.

words.ex: The host showed great hospitality to the guests.
words.ex_cn: 主人对客人表现出极大的款待。
words.en: Hospitality is friendly and generous behaviour towards guests, especially by giving them food, drink, or a place to stay.

words.tr: adj. 卑微的；谦逊的；虚心的；
words.ex: He lived in a humble house near the river.
words.ex_cn: 他住在河边一座简陋的房子里。
words.en: If you describe someone as humble, you mean that they do not think they are better or more important than other people.

words.ex: The child imitates her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If you imitate someone, you copy what they do or produce.

words.tr: adj. 不连贯的；语无伦次的
words.ex: He was tired and gave an incoherent answer.
words.ex_cn: 他很累，给出了一个混乱的回答。
words.en: If someone is incoherent, they are talking in a confused and unclear way.

words.tr: adj. 不兼容的；不相配的；
words.ex: The software is incompatible with old systems.
words.ex_cn: 这个软件与旧系统不兼容。
words.en: If one thing or person is incompatible with another, they are very different in important ways, and do not suit each other or agree with each other.

words.ex: He tries to ingratiate himself with his boss by bringing coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上送咖啡给老板，试图讨好他。
words.en: If someone tries to ingratiate themselves with you, they do things to try and make you like them.

words.ex: He insinuated that she was lying.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示她在撒谎。
words.en: If you say that someone insinuates that something bad is the case, you mean that they say it in an indirect way.

words.tr:
v. 侮辱；辱骂
n. 侮辱；辱骂
words.ex: He insulted her with rude words.
words.ex_cn: 他用粗鲁的话侮辱了她。
words.en: To insult someone means to say or do something that is rude or offensive.

words.tr:
n. 意图；目的；
adj. 专注的；
words.ex: His intent was to help, not to hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他的意图是帮助，而不是伤害。
words.en: If you are intent on doing something, you are determined to get it done. If you have an intent to do something, you have a plan or purpose in mind.

words.tr: v. 互相作用；互相影响；交流；沟通；
words.ex: The two chemicals interact when mixed.
words.ex_cn: 这两种化学物质混合时会互相作用。
words.en: If people interact with each other, they communicate or work together.

words.ex: The two cultures have a lot of interchange.
words.ex_cn: 这两种文化有很多交流。
words.en: The act or process of exchanging things with each other, especially ideas or information.

words.tr: adj. 互相依赖的；相倚的；
words.ex: The two countries are interdependent in trade.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家在贸易上互相依赖。
words.en: If two or more things are interdependent, they depend on each other.

words.ex: He interjected during the meeting to ask a question.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议中插话问了一个问题。
words.en: To say something that interrupts someone who is speaking.

words.ex: The interplay between light and shadow creates beauty.
words.ex_cn: 光与影的相互作用创造了美。
words.en: The way in which two or more things have an effect on each other.

words.tr: v. 置于…之间；插入；插嘴；介入
words.ex: The mediator tried to interpose before the situation escalated.
words.ex_cn: 调解人试图在局势升级之前进行干预。
words.en: If you interpose something between two people or things, you place it between them. If you interpose, you interrupt with a comment or question.

words.ex: They share intimacy through quiet talks at night.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过夜晚的安静交谈建立亲密感。
words.en: A close, familiar, and usually affectionate or loving personal relationship with another person or group.

words.ex: They have an intimate friendship.
words.ex_cn: 他们有着亲密的友谊。
words.en: having a close, friendly, or personal relationship with someone; private and personal

words.ex: The lock has an intricate design.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁有复杂的结构。
words.en: You use intricate to describe something that has many small parts or details.

words.ex: He iterate the importance of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他反复说诚实的重要性。
words.en: To say or do something again or several times.

words.tr:
n. 说笑；玩笑
v. 开玩笑
words.ex: He likes to jest with his friends during lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在午餐时和朋友开玩笑。
words.en: A jest is a remark that is intended to be amusing or funny, especially one that is made in a light-hearted or teasing manner.

words.ex: They felt a strong kinship because they grew up in the same village.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为从小在同一个村庄长大，感到有很强的亲属关系。
words.en: Kinship is the relationship between members of the same family.

words.tr:
v. 意思是说；表示…的意思；
n. 手段；方法；收入；
words.ex: This sign means you cannot park here.
words.ex_cn: 这个标志意思是说这里不能停车。
words.en: Means refers to a method or way of doing something, or the resources or assets available for a particular purpose.

words.ex: Good teachers motivate students to learn.
words.ex_cn: 好老师激励学生学习。
words.en: To motivate someone means to provide them with a reason for doing something, especially something that requires effort.

words.tr:
v. 咕哝；含糊地说
n. 含糊的话；咕哝
words.ex: He mumbles when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，他会嘟囔。
words.en: If you mumble, you speak very quietly and not at all clearly with the result that the words are difficult to understand.

words.tr:
v. 唠叨；喋喋不休；不断困扰
n. 老马；驽马；矮小马
words.ex: She nagged him to clean his room.
words.ex_cn: 她不停地催他打扫房间。
words.en: If someone nags you, they keep asking you to do something you have not done yet or do not want to do.

words.ex: The law obliges drivers to wear seat belts.
words.ex_cn: 法律迫使司机系安全带。
words.en: If you are obliged to do something, you have to do it because the situation, the law, a duty, etc., makes it necessary.

words.ex: The artist lived in obscurity for most of his life.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家一生大部分时间都默默无闻。
words.en: The state of being unknown, inconspicuous, or unimportant.

words.ex: He overstates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸大自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you say that someone is overstating something, you mean they are describing it in a way that makes it seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.tr:
v. 挡开；避开；回避
n. 挡开；闪避
words.ex: He parries the punch with his arm.
words.ex_cn: 他用胳膊格挡了这一拳。
words.en: If you parry a question or argument, you cleverly avoid answering it or dealing with it. In fencing, if you parry a blow, you defend yourself against it by pushing it away with your weapon.

words.tr:
n. 同辈；同等的人；
v. 凝视；
words.ex: He feels comfortable talking to his peers.
words.ex_cn: 他觉得和同辈交谈很自在。
words.en: A peer is someone who is equal to another in abilities, qualifications, age, background, or social status. As a verb, to peer means to look keenly or with difficulty at someone or something.

words.ex: I perceive a change in his mood.
words.ex_cn: 我察觉到他的情绪有变化。
words.en: If you perceive something, you see, notice, or realize it, especially when it is not obvious.

words.tr: adj. 可察觉到的；看得出的；可感知的
words.ex: The change was barely perceptible.
words.ex_cn: 这个变化几乎无法察觉。
words.en: Something that is perceptible can be seen, noticed, or felt.

words.ex: His perception of the sound was very sharp.
words.ex_cn: 他对声音的感知非常敏锐。
words.en: Your perception of something is the way that you think about it or the impression you have of it.

words.tr: adj. 观察敏锐的；有洞察力的
words.ex: She is perceptive and notices small changes.
words.ex_cn: 她很有洞察力，能注意到细微的变化。
words.en: If you describe someone as perceptive, you mean that they are good at noticing or understanding things.

words.ex: This rule pertains to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If one thing pertains to another, it relates, belongs, or applies to it.

words.tr: v. 有关；把…联系起来；认同；叙述；理解；
words.ex: This story relates to your childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事与你的童年有关。
words.en: If you relate a story, you tell it. If two things relate, they are connected in some way.

words.ex: Children rely on their parents for food and shelter.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们依靠父母提供食物和住所。
words.en: If you rely on someone or something, you need them and depend on them in order to live or work properly.

words.ex: He responded to the question quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快回答了问题。
words.en: If you respond to something that is done or said, you react to it by doing or saying something yourself.

words.ex: He likes to seclude himself in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢把自己 secluded 在森林里。
words.en: To seclude means to keep someone away from other people, or to keep something away from other things.

words.ex: Her hug gave me solace after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 在失去亲人后，她的拥抱给了我安慰。
words.en: Solace is comfort that you feel when you are consoled in times of disappointment or sadness.

words.ex: His status in the company is very high.
words.ex_cn: 他在公司里的地位很高。
words.en: The status of someone or something is their position or situation according to the law or according to other people's opinions.

words.ex: He had a stumble on the rocky path.
words.ex_cn: 他在布满石头的小路上绊了一跤。
words.en: To stumble means to trip or momentarily lose one's balance while walking or running. It can also refer to speaking in a hesitant or faltering manner.

words.tr: adj. 怀疑的；令人怀疑的；
words.ex: The police felt suspicious about the man's behavior.
words.ex_cn: 警察对这个人的行为感到怀疑。
words.en: If you are suspicious of someone or something, you do not trust them, and are careful when dealing with them.

words.ex: He taunted his brother for losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他奚落弟弟比赛输了。
words.en: If someone taunts you, they say unkind or insulting things to you, especially about your weaknesses or failures.

words.tr: v. 轻描淡写；打折扣地说；少说
words.ex: He understated the cost of the repair.
words.ex_cn: 他轻描淡写了维修的费用。
words.en: If you understate something, you describe it in a way that suggests it is less important or serious than it really is.

chapters.name: 多彩生活 人脉沟通 认知词

words.tr: n. 喜爱；类同；密切关系；亲和力
words.ex: She has an affinity for painting.
words.ex_cn: 她喜爱绘画。
words.en: A natural liking for or attraction to someone or something.

words.ex: The weather was agreeable for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 天气令人愉悦，适合散步。
words.en: Pleasant and easy to like; willing to agree to something

words.tr: n. 依恋；附件；附加装置；
words.ex: The child showed strong attachment to his teddy bear.
words.ex_cn: 孩子对他的泰迪熊产生了强烈的依恋。
words.en: An attachment is a file that is sent along with an email message.

words.tr:
n. 背后中伤；背后诽谤
v. 背后诽谤；背后中伤；“backbite”的现在分词
words.ex: He hates backbiting in the office.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌在办公室里搬弄是非。
words.en: Backbiting is the act of saying unpleasant or unkind things about someone who is not present, especially in order to damage their reputation.

words.ex: He used a beeper to stay in touch with his team.
words.ex_cn: 他使用传呼机与团队保持联系。
words.en: A beeper is a small device you carry that makes a noise to tell you when someone is trying to contact you.

words.tr:
v. 斗嘴；闪烁
n. 口角
words.ex: They bicker over small things every day.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天为小事争吵。
words.en: If people bicker, they argue or quarrel about unimportant things.

words.ex: I went to the park with my buddy.
words.ex_cn: 我和我的同伴去了公园。
words.en: A buddy is a close friend.

words.ex: Tom and Sam are chums who play football every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 汤姆和萨姆是每周末一起踢足球的密友。
words.en: A close friend.

words.tr: n. 解说词；评论；实况报道；
words.ex: The commentator gave live commentary during the soccer match.
words.ex_cn: 解说员在足球比赛期间进行了现场解说。
words.en: A commentary is a spoken or written description of an event or situation that is broadcast or published as it occurs.

words.ex: His dog gave him constant companionship.
words.ex_cn: 他的狗给了他不断的陪伴。
words.en: the state of being with someone or having someone to spend time with

words.ex: The hotel gave us complimentary breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 酒店免费赠送了我们早餐。
words.en: If something is complimentary, it is given or done free of charge. It can also mean expressing a compliment; praising or approving.

words.ex: He is my confidant and I tell him everything.
words.ex_cn: 他是我的知己，我什么都告诉他。
words.en: A confidant is someone you can share your secrets with or discuss personal matters with, knowing that they will keep your information private.

words.tr:
n. 粪便；废话；质量差的东西
v. 排便
words.ex: The dog left crap on the grass.
words.ex_cn: 狗在草地上拉了粪便。
words.en: If you describe something as crap, you think that it is of very poor quality.

words.tr: v. 公开指责；告发；揭发
words.ex: He denounces corruption in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中谴责腐败。
words.en: If you denounce a person or an action, you criticize them severely and publicly because you feel strongly that they are wrong or evil.

words.ex: The crowd laughed in derision when he fell down.
words.ex_cn: 当他摔倒时，人群发出嘲笑的笑声。
words.en: If you treat someone or something with derision, you express contempt for them; ridicule.

words.ex: His derogatory remarks hurt her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他毁谤的言辞伤害了她的感情。
words.en: If you make a derogatory remark or comment about someone or something, you say something that shows you have a low opinion of them.

words.ex: The divisive comment caused a fight among friends.
words.ex_cn: 这个制造分裂的言论引发了朋友们之间的争吵。
words.en: Causing or likely to cause disagreement or division between people.

words.tr:
v. 慢吞吞地说；拉长语调说话
n. 慢吞吞拉长调子的说话方式
words.ex: He speaks with a slow drawl.
words.ex_cn: 他说话慢吞吞的。
words.en: To speak slowly with vowels greatly prolonged.

words.tr: v. 起绰号；把…称作；配音；译制
words.ex: They dubbed him 'Captain Cool' for his calm style.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他冷静的风格给他起了个绰号叫‘冷静队长’。
words.en: To give a name, title, or nickname to someone or something; to provide a film or television program with a soundtrack in a different language from the original.

words.tr:
n. 回声；
v. 回响；
words.ex: The echo came back from the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 回声从山上反弹回来。
words.en: An echo is a sound which is caused by a noise being reflected off a surface such as a wall.

words.tr: v. 射精；射出；突然说出
words.ex: He cannot ejaculate due to medicine.
words.ex_cn: 由于药物，他无法射精。
words.en: To ejaculate means to say something suddenly and briefly, or to emit semen from the penis during orgasm.

words.ex: The teacher asked a simple question to elicit answers from students.
words.ex_cn: 老师问了一个简单的问题来引出学生的回答。
words.en: To elicit a response or a reaction means to cause it to happen by something that you say or do.

words.ex: The police opened an enquiry into the accident.
words.ex_cn: 警方对这起事故展开了调查。
words.en: An enquiry is a question you ask in order to get some information.

words.ex: He told a falsehood to avoid punishment.
words.ex_cn: 他说了一个谎言来避免惩罚。
words.en: A falsehood is a statement that is not true; a lie.

words.ex: He studied familial patterns in his research.
words.ex_cn: 他在研究中分析了家族模式。
words.en: Relating to or occurring in a family or its members.

words.ex: He joined a fraternity at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学加入了兄弟会。
words.en: Fraternity refers to a group of people sharing a common profession or interests, or a feeling of friendship and mutual support within a group.

words.tr: n. 收集；采集；聚会；聚集； v. 聚集；集合；“gather”的现在分词；
words.ex: The gathering of old books took him years.
words.ex_cn: 收集旧书花了他多年时间。
words.en: A gathering is a group of people meeting together for a particular purpose.

words.tr: v. 叽哩咕噜地叫；急促不清地说
words.ex: He gibbers when he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 当他紧张时，他会胡言乱语。
words.en: To speak rapidly and unintelligibly, often in a state of panic or excitement.

words.ex: He was a habitué of the local café, often seen there at the same time every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是当地咖啡馆的常客，经常在每天的同一时间出现在那里。
words.en: A person who frequents a particular place, especially a place of entertainment.

words.ex: The priest gave a short homily after the prayer.
words.ex_cn: 祷告后，牧师做了一个简短的讲道。
words.en: A homily is a religious discourse which is intended to edify a congregation, typically given by a priest or minister during a service.

words.ex: The police used fingerprint identification to find the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 警察使用指纹识别来找到嫌疑人。
words.en: Identification is the act of recognizing and naming someone or something, or the process of proving who or what someone or something is.

words.tr: n. 相互作用；相互影响；互动交流；
words.ex: The interaction between the two chemicals causes a reaction.
words.ex_cn: 这两种化学物质之间的相互作用引起反应。
words.en: An interaction is a situation where two or more people or things communicate with or react to each other.

words.ex: The app has an interactive game for kids.
words.ex_cn: 这个应用有一个适合孩子的交互式游戏。
words.en: An interactive computer program or system is designed to involve the user in the exchange of information.

words.ex: There is little intercourse between the two villages.
words.ex_cn: 这两个村庄之间很少交往。
words.en: Intercourse refers to communication or dealings between individuals or groups, or sexual activity between people.

words.ex: The interlocutor asked a series of probing questions.
words.ex_cn: 对话者提出了一系列尖锐的问题。
words.en: An interlocutor is someone who takes part in a conversation or dialogue, often in a formal or official capacity.

words.ex: He acted as an intermediary between the two sides.
words.ex_cn: 他充当了双方之间的中间人。
