words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中的表现非常出色。
words.en: The act of performing a play, concert, or some other form of entertainment.

words.ex: She bought a new perfume for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一瓶新香水。
words.en: A perfume is a pleasant-smelling liquid which people put on their skin to make themselves smell nice.

words.tr:
n. 泡菜；腌菜；腌汁；腌制品；困境
v. 腌制（泡菜等）
words.ex: He put a pickle on his sandwich.
words.ex_cn: 他在三明治上放了一颗酸黄瓜。
words.en: A pickle is a vegetable or fruit that has been preserved in vinegar or salt water, or a difficult situation.

words.ex: We had a potluck dinner with neighbors last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 上周末我们和邻居们吃了一顿家常便饭。
words.en: A potluck is a meal or party to which each of the guests contributes a dish.

words.ex: He wears a warm pullover in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天穿一件厚毛衣。
words.en: A pullover is a piece of clothing that is made of wool or cotton and is worn on the upper part of the body. It is put on by pulling it over the head.

words.ex: The school will equip the lab with new computers.
words.ex_cn: 学校将为实验室配备新电脑。
words.en: To provide someone or something with the necessary items for a particular purpose.

words.ex: We had a snack and some drinks as refreshment after the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 会议结束后，我们吃了点心和喝了一些饮料作为茶点。
words.en: Refreshment refers to the act of refreshing or the state of being refreshed, especially by food or drink. It can also mean a light meal or drinks served in a social setting.

words.ex: He listens to music to relax.
words.ex_cn: 他听音乐来放松。
words.en: If you relax or if something relaxes you, you feel more calm and less worried or tense.

words.tr:
v. 喜欢；享受；从…获得乐趣
n. 享受；乐趣；调味品
words.ex: He relishes every bite of his favorite food.
words.ex_cn: 他享受着每一口他最喜欢的食物。
words.en: If you relish something, you enjoy it very much.

words.tr: n. 会合地点；约会；集会
words.ex: They will rendezvous at the park at 6 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 他们将在晚上6点在公园会合。
words.en: A rendezvous is a meeting that has been arranged between people, often secretly.

words.tr:
v. 狂欢作乐；陶醉；酷爱
n. 作乐；狂欢
words.ex: They reveled in the success of their new product.
words.ex_cn: 他们为新产品的成功而狂欢。
words.en: If you revel in something, you enjoy it very much.

words.ex: His ribald jokes were inappropriate for a family gathering.
words.ex_cn: 他的下流笑话不适合家庭聚会。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as ribald, you mean that it refers to sex in a rude or humorous way.

words.tr:
n. 烤肉；烘烤；
adj. 烤的；焙的；
v. 烤；烘烤；
words.ex: We had roast for dinner last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚我们吃了烤肉。
words.en: To cook food, such as meat, in an oven or over a fire.

words.ex: He lost all his money on roulette.
words.ex_cn: 他在轮盘赌上输掉了所有的钱。
words.en: A gambling game in which a ball is dropped onto a revolving wheel with numbered compartments, the players betting on the number at which the ball will come to rest.

words.ex: They played a game of rounders in the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们在公园里玩了一场类似棒球的游戏。
words.en: Rounders is a bat-and-ball game played between two teams, which is popular in the UK and is similar to baseball.

words.tr:
n. 朗姆酒
adj. 古怪的；奇特的
words.ex: He drank a glass of rum by the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在火炉旁喝了一杯朗姆酒。
words.en: Rum is an alcoholic drink made from sugar cane.

words.tr:
v. 品味；细品；享用；体会
n. 风味；滋味
words.ex: He savord the taste of the chocolate slowly.
words.ex_cn: 他慢慢地品味着巧克力的味道。
words.en: To enjoy or appreciate (something) completely.

words.tr:
v. 品味；细品；享用；体会
n. 风味；滋味
words.ex: He savours every bite of the meal.
words.ex_cn: 他细细品味每一口饭菜。
words.en: To savour something means to enjoy it as much as you can. If you savour an experience or a feeling, you enjoy it as much as you can, for example by noticing all its details.

words.ex: He hurt his shin while kicking the ball.
words.ex_cn: 他踢球时伤到了胫部。
words.en: The front part of the leg below the knee.

words.tr: v. （给顾客）少找钱；不公平对待
words.ex: The shopkeeper short-changed me by five dollars.
words.ex_cn: 店主给我少找了五美元。
words.en: To give someone less change than they are owed, especially deliberately.

words.tr:
n. 一小口；
v. 呷；啜；小口喝；
words.ex: He took a sip of water.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了一小口水。
words.en: To drink something slowly by taking small amounts into your mouth.

words.tr:
n. 虹吸管
v. 用虹吸管吸；抽取；挪用
words.ex: He used a siphon to transfer gasoline from one tank to another.
words.ex_cn: 他用虹吸管将汽油从一个油箱输送到另一个油箱。
words.en: A siphon is a tube that is used to move liquids from one container to another at a lower level by atmospheric pressure and gravity.

words.tr: n. 牛里脊肉；牛上腰肉
words.ex: He grilled a sirloin steak for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他为晚餐烤了一块西冷牛排。
words.en: A cut of beef from the lower part of the back, just in front of the rump.

words.tr: n. 潜游运动；赤身潜水
words.ex: He loves skin-diving in the sea on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在周末去海里裸潜。
words.en: The activity of swimming underwater without the use of scuba gear, often using only a mask, snorkel, and fins.

words.ex: The lemon tastes sour.
words.ex_cn: 这个柠檬尝起来是酸的。
words.en: Having a sharp, acidic taste; not sweet.

words.ex: She added cinnamon spice to the cake.
words.ex_cn: 她往蛋糕里加了肉桂香料。
words.en: Spice refers to a substance used to flavor food, which is usually made from parts of plants, especially their seeds, fruits, or roots. It can also mean something that adds interest or excitement.

words.ex: The soup is too spicy for me.
words.ex_cn: 这汤对我来说太辣了。
words.en: Food that is spicy has a strong, hot flavor.

words.tr:
n. 聚光灯；
v. 使公众注意；
words.ex: The spotlight shone on the singer during the concert.
words.ex_cn: 演唱会上，聚光灯照在歌手身上。
words.en: A spotlight is a powerful light, for example in a theatre, which can be directed so that it lights up a small area. If someone or something is in the spotlight, they are getting a lot of attention from the public and the media.

words.ex: The cactus has succulent leaves to store water.
words.ex_cn: 仙人掌有多汁的叶子来储存水分。
words.en: (of food) tender, juicy, and tasty; (of a plant) having thick, fleshy tissues adapted to water storage.

words.tr: n. 食物；营养；维持生计
words.ex: Water and food are basic sustenance for life.
words.ex_cn: 水和食物是生命的基本生存物资。
words.en: Sustenance refers to the food and drink that people, animals, and plants need to live and stay healthy. It can also mean the means of maintaining life or supporting existence.

words.ex: Click the tab to open the new page.
words.ex_cn: 点击标签以打开新页面。
words.en: A tab is a small piece of material that sticks out from something, used for opening, closing, or identifying it. In computing, a tab is a key on a keyboard that moves the cursor a set number of spaces or to a specific position. In a restaurant or bar, a tab is a bill for food or drinks that is kept and paid for later.

words.tr: n. 小装饰品；廉价首饰
words.ex: She bought a small trinket at the market.
words.ex_cn: 她在市场上买了一个小饰物。
words.en: A trinket is a small ornament or item of jewelry that is of little value.

words.tr:
adj. 半生不熟的；煮得嫩的
v. 使煮得嫩；使做得不够；不尽全力做；“underdo”的过去分词
words.ex: The steak is underdone.
words.ex_cn: 这块牛排还没熟。
words.en: If food is underdone, it has not been cooked for long enough and is not ready to eat.

words.ex: He eats veal at the restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 他在餐厅吃小牛肉。
words.en: Veal is the meat of a young calf, especially a cow or bull, that is used for food.

words.ex: He ate venison at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 他在晚宴上吃了鹿肉。
words.en: The flesh of a deer used as food.

words.ex: He drank a glass of vodka last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚喝了一杯伏特加。
words.en: A clear, strong alcoholic drink made from grain or potatoes, originally from Russia.

words.ex: He ate a wafer with honey.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一片薄饼配蜂蜜。
words.en: A wafer is a thin, flat, crisp cake or biscuit, often sweet and eaten as a snack or dessert.

chapters.name: 多彩生活 旅游出行 重点词

words.ex: They walked abreast down the street.
words.ex_cn: 他们并肩走在街上。
words.en: If people or things are abreast, they are lined up next to each other, side by side, and often facing the same direction.

words.ex: There are many shops on this avenue.
words.ex_cn: 这条大街上有许多商店。
words.en: An avenue is a wide street or main thoroughfare, often lined with trees or other landscaping.

words.tr: adj. 温和宜人的（气候）；芳香的
words.ex: The balmy wind felt nice on her skin.
words.ex_cn: 温暖的微风轻拂她的皮肤。
words.en: Balmy weather is pleasantly warm and mild.

words.tr:
n. 路障；栅栏；阻碍
v. 设路障；阻挡
words.ex: The police put up a barricade to stop the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 警察设了一个路障来阻止人群。
words.en: A barricade is a temporary structure that is built across a road, entrance, or other route to prevent people from passing. It can also refer to the act of creating such a structure.

words.tr:
int. 呸；嘘
n. 嘘声
v. 发出嘘声
words.ex: The crowd gave a loud boo when the player missed the goal.
words.ex_cn: 当球员错失进球时，观众发出了大声的嘘声。
words.en: If you boo a speaker or performer, you shout 'boo' or make other loud sounds to indicate that you do not like them, their opinions, or their performance.

words.tr:
n. 刹车；制动器
v. 刹车
words.ex: He pressed the brake to stop the car.
words.ex_cn: 他踩了刹车来停车。
words.en: A brake is a device in a vehicle that makes it go slower or stop.

words.ex: He took a brisk walk in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 他早上轻快地散步。
words.en: If someone or something is brisk, they are quick and lively in their actions or movements.

words.tr:
n. 捆；束；包
v. 匆匆送走
words.ex: He bought a bundle of newspapers.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一捆报纸。
words.en: A bundle is a number of things that are tied or wrapped together so that they can be carried or stored easily.

words.tr:
v. 挖洞；钻进；翻寻
n. 地洞
words.ex: The rabbit burrows under the tree.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在树下打洞。
words.en: A burrow is a hole or tunnel dug by a small animal, such as a rabbit or a mole, as a dwelling. As a verb, to burrow means to dig a hole or tunnel for habitation or refuge.

words.ex: The two cars collided at the intersection.
words.ex_cn: 两辆车在十字路口相撞了。
words.en: If two or more moving people or objects collide, they crash into one another.

words.tr: adj. 拥挤的；堵塞的； v. “congest” 的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The road was congested with cars during rush hour.
words.ex_cn: 高峰时段，这条路被汽车挤满了。
words.en: If a place is congested, it is extremely crowded and blocked with traffic or people.

words.ex: The two roads converge at the town center.
words.ex_cn: 这两条路在镇中心交汇。
words.en: If roads or lines converge, they meet or join at a particular place.

words.ex: He conveyed his thanks with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着表达了谢意。
words.en: If you convey information or a message, you communicate it to someone, often in a way that is not direct.

words.tr:
n. 碰撞；坠毁；崩溃；
v. 碰撞；坠毁；崩溃；
words.ex: The car crash happened at the intersection.
words.ex_cn: 汽车碰撞发生在十字路口。
words.en: If a vehicle crashes or if the driver crashes it, it hits something and is damaged or destroyed.

words.ex: He dawdled away the afternoon at the park.
words.ex_cn: 他在公园里混掉了整个下午。
words.en: If you dawdle, you spend more time than is necessary going somewhere or doing something.

words.ex: He will depart tomorrow morning.
words.ex_cn: 他明天早上离开。
words.en: If you depart from a place, you leave it and start a journey to another place.

words.ex: The car deviated from the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车偏离了道路。
words.en: To deviate means to do something that is different from the usual or common way of behaving.

words.ex: The road was diverted around the park.
words.ex_cn: 这条路被改道绕过公园。
words.en: If you divert someone or something, you cause them to change direction or to go somewhere different.

words.ex: He decided to embark on a new career.
words.ex_cn: 他决定从事一份新职业。
words.en: To embark on something means to start it, especially something new, difficult, or exciting.

words.tr:
v. 想要；
adj. 花哨的；昂贵的；
n. 爱好；
words.ex: I fancy a cup of tea.
words.ex_cn: 我想要一杯茶。
words.en: If you describe something as fancy, you mean that it is special, unusual, or elaborate, often because it has a lot of decoration or is very expensive.

words.tr:
v. 中断；暂停；
n. 停顿下来；
words.ex: The storm halted the flight.
words.ex_cn: 风暴中断了航班。
words.en: to bring or come to a stop; a temporary or permanent stop

words.tr: v. 猛冲；猛投；猛烈碰撞
words.ex: The car hurtled down the hill.
words.ex_cn: 汽车飞速冲下山坡。
words.en: If someone or something hurtles somewhere, they move there very quickly, often in a uncontrolled way.

words.ex: The ship's keel was damaged in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 船的龙骨在风暴中受损了。
words.en: The keel is the central structural basis of a ship or boat, running along the bottom from the bow to the stern. It is the first part of a ship's hull to be constructed and is the primary structural element that provides stability and strength to the vessel.

words.ex: He lingered by the door, not wanting to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他逗留在门口，不想离开。
words.en: If you linger somewhere, you stay there for a longer time than is necessary, for example because you are enjoying yourself.

words.tr:
v. 缓慢而弯曲地流动；漫步；闲聊
n. 河流的曲折；漫步；迂回曲折的进程
words.ex: The river meanders through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这条河蜿蜒穿过森林。
words.en: To meander means to follow a winding and turning course, often used to describe the way a river flows or the way a person walks without a clear direction.

words.tr:
n. 山；
v. 逐渐增加；
words.ex: He climbed the mount early in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 他一大早爬了那座山。
words.en: To mount something means to go up it or to get on it. It can also refer to the act of organizing and beginning something, such as an event or an exhibition.

words.ex: He works on a nautical chart.
words.ex_cn: 他正在使用一张航海图。
words.en: Nautical means relating to ships, sailing, or navigation at sea.

words.ex: The fallen tree obstructs the road.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树挡住了道路。
words.en: If something obstructs a road or path, it blocks it, stopping people or vehicles from getting past.

words.ex: He changed his pace to match the group.
words.ex_cn: 他调整了步伐以跟上队伍。
words.en: The speed at which someone or something moves, or with which something happens or changes.

words.ex: He is always punctual for class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课总是准时。
words.en: If you are punctual, you do something or arrive somewhere at the right time and are not late.

words.ex: He likes to ramble about his travels.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢漫谈他的旅行经历。
words.en: To walk for pleasure, especially in the countryside, without a definite route or destination.

words.tr:
n. 缰绳；驾驭；控制
v. 控制；驾驭
words.ex: He uses a leather rein to control the horse.
words.ex_cn: 他用皮缰绳来控制马。
words.en: A rein is a long, narrow strap attached at one end to a horse's bit, typically used in pairs to guide or check a horse while riding or driving.

words.ex: I made a reservation for two at the restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 我在餐厅预订了两个人的座位。
words.en: A reservation is an arrangement whereby something, especially a seat or room, is kept for a particular person who will arrive later.

words.ex: The cat likes to roam around the garden.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫喜欢在花园里游荡。
words.en: To roam means to move about or travel without any definite purpose or destination.

words.ex: He used to rove through the forests when he was young.
words.ex_cn: 他年轻时常常在森林里漫游。
words.en: To rove means to travel constantly without a fixed destination; wander.

words.tr: n. 漫游者；流浪者；漂泊者；
words.ex: The rover explored the surface of Mars.
words.ex_cn: 漫游者探索了火星表面。
words.en: A rover is someone who travels around, often without a fixed route or destination. It can also refer to a vehicle designed to travel over the rough surface of a planet or moon.

words.ex: There was a scramble for the last ticket.
words.ex_cn: 大家争相抢购最后一张票。
words.en: If you scramble over rocks or up a hill, you move quickly over them or up it using your hands to help you. Scramble can also mean to compete or struggle with others for something that is in short supply.

words.ex: He shoved his way through the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他挤过人群。
words.en: To push someone or something in a rough or careless way.

words.tr:
v. 使转轨；使分流；转向一边
n. 转轨；分流器
words.ex: The train was shunted to a side track.
words.ex_cn: 火车被调到了侧线。
words.en: If a train or a railway carriage is shunted, it is moved from one track to another, usually in order to make space for another train or carriage.

words.tr:
v. 打滑；侧滑
n. 打滑；侧滑
words.ex: The car skid on the wet road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在湿滑的路面上打滑了。
words.en: If a vehicle skids, it slides sideways or forwards while moving, usually because of bad weather conditions or because the driver is going too fast.

words.tr:
n. 幻灯片；滑梯；
v. （使）滑动；下滑；
words.ex: He showed a slide of his vacation photos.
words.ex_cn: 他展示了一张他度假照片的幻灯片。
words.en: To move smoothly along a surface while maintaining continuous contact with it; to pass or move quietly or smoothly; a structure with a smooth sloping surface for children to slide down; a decline from a higher to a lower level or status.

words.ex: The stray dog wandered into the backyard.
words.ex_cn: 这只走失的狗走进了后院。
words.en: If someone or something strays, they wander away from where they are supposed to be.

words.tr:
v. 闲逛；散步；漫步；
n. 闲逛；散步；漫步；
words.ex: They stroll in the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他们晚饭后在公园里闲逛。
words.en: If you stroll somewhere, you walk there in a slow, relaxed way.

words.ex: The bus stops at the terminal at 9 PM.
words.ex_cn: 公交车晚上9点到达终点站。
words.en: A terminal is a place where vehicles, passengers, or goods begin or end a journey. It can also refer to a computer device at which a user enters data or commands.

words.tr:
n. 小径；路径；踪迹；
v. 跟踪；尾随；落后于；
words.ex: We walked along the forest trail.
words.ex_cn: 我们沿着森林小径散步。
words.en: A trail is a path through the countryside or through a forest, often made or used by people walking. As a verb, to trail means to follow someone or something secretly or to be behind in a race or competition.

words.ex: The transit of goods takes three days.
words.ex_cn: 货物的运输需要三天。
words.en: The act or process of passing through or across; the conveyance of people or goods from one place to another.

words.tr:
n. 运输；
v. 运输；
words.ex: He uses public transport to go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他乘坐公共交通去上班。
words.en: To transport something or someone is to move them from one place to another, especially over long distances.

words.tr:
v. 改变方向；转向
n. 转向
words.ex: The car veers to the left when the driver turns too fast.
words.ex_cn: 当司机转得太快时，汽车会向左偏转。
words.en: If something veers in a certain direction, it suddenly changes direction and moves in that direction.

words.ex: The hikers enjoyed a beautiful vista from the mountain top.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者们从山顶欣赏到了美丽的景色。
words.en: A vista is a pleasing view, especially one seen through a long, narrow opening.

words.tr: v. 趟水；涉水；艰苦地进行
words.ex: He wades through the shallow river.
words.ex_cn: 他涉水走过浅河。
words.en: To walk through water or another liquid or soft substance that impedes movement.

words.ex: He likes to wander in the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢晚饭后在公园里徘徊。
words.en: If you wander in a place, you walk around there in a casual way, often without intending to go in any particular direction or to any particular place.

chapters.name: 多彩生活 旅游出行 认知词

words.tr:
adv. 漂流地；漫无目的地
adj. 漂泊的；漫无目的的；脱落的
words.ex: The boat was adrift in the sea.
words.ex_cn: 小船在海上漂流。
words.en: If something is adrift, it is floating on the water and not fastened to anything or controlled by anyone.

words.ex: The boat went aground on the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 船在岩石上搁浅了。
words.en: If a ship runs aground, it touches the ground in a shallow part of a river, lake, or the sea, and gets stuck.

words.tr: n. 简易机场；临时跑道
words.ex: The small plane landed on the airstrip.
words.ex_cn: 小型飞机降落在飞机跑道上。
words.en: An airstrip is a piece of land that is used by aircraft to take off and land, especially one that is in a remote area and does not have the facilities of an airport.

words.tr:
v. 落下；
adj. 点亮的；
words.ex: The bird alighted on the tree.
words.ex_cn: 鸟落在了树上。
words.en: If someone alights from a vehicle or if they alight, they get out of it after a journey.

words.ex: The apex of the mountain is covered with snow.
words.ex_cn: 山的最高点被雪覆盖。
words.en: The highest point or top of something; the climax or culmination of something.

words.tr: n. 拱廊；有拱廊的街道；游乐中心
words.ex: The old arcade has stone pillars and a tiled roof.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的拱廊有石柱和瓦片屋顶。
words.en: A covered passage with arches along one or both sides.

words.tr:
adv. 迷路地；误入歧途地
adj. 迷路的；误入歧途的
words.ex: The little dog went astray in the park.
words.ex_cn: 那只小狗在公园里走丢了。
words.en: If you go astray, you lose your direction when you are trying to go somewhere.

words.ex: He leaned on the wooden balustrade.
words.ex_cn: 他靠在木制栏杆上。
words.en: A balustrade is a row of small columns topped by a rail, serving as a protective barrier at the edge of a balcony, bridge, or terrace.

words.ex: He pushes a barrow full of bricks.
words.ex_cn: 他推着一辆装满砖块的手推车。
words.en: A barrow is a large mound of earth that was used to cover a grave in ancient times. It can also refer to a small cart with two wheels that is used for carrying goods.

words.tr: v. 晒太阳（取暖）；沉浸于
words.ex: He basks in the warm sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 他沐浴在温暖的阳光下。
words.en: If you bask in the sunshine, you lie somewhere sunny and enjoy the heat.

words.ex: He competes in bobsleigh during winter.
words.ex_cn: 他在冬天参加雪车比赛。
words.en: A bobsleigh is a vehicle used for racing on ice, typically consisting of a streamlined body mounted on two pairs of runners, with the front pair being steerable.

words.ex: He races in a bobsled during the winter Olympics.
words.ex_cn: 他在冬奥会上参加雪橇比赛。
words.en: A bobsled is a vehicle used in the sport of bobsleighing, which is a winter sport where teams make timed runs down narrow, twisting, banked, iced tracks in a gravity-powered sled.

words.ex: He walked down the wide boulevard with many shops.
words.ex_cn: 他沿着满是商店的宽阔大马路散步。
words.en: A boulevard is a wide street in a city, usually with trees along the sides.

words.tr:
adj. 臭虫多的
n. 轻型马车；婴儿车
words.ex: The old cabin is buggy after the summer rain.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧小屋在夏雨后虫子很多。
words.en: A buggy is a small, lightweight vehicle, often open and with four wheels, used for recreation or transportation over rough terrain.

words.ex: They had a bumper harvest this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年他们获得了异常大的收成。
words.en: A bumper is a bar at the front and back of a vehicle that reduces damage if the vehicle hits something.

words.tr:
n. 旁路；
v. 绕过；
words.ex: The city built a bypass around the old town.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市建了一条绕过老城区的旁路。
words.en: If you bypass a place or a system, you avoid it or go around it instead of going through it.

words.tr: n. 歌舞表演；卡巴莱歌舞表演；有歌舞表演的餐馆
words.ex: The cabaret featured a variety of musical acts.
words.ex_cn: 卡巴莱歌舞表演包括了多种音乐表演。
words.en: A cabaret is a type of entertainment venue, combining music, dance, and drama, often performed in a restaurant or nightclub setting.

words.ex: He paddles a canoe on the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他划着独木舟在湖上航行。
words.en: A canoe is a small, narrow boat that you move through the water using a paddle.

words.ex: The tent has a waterproof canopy.
words.ex_cn: 这顶帐篷有一个防水天篷。
words.en: A canopy is a layer of something that spreads out and covers an area, especially the branches and leaves that spread out at the top of trees in a forest.

words.ex: The river flows through a deep canyon.
words.ex_cn: 河流流经一个深峡谷。
words.en: A canyon is a large valley with very steep sides and usually a river flowing along the bottom.

words.ex: The lighthouse is on the cape.
words.ex_cn: 灯塔位于海角上。
words.en: A cape is a sleeveless outer garment that fastens at the neck and hangs over the shoulders and back, or a piece of land jutting into the sea or some other large body of water.

words.ex: The workers walked on the catwalk above the factory floor.
words.ex_cn: 工人们走在工厂地板上方的狭窄人行道上。
words.en: A narrow walkway, especially one high above the ground or one used by models in a fashion show.

words.ex: The clearway is blocked by a broken car.
words.ex_cn: 清空通道被一辆坏掉的车堵住了。
words.en: A clearway is a road or section of road where vehicles are not allowed to stop, except in an emergency, in order to keep the traffic moving smoothly.

words.ex: The axe will cleave the wood in two.
words.ex_cn: 斧头会把木头劈成两半。
words.en: To split or sever something, especially along a natural line or grain; to adhere firmly and closely or loyally and unwaveringly to something.

words.tr:
n. 厚木底皮鞋；木屐
v. 堵塞；妨碍
words.ex: She wore wooden clogs to work in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 她穿着厚木底皮鞋去花园干活。
words.en: If something clogs a hole or place, it blocks it so that nothing can pass through.

words.tr:
n. 鹅卵石
v. 修补（鞋）；粗制滥造
words.ex: He cobbled together a shoe from old leather.
words.ex_cn: 他用旧皮革拼凑了一双鞋。
words.en: To cobble means to make or assemble something in a rough or improvised way, or to pave with cobblestones.

words.ex: The train has a sleeping compartment for passengers.
words.ex_cn: 火车上有一个供乘客休息的隔间。
words.en: A compartment is a separate section or part of something, especially a space in a vehicle that is separated from other spaces.

words.ex: He used a compass to find north.
words.ex_cn: 他用指南针找北方。
words.en: A compass is an instrument that you use for finding directions. It has a dial and a magnetic needle that always points to the north.

words.ex: He stopped at the crossroads to decide which way to go.
words.ex_cn: 他在十字路口停下来，决定走哪条路。
words.en: A crossroads is a place where two roads cross each other. It can also refer to a point in time when a crucial decision must be made that will have far-reaching consequences.

words.tr: n. 甲板水手；下级水手
words.ex: The deckhand cleaned the boat every morning.
words.ex_cn: 甲板工每天早上打扫船。
words.en: A deckhand is a person who works on the deck of a ship, performing various tasks to assist in the operation and maintenance of the vessel.

words.ex: The departure of the train was at 8 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 火车的出发时间是晚上8点。
words.en: The act of leaving a place, especially at the start of a journey.

words.ex: The trucks stop at the depot to load goods.
words.ex_cn: 卡车在仓库停靠以装载货物。
words.en: A depot is a place where large amounts of raw materials, manufactured goods, or equipment are stored until they are needed.

words.ex: The train will derail if the tracks are broken.
words.ex_cn: 如果铁轨损坏，火车就会脱轨。
words.en: To cause a train or other vehicle to leave its tracks accidentally; to divert or cause to deviate from an intended course.

words.tr: n. 无篷小艇；小舟；救生筏；
words.ex: They rowed the dinghy to the island.
words.ex_cn: 他们划着无篷小艇去了岛上。
words.en: A dinghy is a small boat that you sail or row.

words.tr:
adj. 免下车即可得到服务的
n. 免下车餐馆；免下车电影院；免下车商业场所
words.ex: We ate burgers at a drive-in last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚在汽车餐厅吃了汉堡。
words.en: A drive-in is a place such as a restaurant or cinema where you can be served or watch a film without leaving your car.

words.ex: The elevation of his skills helped him get a better job.
words.ex_cn: 他技能的提升帮助他找到了一份更好的工作。
words.en: The height to which something is elevated or to which it rises.

words.ex: The entrance to the building is on the left.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑的入口在左边。
words.en: An entrance is a way into a place, such as a door or gate. It can also refer to the act of entering a place or the right to enter.

words.ex: He showed his entree to the concert hall.
words.ex_cn: 他向音乐厅出示了他的入场许可。
words.en: The main course of a meal; the act of entering.

words.ex: We went on an excursion to the mountains last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 上周末我们去山区进行了短途旅行。
words.en: An excursion is a short journey or trip, especially one taken as a leisure activity.

words.ex: The team went on an expedition to the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍去山上探险了。
words.en: An expedition is an organized journey that is made for a particular purpose such as exploration.

words.ex: The bicycle's freewheel allows the rider to coast without pedaling.
words.ex_cn: 自行车上的自由飞轮使骑车人可以在不踩踏板的情况下滑行。
words.en: To freewheel means to move or operate freely without constraint or control, often implying a lack of concern for the consequences.

words.ex: The freight train carried boxes to the city.
words.ex_cn: 货运列车把箱子运到了城市。
words.en: Freight refers to goods transported in bulk by truck, train, ship, or aircraft. It can also mean the charge for such transportation.

words.ex: The freighter was loaded with tons of cargo.
words.ex_cn: 这艘货船装载了数吨货物。
words.en: A freighter is a large ship or aircraft designed to carry goods.

words.tr:
n. 缆索铁道
adj. 索状的
words.ex: The funicular railway climbs the steep mountain.
words.ex_cn: 缆车沿着陡峭的山坡攀爬。
words.en: A funicular is a type of cable railway system which connects points along a railway track laid on a steep slope.

words.ex: The children played on the gravel path.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在砾石小路上玩耍。
words.en: Gravel consists of very small stones. It is often used to make paths and roads.

words.tr:
n. 马笼头；缰绳
v. 套上笼头；系上缰绳
words.ex: The cowboy carefully adjusted the halter on his horse.
words.ex_cn: 牛仔仔细地调整了马的笼头。
words.en: A halter is a piece of rope or a strap that is fastened around an animal's head so that it can be led by someone.

words.ex: She applied the handbrake to stop the car.
words.ex_cn: 她拉起手刹来停车。
words.en: A handbrake is a device in a vehicle that is used to keep it stationary when it is parked, operated by hand.

words.tr: n. （自行车或摩托车的）把手
words.ex: He adjusted the handlebar before riding his bike.
words.ex_cn: 他骑自行车前调整了把手。
words.en: The handlebar is the bar on a bicycle or motorcycle that you hold onto when riding.

words.ex: The airplane was parked in the hangar for maintenance.
words.ex_cn: 飞机被停在机库中进行维修。
words.en: A hangar is a large building in which aircraft are kept.

words.tr: adj. 构成核心的；顽固的；赤裸裸的
words.ex: The hard-core members of the team never miss practice.
words.ex_cn: 团队的核心成员从不缺席训练。
words.en: Someone who is hard-core is very committed to a particular activity or belief, often to an extreme degree.

words.tr: n. 硬顶小汽车；室内电影院
words.ex: The convertible has a removable hardtop for all-weather driving.
words.ex_cn: 这款敞篷车有一个可拆卸的金属顶盖，适合各种天气驾驶。
words.en: A hardtop is a car with a rigid roof, as distinct from a convertible.

words.ex: He drives a hatchback for its practicality.
words.ex_cn: 他开一辆掀背车，因为它的实用性。
words.en: A hatchback is a car with a door across the full width at the back end that opens upwards to provide access to a storage area.

words.ex: The company specializes in haulage of goods across the country.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司专门从事全国范围的货物运输。
words.en: Haulage refers to the business of transporting goods by road or railway.

words.ex: He slung his haversack over his shoulder and set off on his journey.
words.ex_cn: 他把粗帆布背包甩到肩上，开始了他的旅程。
words.en: A haversack is a bag carried over one shoulder, typically made of canvas and used by soldiers or hikers to carry their belongings.

words.ex: He took the helm of the company after the CEO retired.
words.ex_cn: CEO退休后，他成为了公司的领导人。
words.en: The helm is the wheel or control which is used to steer a ship or boat.

words.tr: n. （旅行用的）手提箱或手提袋
words.ex: He packed his clothes in a holdall.
words.ex_cn: 他把衣服装进了一个旅行包。
words.en: A holdall is a large bag that you carry your clothes and other possessions in when you are traveling.

words.tr:
adj. 有返回原地本能的；自动寻向的
v. 送…回家；提供住处；“home”的现在分词
words.ex: The pigeon is homing to its nest.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子正飞回它的巢。
words.en: Homing refers to the ability to return home or to a specific location, especially used in the context of animals or devices.

words.tr:
n. 雁叫声；汽车喇叭声
v. （使汽车喇叭）鸣响；（雁）叫
words.ex: The honk of the geese echoed over the lake.
words.ex_cn: 大雁的叫声在湖面上回荡。
words.en: 1. The sound made by a car horn. 2. The cry of a goose. 3. To make a sound like a car horn or a goose.

words.tr:
n. 猫头鹰叫声；汽笛响声；叫嚣声
v. 作猫头鹰叫声；汽笛等嘟嘟响；大声叫嚣
words.ex: The hoot of an owl echoed through the night.
words.ex_cn: 猫头鹰的叫声在夜晚回荡。
words.en: To make the sound that an owl makes, or to make a similar sound as a signal or in disapproval.

words.ex: The horseshoe is nailed to a horse's hoof.
words.ex_cn: 马蹄形铁掌被钉在马的蹄子上。
words.en: A horseshoe is a piece of metal shaped like a U, which is fixed with nails to the bottom of a horse's foot in order to protect it.

words.ex: The boy rides a horse every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩每天早上骑马。
words.en: A horse is a large animal which people can ride. Some horses are used for pulling ploughs and carts.

words.ex: The little girl rides a horsey at the park.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩在公园里骑小马。
words.en: Resembling or characteristic of a horse; fond of horses.

words.tr: n. 旅馆经理；旅馆老板；
words.ex: The hotelier welcomed guests with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 旅馆经理微笑着欢迎客人。
words.en: A person who owns or manages a hotel.

words.tr: n. 大型废弃物；巨大笨重的人（物）
words.ex: The old boat was left as a hulk on the shore.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船被遗弃在岸边，成为了一堆大型废弃物。
words.en: A hulk is a large, clumsy, or old ship that is no longer in use and is often left to decay in a harbor.

words.tr: n. 破冰船；打破僵局者
words.ex: He told a joke to start an icebreaker.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了个笑话来破冰。
words.en: An icebreaker is a ship designed to move through ice-covered waters, or something that serves to relieve tension or get conversation going in a social situation.

words.ex: We planned our itinerary before the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们在旅行前规划了路线。
words.en: An itinerary is a plan of a journey, including the route and the places that you will visit.

words.ex: He jaywalks across the street without looking.
words.ex_cn: 他不看路就横穿马路。
words.en: To jaywalk means to cross a street in a careless and dangerous way, or in an illegal place.

words.ex: The car stopped at the junction.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在交叉路口停了下来。
words.en: A junction is a place where two or more things, especially roads or railways, come together.

words.ex: At this juncture, we need to make a decision.
words.ex_cn: 在这一关键时刻，我们需要做出决定。
words.en: A particular point in events or time, especially one that is critical or decisive.

words.ex: The landscape after the rain is very beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 雨后的景色非常美丽。
words.en: A landscape is all the visible features of an area of land, often considered in terms of their aesthetic appeal.

words.tr: n. 小路；小巷；航道；车道；航线；
words.ex: The children walked down the narrow lane to school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们沿着狭窄的小路去上学。
words.en: A lane is a narrow road, especially in the country. It can also refer to a division of a road intended to separate lines of traffic moving in the same or opposite directions.

words.ex: The liner sailed across the ocean with hundreds of passengers.
words.ex_cn: 这艘邮轮载着数百名乘客横渡了海洋。
words.en: A liner is a large ship that carries passengers on regular journeys.

words.ex: He is loitering near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他正在公园附近闲逛。
words.en: If someone loiters somewhere, they remain there or walk up and down without any real purpose.

words.ex: The mechanic applied a lubricant to the moving parts.
words.ex_cn: 机械师给活动部件涂上了润滑油。
words.en: A substance, such as oil or grease, used to minimize friction, heat, and wear between mechanical parts in contact with each other.

words.ex: He had to lug the heavy box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不用力拖动那个沉重的箱子穿过房间。
words.en: To carry or drag something heavy with great effort.

words.tr: n. 支柱；中坚；中流砥柱
words.ex: His support has been the mainstay of the project.
words.ex_cn: 他的支持一直是这个项目的支柱。
words.en: If you describe something as the mainstay of a particular thing, you mean that it is the most basic part of it.

words.ex: The marine birds fly over the sea.
words.ex_cn: 这些海鸟在海面上飞翔。
words.en: Marine is used to describe things relating to the sea or to the ships and boats which sail on it.

words.ex: The wedding party was held under a large marquee in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 婚礼派对在花园里的大帐篷下举行。
words.en: A marquee is a large tent used for social or commercial events, or the canopy over the entrance to a theater or cinema.

words.tr: n. 纪念品；用以回忆的东西
words.ex: She keeps a photo as a memento of her trip.
words.ex_cn: 她保留了一张照片作为旅行的纪念品。
words.en: A memento is an object which you keep because it reminds you of a person or a special event.

words.ex: The school is five kilometers from my house.
words.ex_cn: 学校离我家五公里。
words.en: A kilometer is a unit of length in the metric system, equal to one thousand meters.

words.ex: The ship uses GPS for navigation.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船使用GPS进行导航。
words.en: The process or activity of accurately ascertaining one's position and planning and following a route.

words.tr:
adj. 不停的；直达的；
adv. 不停地；直达地；
words.ex: The train makes a nonstop journey from Beijing to Shanghai.
words.ex_cn: 这列火车从北京到上海是不停站的。
words.en: If something is nonstop, it continues without any pauses or interruptions.

words.tr: n. 路由；路径选择；（材料或产品的）加工路线安排
words.ex: The router uses routing to send data to the right place.
words.ex_cn: 路由器使用路由将数据发送到正确的地方。
words.en: Routing refers to the process of selecting paths in a network along which to send network traffic, or the act of directing or sending something along a particular path.

words.ex: The children ran outwards from the house.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们从房子里向外跑。
words.en: Moving or facing away from the center or a particular point; towards the outside.

words.ex: The sailor fell overboard during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 水手在风暴中从船上掉入海中。
words.en: If someone falls overboard, they fall from a ship into the water. It can also mean doing something to an excessive degree.

words.ex: He pressed the pedal to speed up the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他踩下踏板让自行车加速。
words.en: A pedal is a lever that you press with your foot in order to control a vehicle or machine.

words.ex: The pedestrian crossed the street at the zebra crossing.
words.ex_cn: 行人在斑马线处过马路。
words.en: A pedestrian is a person who is walking in a city, town, or village, especially along a pavement or in a pedestrian area.

words.ex: The fence marks the perimeter of the garden.
words.ex_cn: 围栏标出了花园的边界。
words.en: The perimeter of an area or object is the total length of its sides or outer boundary.

words.ex: The fisherman walked to the pier to check his nets.
words.ex_cn: 渔夫走到码头去检查他的渔网。
words.en: A pier is a platform sticking out into water, usually the sea, which people walk along or use when getting onto or off boats.

words.ex: The procession moved slowly down the street.
words.ex_cn: 行列缓缓沿着街道行进。
words.en: A procession is a group of people who are walking, riding, or driving in a line as part of a public event.

words.ex: They crossed the river on a wooden raft.
words.ex_cn: 他们乘着木筏渡过了河。
words.en: A raft is a flat structure made of pieces of wood tied together, which is used as a boat or floating platform.

words.ex: He rides a rickshaw to the market.
words.ex_cn: 他坐人力车去市场。
words.en: A rickshaw is a small, light vehicle with two wheels that is pulled by one person and used for carrying passengers, especially in Asian countries.

words.tr:
n. 索具装备；钻探设备；装备
v. 配备索具；操纵；舞弊
words.ex: He uses a rig to hold the camera steady.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个支架来固定相机。
words.en: To rig something means to arrange or set it up in a particular way, often in a temporary or makeshift manner. It can also refer to the equipment used in drilling for oil or gas, or the sails and ropes on a ship.

words.ex: The company is responsible for maintaining the rolling-stock.
words.ex_cn: 该公司负责维护铁路车辆。
words.en: Rolling stock refers to the vehicles that move on a railway, including locomotives, passenger coaches, and freight wagons.

words.ex: The helicopter's rotor began to spin rapidly.
words.ex_cn: 直升机的旋翼开始快速旋转。
words.en: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine or device, especially in motors, turbines, and helicopters.

words.ex: The car turned at the roundabout near the park.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在公园附近的环形交叉路口转弯。
words.en: A roundabout is a circular area at a place where several roads meet. You drive round it until you come to the road that you want.

words.ex: He carries his books in a rucksack.
words.ex_cn: 他把书放在帆布背包里。
words.en: A rucksack is a bag with shoulder straps that allow it to be carried on someone's back, typically used by hikers or travelers.

words.ex: The hikers walked on a rugged trail.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者走在一条崎岖的小路上。
words.en: A rugged area of land is uneven and covered with rocks, with few trees or plants.

words.tr:
n. 马鞍；鞍座
v. 给（马）装鞍
words.ex: The boy rode on a saddle on the horse.
words.ex_cn: 男孩骑在马的马鞍上。
words.en: A saddle is a seat for a rider on the back of a horse or other animal, or a similar seat on a bicycle or motorcycle. It can also refer to the act of putting a saddle on a horse or to burden someone with a responsibility.

words.tr: n. （在非洲的）旅行；狩猎旅行；
words.ex: We went on a safari in Kenya to see lions and elephants.
words.ex_cn: 我们去肯尼亚旅行，去看狮子和大象。
words.en: A safari is a trip to observe or hunt wild animals, especially in East or Southern Africa.

words.tr: n. 厚篷帆布；制衣用帆布
words.ex: The tent was made of sturdy sailcloth.
words.ex_cn: 这个帐篷是用结实的帆布做的。
words.en: A type of strong, heavy cloth that is used for making sails.

words.tr: n. 轿子；小轿车；厢式轿车
words.ex: The man rode in a sedan carried by two servants.
words.ex_cn: 这个人坐在两个仆人抬的轿子里。
words.en: A sedan is a type of car that has a closed body and a separate trunk, typically seating four or more people.

words.ex: He found a shortcut to school.
words.ex_cn: 他找到了一条去学校的捷径。
words.en: A quicker or more direct way to get somewhere or do something.

words.tr: n. 看见； v. “sight”的现在分词；
words.ex: The sighting of a rare bird excited the birdwatchers.
words.ex_cn: 看到一只稀有鸟类让观鸟者兴奋不已。
words.en: The act of seeing or noticing someone or something, especially something unusual or unexpected.

words.ex: The sleeper breathed deeply in the quiet room.
words.ex_cn: 睡眠者在安静的房间里深呼吸。
words.en: A sleeper is someone who is sleeping, or a thing that unexpectedly becomes very successful.

words.ex: The children played on the slope behind the house.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在房子后面的斜坡上玩耍。
words.en: A slope is a surface that is at an angle, so that one end is higher than the other.

words.tr:
n. 陷阱；圈套
v. 用陷阱（或罗网）捕捉
words.ex: The hunter set a snare to catch the rabbit.
words.ex_cn: 猎人设了一个陷阱来抓兔子。
words.en: A snare is a trap for catching animals, especially one that uses a noose. It can also refer to a situation that tricks someone into doing something or to catch someone in such a situation.

words.ex: I bought a souvenir from the beach.
words.ex_cn: 我从海边买了一个纪念品。
words.en: A souvenir is something which you buy or keep to remind you of a holiday, place, or event.

words.ex: The fireworks at night were a beautiful spectacle.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚的烟花是一场美丽的奇观。
words.en: A spectacle is a visually striking performance or display.

words.ex: The boat turned to starboard to avoid the rock.
words.ex_cn: 船向右转以避开岩石。
words.en: The right side of a ship or aircraft when facing forward.

words.ex: He adjusted his stirrup before mounting the horse.
words.ex_cn: 他上马前调整了马镫。
words.en: A stirrup is a loop, ring, or other contrivance of metal, wood, leather, etc., suspended from the saddle of a horse to support the rider's foot.

words.tr:
adj. 用柏油覆盖的
v. 耽搁；逗留
words.ex: The workers tarry at the road, waiting for the asphalt to dry.
words.ex_cn: 工人们在道路上耽搁，等着沥青变干。
words.en: To tarry means to stay longer than intended or to delay leaving a place.

words.tr: n. 运输；运输系统；交通工具；
words.ex: The city improved its transportation system.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市改善了它的运输系统。
words.en: Transportation refers to the movement of people, animals, and goods from one place to another.

words.ex: They traverse the forest to reach the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们横穿森林去到达村庄。
words.en: To traverse something means to move or travel across it, often with some difficulty.

words.tr: n. 拖网渔船；拖网捕鱼者
words.ex: The trawler caught fish far out at sea.
words.ex_cn: 那艘拖网渔船在远海捕到了鱼。
words.en: A trawler is a fishing boat that is used for trawling, which is a method of fishing that involves pulling a fishing net through the water behind one or more boats.

words.tr:
n. 艰苦跋涉；
v. 长途跋涉；
words.ex: The trek across the mountains took five days.
words.ex_cn: 穿越群山的艰苦跋涉花了五天时间。
words.en: A trek is a long and often difficult journey, especially one made on foot.

words.ex: The tripper bought a souvenir at the market.
words.ex_cn: 这个旅行者在市场买了一件纪念品。
words.en: A person who travels or visits a place for pleasure; someone who stumbles or trips; a person who uses hallucinogenic drugs.

words.tr:
adj. 地下的；
n. 地铁；地下；
adv. 在地下；
words.ex: The underground tunnel connects two buildings.
words.ex_cn: 这条地下的隧道连接了两座建筑。
words.en: Something that is underground is below the surface of the ground. It can also refer to secret activities or organizations.

words.tr: n. （铁路或公路下的）地下通道
words.ex: The dog ran under the underpass.
words.ex_cn: 狗从立交桥下跑过去了。
words.en: An underpass is a road or path that goes under another road or a railway.

words.ex: The upkeep of the house costs a lot each month.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子的维护每月花费很多。
words.en: The process of keeping something in good condition, especially a building or a piece of equipment.

words.ex: The vagabond sleeps under the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 这个流浪汉睡在桥下。
words.en: A vagabond is someone who wanders from place to place without a home or job.

chapters.name: 多彩生活 健康医疗 重点词

words.ex: The wind began to abate after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，风开始减弱。
words.en: If something bad or undesirable abates, it becomes much less strong or severe.

words.tr:
v. 中止；中断；放弃；堕（胎）
n. 中止计划
words.ex: He decided to abort the mission because it was too dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 他决定中止任务，因为太危险了。
words.en: If an unborn baby is aborted, the pregnancy is ended deliberately and the baby is not born alive.

words.ex: Loud noise aggravates his headache.
words.ex_cn: 噪音加重了他的头痛。
words.en: If someone or something aggravates a situation, they make it worse.

words.ex: He is allergic to peanuts.
words.ex_cn: 他对花生过敏。
words.en: If you are allergic to something, you become ill or get a rash when you eat it, smell it, or touch it.

words.ex: Drugs can alleviate pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To make something less severe or intense.

words.ex: He tries to assimilate new words every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力吸收新单词。
words.en: To assimilate means to take in and understand fully ideas, information, or culture, or to make something become part of a group or system.

words.ex: The benign teacher always helped students after class.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师总是在课后帮助学生。
words.en: A benign substance or process does not have any harmful effects.

words.tr: v. 擦伤；挫伤；出现伤痕；
words.ex: He bruised his knee when he fell off the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他从自行车上摔下来时擦伤了膝盖。
words.en: A bruise is a mark that appears on your skin after you have been injured, but the skin is not broken.

words.ex: He has a chronic cough that lasts for months.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个持续数月的慢性咳嗽。
words.en: A chronic illness or condition lasts for a long time and cannot be cured, but it can usually be controlled.

words.ex: He could not conceive a world without technology.
words.ex_cn: 他无法设想一个没有科技的世界。
words.en: To conceive means to form or devise a plan or idea in the mind; to become pregnant.

words.ex: He will consult a doctor for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他将咨询医生治疗他的头痛。
words.en: to seek information or advice from someone, especially someone who is an expert in a particular field

words.ex: The corpulent man walks slowly.
words.ex_cn: 这位肥胖的男人走得很慢。
words.en: If you describe someone as corpulent, you mean they are fat.

words.tr:
n. 抽筋；痉挛；夹钳
v. 束缚；使痉挛；用夹钳夹紧
words.ex: He got a cramp in his leg while running.
words.ex_cn: 他在跑步时腿抽筋了。
words.en: A cramp is a sudden, involuntary muscle contraction or over-shortening; while generally temporary and non-damaging, they can cause mild-to-severe pain, and a paralysis-like immobility of the affected muscle.

words.tr:
v. 使目眩；使眼花；使惊叹
n. 耀眼；眩惑；灿烂
words.ex: The stars dazzle at night.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚的星星闪耀夺目。
words.en: If something dazzles you, it is so bright that you cannot see properly for a short time. It can also mean to greatly impress someone.

words.ex: The doctor can diagnose the illness quickly.
words.ex_cn: 医生能很快诊断出这种病。
words.en: If someone or something is diagnosed as having a particular illness or problem, their illness or problem is identified. If an illness or problem is diagnosed, it is identified.

words.tr: v. 使关节脱位；使脱臼；使混乱
words.ex: He dislocated his shoulder while playing basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他在打篮球时脱臼了肩膀。
words.en: To dislocate something means to force it out of its proper position or place, especially a bone in a joint.

words.ex: The nurse will dispense medicine to the patients.
words.ex_cn: 护士将分发药品给病人。
words.en: To dispense means to distribute or provide something, especially in a systematic way, or to prepare and give out medicine.

words.ex: He did a disservice to his team by lying.
words.ex_cn: 他通过撒谎给团队带来了害处。
words.en: If you do someone or something a disservice, you harm them in some way.

words.ex: The doctor gave him a small dose of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他一小剂量的药。
words.en: A dose of a medicine or a drug is the amount of it that you take at one time, or the amount that is recommended for you to take.

words.ex: The epidemic spread quickly across the country.
words.ex_cn: 这种流行病迅速蔓延到全国。
words.en: An epidemic is a large number of cases of an infectious disease occurring at the same time.

words.ex: The wound began to fester if not cleaned.
words.ex_cn: 如果不清洗，伤口就会恶化。
words.en: If a wound festers, it becomes infected, making it worse.

words.tr: adj. 发烧的；紧张忙乱的；极度紧张（或兴奋）的
words.ex: He is feverish after running in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 他在太阳下跑步后发高烧。
words.en: If you are feverish, you are suffering from a fever, or you are extremely excited or worried about something.

words.ex: He has flabby arms from not exercising.
words.ex_cn: 他因为不锻炼，手臂松软。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as flabby, you are criticizing them for being soft and loose rather than firm and strong.

words.ex: He fractured his arm during the soccer game.
words.ex_cn: 他在足球比赛中摔断了手臂。
words.en: If something such as a bone fractures or is fractured, it breaks or cracks.

words.ex: He hallucinates when he is very sick.
words.ex_cn: 当他病得很重时，他会产生幻觉。
words.en: To hallucinate means to experience a seemingly real perception of something not actually present, often as a result of a mental disorder or the use of drugs.

words.tr:
n. 绳肌腱；腿筋
v. 割断腿筋；使不能正常工作
words.ex: He injured his hamstring during the soccer match.
words.ex_cn: 他在足球比赛中拉伤了绳肌腱。
words.en: A hamstring is a tendon at the back of a person's knee. If someone is hamstrung by something, it means they are severely restricted in their ability to act or perform.

words.tr:
n. 残疾；障碍；阻碍；不利
v. 妨碍；使不利
words.ex: He has a physical handicap but still runs every day.
words.ex_cn: 他有身体残疾，但仍然每天跑步。
words.en: A handicap is a condition that markedly restricts a person's ability to function physically, mentally, or socially.

words.ex: The wound will heal in a few days.
words.ex_cn: 伤口几天后就会愈合。
words.en: To make or become healthy or whole again; to cure or recover from an injury or illness.

words.tr: v. 送医院治疗；使住院
words.ex: He was hospitalized after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后被送进了医院。
words.en: To admit someone into a hospital for treatment.

words.ex: Good hygiene helps prevent sickness.
words.ex_cn: 良好的卫生有助于预防疾病。
words.en: Hygiene refers to conditions and practices that help to maintain health and prevent the spread of diseases.

words.tr: adj. 有免疫力的；免疫的；不受影响的；
words.ex: Children are immune to this disease after vaccination.
words.ex_cn: 儿童接种疫苗后对这种疾病有免疫力。
words.en: If you are immune to a particular disease, you cannot be affected by it. If you are immune to something such as criticism, it does not affect you.

words.ex: The doctor will immunize the child against measles.
words.ex_cn: 医生会给这个孩子接种麻疹疫苗。
words.en: To immunize someone or something means to protect them against a disease by giving them a vaccine.

words.ex: The dentist placed a dental implant to replace the missing tooth.
words.ex_cn: 牙医植入了一个牙科植入物来替代缺失的牙齿。
words.en: To implant something means to put it firmly into something else, especially into a person's body.

words.tr: v. 使充满；灌注；使怀孕
words.ex: The rain impregnates the soil quickly.
words.ex_cn: 雨水迅速浸透了土壤。
words.en: To make a woman or female animal pregnant; to saturate or fill something with a substance.

words.ex: The artist incised the design into the wood.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家将设计雕刻在木头上。
words.en: To cut into a surface with a sharp tool; to carve or engrave.

words.tr:
adj. 不能治愈的；无可救药的
n. 患不治之症者；不能治愈的人
words.ex: The disease is incurable.
words.ex_cn: 这种病无法治愈。
words.en: If someone has an incurable disease, they cannot be cured of it.

words.ex: He ate too much and had indigestion.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多了，导致消化不良。
words.en: Indigestion is pain or discomfort in your stomach, usually after eating, which is caused by difficulty in digesting food.

words.tr:
adj. 不舒服的；有病的；不愿意的
v. 使厌恶；使不适当；使不能；“indispose”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is indisposed today and cannot come to work.
words.ex_cn: 他今天身体不适，不能来上班。
words.en: If you say that someone is indisposed, you mean that they are not available because they are ill, or for a reason that you do not want to mention.

words.ex: The virus can infect people quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒能迅速感染人。
words.en: To infect someone or something means to cause them to have a disease or illness.

words.ex: The spy tried to infiltrate the enemy base.
words.ex_cn: 间谍试图渗透敌方基地。
words.en: To enter or gain access to (an organization, place, etc.) surreptitiously and gradually, especially in order to acquire secret information.

words.ex: The old man is infirm and needs help to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人身体虚弱，需要帮助才能走路。
words.en: If someone is infirm, they are weak or ill, and often old.

words.ex: His infirmity made it hard to walk.
words.ex_cn: 他的虚弱使他走路困难。
words.en: An infirmity is a physical or mental weakness.

words.ex: His rude words inflamed the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了人群。
words.en: To inflame a situation or feeling means to make it much more intense or serious.

words.tr: v. 预防注射；接种疫苗
words.ex: The doctor will inoculate the child against measles.
words.ex_cn: 医生会给这个孩子接种麻疹疫苗。
words.en: To inoculate someone against a disease means to inject a weak form of the disease into their body as a way of protecting them against it.

words.tr: n. 精神错乱；精神失常；疯狂
words.ex: He was sent to a hospital because of insanity.
words.ex_cn: 他因精神错乱被送进了医院。
words.en: Insanity is the state of being seriously mentally ill; madness.

words.ex: The poison is lethal to humans.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒药对人类是致命的。
words.en: Something that is lethal can kill people or animals.

words.tr:
adj. 有害的；恶意的
v. 中伤；污蔑
words.ex: The virus is malign and spreads quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒是有害的，并且传播迅速。
words.en: If you malign someone, you say unpleasant and untrue things about them. If something is malign, it is harmful or evil.

words.tr: adj. 恶毒的；恶性的；恶意的
words.ex: His malignant words hurt everyone around him.
words.ex_cn: 他恶毒的话语伤害了周围的所有人。
words.en: If you say that someone is malignant, you mean they are very dangerous and cause harm to people.

words.tr: n. 狂热； 癖好；躁狂症
words.ex: He has a mania for collecting stamps.
words.ex_cn: 他痴迷于收集邮票。
words.en: An extreme enthusiasm or desire for something, often to the point of obsession.

words.tr:
v. 严重伤害；粗暴对待；抨击
n. 大木槌
words.ex: The bear mauled the hiker, leaving deep wounds.
words.ex_cn: 熊袭击了徒步者，留下了深深的伤口。
words.en: To maul someone or something means to attack them and cause them serious injury, or to handle them roughly.

words.tr: n. 流产；早产；误投；失败
words.ex: She had a miscarriage last month.
words.ex_cn: 她上个月流产了。
words.en: A miscarriage is the premature expulsion of a fetus from the womb before it is able to survive independently, or a failure to achieve the intended result of a plan or action.

words.ex: Planting trees can mitigate air pollution.
words.ex_cn: 植树可以减轻空气污染。
words.en: To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.

words.tr: adj. 病态的；心理不健康的
words.ex: He has a morbid fear of the dark.
words.ex_cn: 他对黑暗有一种病态的恐惧。
words.en: If you describe a person or their interest in something as morbid, you mean that they are very interested in unpleasant things, especially death, and you think this is strange.

words.ex: The mortality rate in the region increased last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年该地区的死亡率上升了。
words.en: Mortality refers to the state of being subject to death or the number of deaths in a particular population or period.

words.tr: v. 使残废；使残缺不全；毁伤
words.ex: The accident mutilated his hand.
words.ex_cn: 事故使他的手残废了。
words.en: To mutilate something or someone means to damage them severely, for example by cutting off or destroying part of them.

words.ex: The baby's neural connections are developing fast.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿的神经连接正在迅速发展。
words.en: Neural relates to a nerve or the nervous system.

words.tr: n. 神经症；神经衰弱症
words.ex: He has a neurosis about being late.
words.ex_cn: 他对迟到有一种神经症般的焦虑。
words.en: A neurosis is a mental illness that causes feelings of fear and worry, often leading to unreasonable behavior.

words.tr:
adj. 神经（官能）症的；神经质的；神经过敏的
n. 神经官能症患者；神经质者；神经过敏者
words.ex: She had a neurotic fear of flying.
words.ex_cn: 她对飞行有一种神经质的恐惧。
words.en: If you say that someone is neurotic, you mean that they are always worried or anxious about things that you consider unimportant.

words.ex: Mother's milk nourishes the baby.
words.ex_cn: 母乳滋养婴儿。
words.en: To nourish someone or something means to provide them with the food and other substances they need in order to live, grow, and be healthy.

words.tr:
adj. 麻木的；失去知觉的
v. 使麻木；使迟钝
words.ex: His fingers felt numb after being in the cold.
words.ex_cn: 他的手指在寒冷中变得麻木。
words.en: If a part of your body is numb, you cannot feel it, usually for a short time.

words.ex: Vegetables are rich in nutrient.
words.ex_cn: 蔬菜富含营养物。
words.en: A nutrient is a substance that is essential for life and growth, such as the vitamins and minerals in food.

words.ex: He is obese because he eats too much junk food.
words.ex_cn: 他因为吃太多垃圾食品而肥胖。
words.en: If someone is obese, they are extremely fat.

words.ex: Obesity is a serious health problem in many countries.
words.ex_cn: 肥胖是许多国家的一个严重健康问题。
words.en: Obesity is a medical condition in which excess body fat has accumulated to the extent that it may have a negative effect on health.

words.ex: It is obvious that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is obvious, it is easy to see or understand.

words.ex: He thinks this new pill is a panacea for all diseases.
words.ex_cn: 他认为这种新药是治百病的万应药。
words.en: A panacea is a remedy for all diseases or ills.

words.tr:
v. 喘气；喘息
n. 气喘；喘息
words.ex: He panted after running up the stairs.
words.ex_cn: 他跑上楼梯后喘着气。
words.en: To breathe quickly and loudly through your mouth, usually because you have been doing something energetic.

words.ex: The accident caused paralysis in his legs.
words.ex_cn: 这次事故导致他双腿瘫痪。
words.en: Paralysis is the loss of the ability to move and sometimes to feel anything in part or most of the body, typically as a result of illness, poison, or injury.

words.tr:
adj. 瘫痪的；麻痹的；烂醉的
n. 瘫痪病人；麻痹患者
words.ex: The accident left him paralytic.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故使他瘫痪了。
words.en: A paralytic is someone who is unable to move or control part or all of their body because of injury or illness.

words.tr: adj. 身体的；物质的；物理的；外观的；
words.ex: He has a physical injury from the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在这次事故中受了身体上的伤。
words.en: Relating to the body as opposed to the mind; relating to things that can be seen or touched, as opposed to things that are abstract or imaginary.

words.ex: He stayed in quarantine for 14 days.
words.ex_cn: 他隔离了14天。
words.en: A quarantine is a period of time during which an animal or person that might have a disease is kept away from other people or animals so that the disease cannot spread.

words.tr: adj. 泛滥的；猖獗的；蔓生的
words.ex: Rumors are rampant in the small town.
words.ex_cn: 谣言在这个小镇上四处流传。
words.en: If you describe something bad, such as a crime or disease, as rampant, you mean that it is very common and is increasing in an uncontrolled way.

words.tr: n. 再发；重陷；故态复萌；
words.ex: He had a relapse after stopping his medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他停药后病情复发了。
words.en: If someone relapses, they return to a less advanced state, or to a previous way of behaving that they wanted to change.

words.ex: Drugs can relieve pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To relieve someone or something means to make a problem, pain, or unpleasant feeling less severe or to take it away completely.

words.ex: The rupture in the pipe caused a flood.
words.ex_cn: 管道的破裂导致了洪水。
words.en: A rupture is a severe injury in which an internal part of your body tears or bursts open, or the act of breaking or bursting something.

words.ex: The kitchen must be sanitary to prevent illness.
words.ex_cn: 厨房必须保持清洁以防止疾病。
words.en: relating to the conditions that affect hygiene and health, especially the supply of sewage facilities and clean drinking water

words.tr:
n. 肌腱；力量的来源
v. 给…以力量
words.ex: The sinew held the muscle to the bone.
words.ex_cn: 肌腱将肌肉连接到骨头。
words.en: A sinew is a tendon, the strong tissue that connects muscles to bones, or it can refer to the strength and energy that makes someone able to do something difficult.

words.tr: n. 痉挛；抽搐；一阵发作
words.ex: He had a spasm in his leg.
words.ex_cn: 他的腿抽筋了。
words.en: A spasm is a sudden and involuntary contraction of a muscle or group of muscles, often causing pain or discomfort.

words.tr:
n. 刺；戳
v. 刺；戳
words.ex: He felt a sharp stab in his side.
words.ex_cn: 他感到侧腹一阵刺痛。
words.en: If someone stabs you, they push a knife or sharp object into your body.

words.ex: She will sterilize the bottles before use.
words.ex_cn: 她将在使用前消毒瓶子。
words.en: To sterilize something means to make it completely clean and free from bacteria.

words.tr:
n. 压力；（动植物的）品种；
v. 竭力；
words.ex: The job gave him a lot of strain.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作给他带来了很大的压力。
words.en: To strain means to make a great effort to do something, to pull or stretch something tightly, or to injure a muscle by stretching it too much.

words.ex: Children are susceptible to colds.
words.ex_cn: 孩子容易感冒。
words.en: If you are susceptible to something or someone, you are very likely to be influenced by them.

words.ex: He has a high fever as a symptom of the flu.
words.ex_cn: 他发烧是流感的症状。
words.en: A symptom is a physical or mental feature which is regarded as indicating a condition of disease, particularly such a feature that is apparent to the patient.

words.ex: Children tend to be more active in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 孩子往往在早上更活跃。
words.en: If someone tends to do something, they usually do it or they often do it.

words.ex: There is a tendency for people to use phones before bed.
words.ex_cn: 人们在睡觉前使用手机是一种趋势。
words.en: A tendency is a likelihood of behaving in a particular way or going in a particular direction, which is often bad or undesirable.

words.tr:
v. 跳动；悸动；颤动
n. 跳动；搏动；悸动
words.ex: His heart throbbed with fear.
words.ex_cn: 他的心脏因恐惧而跳动。
words.en: If part of your body throbs, you feel a series of strong and usually painful beats there.

words.ex: The doctor will transfuse blood to the patient.
words.ex_cn: 医生将给病人输血。
words.en: To transfer (as a fluid) into a vein or an artery of a person or animal; to instill or communicate gradually.

words.tr:
v. 移栽；移植；
n. 移植；
words.ex: He will transplant the flowers to the garden tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天要把这些花移栽到花园里。
words.en: To transplant something means to move it from one place to another. In medicine, to transplant an organ, piece of skin, etc. means to use it to replace a damaged part in someone's body.

words.ex: He twitched the rope to pull the box closer.
words.ex_cn: 他猛地一拉绳子，把箱子拉近了些。
words.en: To make a sudden, small movement with a part of your body, especially because you are nervous or in pain.

chapters.name: 多彩生活 健康医疗 认知词

words.ex: He felt pain in his abdominal area.
words.ex_cn: 他感到腹部疼痛。
words.en: Relating to the abdomen.

words.tr: abbr. 艾滋病；获得性免疫缺乏综合症；“Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome”的缩写；
words.ex: He got tested for aids last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周做了艾滋病检测。
words.en: AIDS is a disease caused by a virus that weakens a person's immune system, making them vulnerable to other infections and diseases.

words.tr: adj. 处境困难的； v. “ail”的现在分词；
words.ex: The ailing business needs help to survive.
words.ex_cn: 这家处境困难的公司需要帮助才能生存。
words.en: If someone is ailing, they are ill and are not getting better.

words.ex: He had a minor ailment and stayed home from work.
words.ex_cn: 他得了一点小病，没去上班。
words.en: An ailment is a minor illness or health problem.

words.ex: He went to a clinic to treat his alcoholism.
words.ex_cn: 他去诊所治疗自己的酒精中毒。
words.en: Alcoholism is the condition of being addicted to alcohol.

words.ex: He has an allergy to peanuts.
words.ex_cn: 他对花生过敏。
words.en: An allergy is a condition in which your immune system reacts abnormally to a foreign substance.

words.ex: He has amnesia and cannot remember his name.
words.ex_cn: 他患有失忆症，想不起自己的名字。
words.en: Amnesia is a medical condition that affects someone's memory and they are unable to remember events or information.

words.ex: He feels tired because of anaemia.
words.ex_cn: 他因为贫血而感到疲倦。
words.en: A condition in which there is a deficiency of red cells or of haemoglobin in the blood, resulting in pallor and weariness.

words.ex: The doctor gave him anesthesia before the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 医生在手术前给他打了麻醉。
words.en: Anesthesia is the use of drugs to prevent pain during surgery or other medical procedures.

words.ex: The patient felt no pain because of the anaesthesia.
words.ex_cn: 由于麻醉，病人没有感到疼痛。
words.en: Anaesthesia is the use of drugs to prevent pain during medical procedures.

words.tr:
n. 麻醉剂；麻醉药
adj. 麻醉的
words.ex: The doctor gave him an anesthetic before the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 医生在手术前给他用了麻醉剂。
words.en: An anesthetic is a substance that causes loss of sensation or consciousness, used especially to prevent pain during medical procedures.

words.tr:
n. 麻醉剂；麻醉药
adj. 麻醉的
words.ex: The doctor gave her an anaesthetic before the operation.
words.ex_cn: 医生在手术前给她打了麻醉剂。
words.en: A substance that causes insensitivity to pain, used especially in surgery.

words.ex: The doctor will anesthetize the patient before the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 医生将在手术前给病人麻醉。
words.en: To anesthetize someone means to make them unconscious or unable to feel pain, typically by administering a drug.

words.ex: The doctor will anaesthetize the patient before the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 医生将在手术前让病人麻醉。
words.en: To anaesthetize someone means to make them unconscious or unable to feel pain, especially by giving them an anaesthetic before a medical operation.

words.ex: He had an anal infection after the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 手术后他出现了肛门感染。
words.en: Relating to the anus or the region of the body near the anus.

words.ex: The doctor gave me an antibiotic for my infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了抗菌素治疗感染。
words.en: A substance that can kill or inhibit the growth of bacteria and other microorganisms.

words.ex: The body makes an antibody to fight the virus.
words.ex_cn: 身体产生一种抗体来对抗病毒。
words.en: An antibody is a protein produced by the body's immune system when it detects harmful substances, called antigens. Each type of antibody is unique and defends the body against one specific type of antigen.

words.ex: The doctor gave him an antidote for the poison.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他一种解毒剂来对抗毒药。
words.en: An antidote is a substance that counteracts the effects of poison or something harmful.

words.ex: The doctor used antiseptic cream on the cut.
words.ex_cn: 医生在伤口上用了防腐药膏。
words.en: An antiseptic is a substance that prevents the growth of disease-causing microorganisms.

words.ex: The doctor checked the anus for signs of infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了肛门是否有感染的迹象。
words.en: The opening at the end of the digestive tract through which solid waste leaves the body.

words.ex: He suffered apoplexy after a sudden anger.
words.ex_cn: 他突然发怒后中风了。
words.en: A medical condition in which there is a loss of consciousness and control of the body, caused by bleeding in the brain or a blood clot in the brain.

words.ex: He has appendicitis and needs surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他得了阑尾炎，需要手术。
words.en: Appendicitis is a medical condition in which the appendix becomes inflamed and painful, often requiring surgery to remove the appendix.

words.ex: The appendix contains extra data for the report.
words.ex_cn: 附录包含了报告的额外数据。
words.en: An appendix is a section at the end of a book that contains additional information. It can also refer to the small tube attached to the large intestine in the human body, known as the vermiform appendix.

words.ex: He has arthritis in his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他双手有关节炎。
words.en: Arthritis is a medical condition in which the joints in someone's body are swollen and painful.

words.ex: He has asthma and cannot run fast.
words.ex_cn: 他有哮喘，不能跑快。
words.en: A respiratory condition marked by spasms in the bronchi of the lungs, causing difficulty in breathing. It usually results from an allergic reaction or other forms of hypersensitivity.

words.ex: He passed the aural test by listening carefully.
words.ex_cn: 他通过仔细听通过了听力测试。
words.en: Relating to the ear or the sense of hearing.

words.ex: The dog ran to the backside of the house.
words.ex_cn: 狗跑到房子的后方。
words.en: The backside of something is the part of it that is furthest from the front.

words.ex: Bacteria can make you sick.
words.ex_cn: 细菌会让你生病。
words.en: Bacteria are very small organisms. Some bacteria can cause diseases.

words.ex: She applied a soothing balm to the wound.
words.ex_cn: 她在伤口上涂了镇痛软膏。
words.en: A balm is a preparation that soothes, heals, or comforts, often applied to the skin.

words.tr:
n. 绷带
v. 用绷带包扎
words.ex: He put a bandage on his cut finger.
words.ex_cn: 他在他割伤的手指上贴了绷带。
words.en: A bandage is a piece of material used to cover a wound or to support an injured part of the body.

words.tr: v. 击败；敲打；“beat”的现在分词； n. 打；打败；
words.ex: Our team was beating the rivals in the final match.
words.ex_cn: 我们的队伍在决赛中击败了对手。
words.en: The act of hitting someone or something repeatedly, or a defeat in a game or competition.

words.ex: He feels sick because of too much bile.
words.ex_cn: 他因为胆汁过多而感到恶心。
words.en: Bile is a bitter, yellow-green fluid that is produced by the liver and helps in the digestion of fats.

words.ex: He has bronchitis and can't stop coughing.
words.ex_cn: 他得了支气管炎，一直止不住咳嗽。
words.en: Bronchitis is an illness in which the bronchial tubes become inflamed and produce a lot of mucus, causing coughing and difficulty in breathing.

words.ex: Milk has a lot of calcium.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶含有大量的钙。
words.en: A chemical element that is present in teeth and bones and is necessary for their health.

words.tr:
n. 毛细血管
adj. 毛细管的；毛细作用的
words.ex: Blood moves through tiny capillary tubes.
words.ex_cn: 血液通过微小的毛细管流动。
words.en: A capillary is a very small blood vessel in the body that connects arteries and veins and allows the exchange of oxygen and nutrients between blood and tissues.

words.ex: He took a capsule for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一粒胶囊来缓解头痛。
words.en: A capsule is a small container or case, especially one that is sealed and contains a dose of medicine, or a spacecraft's compartment for astronauts.

words.ex: The cardiac patient needs to rest daily.
words.ex_cn: 这位心脏病人需要每天休息。
words.en: Cardiac means relating to the heart.

words.tr: adj. 肉体的；肉欲的；性欲的
words.ex: He denied any carnal desires.
words.ex_cn: 他否认有任何肉体的欲望。
words.en: Carnal is used to describe things relating to the body or to sexual desires, often in contrast to spiritual or intellectual matters.

words.ex: The cerebral cortex controls thinking and memory.
words.ex_cn: 大脑皮层控制思考和记忆。
words.en: Relating to the brain or the intellect.

words.ex: He got cholera from dirty water.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了脏水染上了霍乱。
words.en: Cholera is an infectious and often fatal bacterial disease of the small intestine, typically contracted from infected water supplies and causing severe vomiting and diarrhea.

words.ex: He eats eggs but watches his cholesterol.
words.ex_cn: 他吃鸡蛋，但注意自己的胆固醇。
words.en: Cholesterol is a substance that exists in the cells of the body and in blood, which can cause heart disease if there is too much of it.

words.ex: He feels panic in small rooms because of claustrophobia.
words.ex_cn: 他因为幽闭恐惧症在小房间里感到恐慌。
words.en: A morbid fear of being closed in a confined space.

words.tr:
n. 凝块；泥团；密集的一群
v. 凝结成块
words.ex: The blood began to clot after the cut.
words.ex_cn: 伤口流血后开始凝固。
words.en: A clot is a sticky lump that forms when blood dries up or becomes thick. If blood clots, it becomes thick and forms a lump.

words.ex: She wrote: 'I love reading.'
words.ex_cn: 她写道：‘我喜欢阅读。’
words.en: A colon is a punctuation mark consisting of two equally sized dots centered on the same vertical line. It is also used to refer to the part of the large intestine that extends from the cecum to the rectum.

words.ex: He bought a condom at the store.
words.ex_cn: 他在商店买了一个安全套。
words.en: A condom is a thin rubber sheath worn on a man's penis during sexual intercourse as a contraceptive or as a protection against infection.

words.tr: adj. 先天的；天生的；生性的
words.ex: He was born with a congenital heart problem.
words.ex_cn: 他出生时就有先天性心脏病。
words.en: A congenital disease or condition exists at or from birth.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The flu is contagious and spreads easily.
words.ex_cn: 流感具有传染性，容易传播。
words.en: A contagious disease can be caught by touching someone who has the disease or by touching an infected object or by breathing in infected air.

words.ex: The continuity of the story made it easy to follow.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的连续性让它容易理解。
words.en: Continuity is the fact that something continues to happen or exist, with no great changes or interruptions.

words.ex: He uses contraception to avoid having a baby.
words.ex_cn: 他使用避孕措施来避免怀孕。
words.en: Contraception is the use of methods or devices to prevent pregnancy.

words.tr:
n. 避孕药；避孕用具
adj. 避孕的
words.ex: She uses a contraceptive to avoid pregnancy.
words.ex_cn: 她使用避孕药来避免怀孕。
words.en: A contraceptive is a device or drug used to prevent pregnancy.

words.ex: The illness debilitates him every winter.
words.ex_cn: 每年冬天，这场疾病都会使他虚弱。
words.en: To make someone weak and infirm.

words.ex: He went to the dental clinic for a check-up.
words.ex_cn: 他去牙科诊所做检查。
words.en: Relating to the teeth or to the work of a dentist.

words.ex: He has diabetes and must check his blood every day.
words.ex_cn: 他患有糖尿病，必须每天检查血糖。
words.en: A medical condition in which the body cannot produce enough insulin or cannot use insulin properly, leading to high levels of sugar in the blood.

words.ex: The doctor made a diagnosis after checking the symptoms.
words.ex_cn: 医生在检查了症状后做出了诊断。
words.en: The identification of the nature of an illness or other problem by examination of the symptoms.

words.ex: He had diarrhea after eating bad food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了坏食物后得了腹泻。
words.en: A condition in which feces are discharged from the bowels frequently and in a liquid form.

words.ex: He had diarrhoea after eating bad food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了坏食物后得了腹泻。
words.en: Diarrhoea is an illness in which the body's solid waste is more liquid than usual and comes out of the body more often.

words.tr: adj. 易消化的；易理解的
words.ex: The food is easy and digestible.
words.ex_cn: 这种食物容易消化。
words.en: Capable of being digested; easily digested.

words.ex: The digestive system breaks down food.
words.ex_cn: 消化系统分解食物。
words.en: Relating to the process of digesting food.

words.ex: He uses disinfectant to clean the bathroom.
words.ex_cn: 他用消毒剂清洁浴室。
words.en: A disinfectant is a chemical substance that is used to kill harmful bacteria and viruses.

words.tr: n. （学校、兵营或工厂的）医务室；药房
words.ex: The workers go to the dispensary when they feel sick.
words.ex_cn: 工人感到不舒服时去医务室。
words.en: A dispensary is a place where medicines are prepared and given out, especially in a hospital or clinic.

words.tr:
n. 麻醉剂；毒品；内幕消息；笨蛋
v. 给…用兴奋剂（或麻醉剂）；掺杂
words.ex: He was arrested for selling dope on the street.
words.ex_cn: 他因在街上贩卖麻醉剂而被逮捕。
words.en: Dope can refer to a drug that is illegal or a piece of information that is not generally known.

words.ex: The doctor adjusted the dosage of the medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生调整了药物的剂量。
words.en: The amount of a medicine or drug that is taken at one time or over a period of time.

words.ex: He has eczema on his arms.
words.ex_cn: 他的胳膊上有湿疹。
words.en: A condition in which patches of skin become rough and inflamed, with blisters that cause itching and bleeding.

words.ex: He asked for euthanasia because he was in great pain.
words.ex_cn: 他因为痛苦不堪而要求安乐死。
words.en: Euthanasia is the practice of ending the life of a person or animal in a painless or minimally painful way, usually to relieve suffering from an incurable condition or disease.

words.ex: Smoking can exacerbate asthma.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会使哮喘加重。
words.en: If something exacerbates a problem or bad situation, it makes it worse.

words.ex: The extraction of coal harms the environment.
words.ex_cn: 煤炭的开采对环境有害。
words.en: The process of removing or obtaining something from something else.

words.ex: He put some eyewash in his eyes to relieve the irritation.
words.ex_cn: 他滴了一些眼药水来缓解眼睛的刺激。
words.en: If you describe something that someone says as eyewash, you mean that it is not true or is intended to deceive people.

words.ex: The car accident caused one fatality.
words.ex_cn: 这场车祸导致一人死亡。
words.en: A fatality is a death caused by an accident or by violence, or is the fact of causing death.

words.ex: The fetus is growing inside the mother's womb.
words.ex_cn: 胎儿正在母亲的子宫内成长。
words.en: An unborn or unhatched offspring of a mammal, in particular an unborn human more than eight weeks after conception.

words.tr: adj. 松弛的；软弱的；无活力的
words.ex: The leaves looked flaccid after the long dry spell.
words.ex_cn: 长时间干旱后，树叶看起来软弱无力。
words.en: Lacking firmness, resilience, or muscle tone; soft and limp.

words.tr:
n. 侧面；侧翼；胁腹
v. 在…侧面（有）
words.ex: The soldiers moved to the flank to avoid the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们移动到侧翼以避开敌人。
words.en: The side of something, especially a part of the body between the ribs and the hip; to be situated on each side of or on one side of (something).

words.ex: He got frostbite on his fingers after playing in the snow too long.
words.ex_cn: 他在雪地里玩太久，手指冻伤了。
words.en: Frostbite is an injury caused by freezing of the skin and underlying tissues.

words.ex: He has a gastric pain after eating spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完辛辣食物后胃痛。
words.en: Gastric means relating to the stomach.

words.ex: He has gastritis from eating too much spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他因为吃太多辛辣食物得了胃炎。
words.en: Inflammation of the lining of the stomach.

words.ex: He was diagnosed with gonorrhea last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周被诊断出患有淋病。
words.en: Gonorrhea is a sexually transmitted disease caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae. It can infect the genital tract, mouth, or anus.

words.ex: He had a hallucination after taking the medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他服药后出现了幻觉。
words.en: A hallucination is a perception in the absence of external stimulus that has qualities of real perception. Hallucinations are vivid, substantial, and are perceived to be located in external objective space.

words.ex: He had a bad hangover after drinking too much beer.
words.ex_cn: 他喝太多啤酒后得了严重的宿醉。
words.en: A hangover is the unpleasant physical condition following the consumption of alcohol, characterized by headache and nausea.

words.ex: The child was born with a harelip.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子出生时患有唇裂。
words.en: A congenital deformity characterized by a cleft or split in the upper lip, resembling that of a hare.

words.ex: He got heatstroke from working in the sun all day.
words.ex_cn: 他因在阳光下工作一整天而中暑。
words.en: Heatstroke is a condition caused by your body overheating, usually as a result of prolonged exposure to or physical exertion in high temperatures.

words.ex: Hemophilia is a genetic disorder that impairs the body's ability to make blood clots.
words.ex_cn: 血友病是一种遗传性疾病，会损害身体形成血块的能力。
words.en: A hereditary disorder where the blood does not clot properly, leading to excessive bleeding.

words.tr:
n. 体内大出血；严重流失
v. 体内大出血；（使）严重流失
words.ex: The patient suffered a severe hemorrhage after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 病人在事故后发生了严重的出血。
words.en: A hemorrhage is a severe loss of blood from a burst blood vessel, either inside or outside the body.

words.ex: He has a hemorrhoid and feels pain when he sits.
words.ex_cn: 他有痔疮，坐着时感到疼痛。
words.en: A hemorrhoid is a swollen vein or group of veins in the region of the anus.

words.ex: He has hepatitis and needs to rest.
words.ex_cn: 他患有肝炎，需要休息。
words.en: Hepatitis is an inflammation of the liver, often caused by a viral infection.

words.ex: He had a loud hiccup during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议期间打了个响亮的嗝。
words.en: A hiccup is an involuntary spasm of the diaphragm and respiratory organs, with a sudden closure of the glottis and a characteristic sound.

words.tr:
n. 打嗝
