words.en: A regulation is an official rule or order.

words.ex: The respondent answered all the questions honestly.
words.ex_cn: 这位调查对象诚实地回答了所有问题。
words.en: A respondent is someone who replies to something such as a survey or set of questions.

words.ex: The rules are too restrictive.
words.ex_cn: 这些规则太严格了。
words.en: Something that is restrictive prevents people from doing what they want to do, or from moving or acting freely.

words.tr: n. 保持器；保留金；家仆
words.ex: The dentist gave me a retainer to wear at night.
words.ex_cn: 牙医给了我一个保持器，让我晚上戴着。
words.en: A retainer is a fee that you pay to someone in order to make sure that they will be available to do work for you when you need them to.

words.tr: adj. 回顾的；回想的；溯及既往的
words.ex: He made a retrospective look at his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他回顾了自己的童年。
words.en: A retrospective is an exhibition or compilation showing the development of an artist's work over a period of time. It can also refer to a look back at past events or situations.

words.tr: adj. 公正的；正当的；正义的
words.ex: He is a righteous man who helps the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个帮助穷人的正直的人。
words.en: If you think that someone behaves or lives in a way that is morally good, you can say that they are righteous.

words.ex: The ruffian shouted at the old man.
words.ex_cn: 那个恶棍对老人大喊大叫。
words.en: A ruffian is a violent, lawless person.

words.tr: n. 蓄意破坏者；破坏分子
words.ex: The saboteur tried to disrupt the operation by cutting the power lines.
words.ex_cn: 破坏者试图通过切断电源线来破坏运营。
words.en: A saboteur is a person who deliberately destroys or damages something, especially for political or military advantage.

words.tr: n. 野蛮行为；暴行；未开化
words.ex: The savagery of the attack shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这次攻击的凶猛程度震惊了所有人。
words.en: Savagery refers to the quality of being fierce or cruel, often used to describe violent and brutal actions or behaviors.

words.ex: The workers are climbing the scaffold to paint the building.
words.ex_cn: 工人们正在爬脚手架去粉刷大楼。
words.en: A scaffold is a temporary structure erected to support workers and materials during the construction, repair, or cleaning of a building or other large structure. It can also refer to a raised wooden platform used formerly for the public execution of criminals.

words.ex: The movie shows the seduction of a young man by a clever woman.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一位聪明女性对年轻男子的诱惑。
words.en: Seduction is the act of persuading someone to do something, especially something wrong or unwise, by being attractive or offering pleasure.

words.tr:
n. 假象；假冒者；冒牌货
adj. 虚假的
v. 假装
words.ex: The gift was a sham, not real.
words.ex_cn: 这份礼物是假的，不是真的。
words.en: A sham is something that is not what it appears to be and is intended to deceive people.

words.tr: v. 上海（中国城市）；诱骗（某人）做某事；
words.ex: They shanghai the tourists to visit the Bund.
words.ex_cn: 他们带游客去参观外滩。
words.en: To shanghai someone means to trick or force them into doing something they do not want to do, especially to make them join a ship's crew.

words.ex: The article contained slanderous remarks about the company.
words.ex_cn: 这篇文章包含了对公司的诽谤性评论。
words.en: If something is slanderous, it falsely harms someone's reputation by saying something bad about them that is not true.

words.ex: He hired a solicitor to help with his house sale.
words.ex_cn: 他聘请了一名事务律师来帮助处理他的房屋出售。
words.en: A solicitor is a lawyer who gives legal advice and prepares legal documents, especially in England.

words.ex: The statute says drivers must stop at red lights.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律规定司机必须在红灯时停车。
words.en: A statute is a formal written law of a country or state, enacted by its legislative authority.

words.tr: adj. 法定的；依照法规的；
words.ex: The statutory minimum wage is $10 per hour.
words.ex_cn: 法定最低工资是每小时10美元。
words.en: Statutory means relating to rules or laws which have been formally written down.

words.ex: The school has stringent rules about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学校对作业有严格的规定。
words.en: Stringent measures, rules, or conditions are very strict or severe.

words.ex: The police used surveillance to watch the building.
words.ex_cn: 警察使用监视来观察那栋大楼。
words.en: The careful watching of a person or place, especially by the police or army, because of a crime that has happened or is expected.

words.ex: The will of the testator was contested by his heirs.
words.ex_cn: 立遗嘱者的遗嘱被他的继承人质疑。
words.en: A person who has made a will or given a testament.

words.ex: The thug stole the wallet from the man.
words.ex_cn: 那个恶棍从那人身上偷了钱包。
words.en: A thug is a violent person, especially a criminal.

words.ex: The doctor ran a trial to test the new medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生进行了试验来测试这种新药。
words.en: A trial is a formal meeting in a law court, at which a judge and jury listen to evidence and decide whether a person is guilty of a crime.

words.ex: He learned piano under his teacher's tutelage.
words.ex_cn: 他在老师的指导下学习钢琴。
words.en: The act of guarding, protecting, or guiding; the office or function of a guardian; guardianship; protection; as, the king's right of seigniory and tutelage.

words.ex: He gave an ultimatum: leave now or stay forever.
words.ex_cn: 他发出最后通牒：现在走，或者永远留下。
words.en: An ultimatum is a final demand or statement of terms, the rejection of which will result in retaliation or a breakdown in relations.

words.ex: The vandal defaced the monument with graffiti.
words.ex_cn: 那个破坏公物的人用涂鸦污损了纪念碑。
words.en: A vandal is someone who deliberately destroys or damages property belonging to others.

words.tr: n. 恣意毁坏他人财产罪
words.ex: The boys did vandalism by breaking the windows.
words.ex_cn: 那些男孩通过砸坏窗户实施了破坏行为。
words.en: The crime of deliberately damaging or destroying public or private property.

chapters.name: 全球风云 社会生活 重点词

words.tr: v. 使不抱幻想；使不再着迷；使醒悟
words.ex: The truth disenchant him about his hero.
words.ex_cn: 真相让他对他的偶像不再抱有幻想。
words.en: If you are disenchanted with something, you are disappointed with it and no longer believe that it is good or worthwhile.

words.tr: v. 解开；解脱；解决（纠纷等）
words.ex: He tried to disentangle the tangled wires.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把缠在一起的电线解开。
words.en: To free something or someone from being tangled or twisted, or to separate things that are twisted together.

words.tr: n. 意见分歧；纠纷；争执
words.ex: The team had dissension about the new plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队对新计划有分歧。
words.en: Disagreement among people or groups, especially when it leads to conflict.

words.ex: He tried to dissuade her from quitting her job.
words.ex_cn: 他试图劝她不要辞掉工作。
words.en: If you dissuade someone from doing something, you persuade them not to do it.

words.ex: The two roads diverge after the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 两条路在桥后分岔。
words.en: If one thing diverges from another similar thing, the first thing becomes different from the second or develops differently from it. You can also say that two things diverge.

words.tr: v. 体现；使具体化；包含
words.ex: He embodies kindness and patience.
words.ex_cn: 他体现了善良和耐心。
words.en: To embody means to represent a quality or an idea exactly; to include or contain something.

words.tr: v. 使卷入；使陷入；牵连
words.ex: He didn't want to embroil his friend in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他不想让朋友卷入这场争吵。
words.en: To involve someone in a difficult or complicated situation.

words.tr:
v. 遭遇；遇到；邂逅；
n. 遭遇；
words.ex: He encountered a bear while hiking in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他在森林里徒步时遭遇了一只熊。
words.en: If you encounter problems or difficulties, you experience them.

words.ex: He is encumbered by too many debts.
words.ex_cn: 他被太多的债务拖累。
words.en: To encumber someone or something means to weigh them down or to block or hinder them.

words.ex: Exercise can enhance your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提高你的健康。
words.en: To enhance something means to improve its value, quality, or attractiveness.

words.ex: The new job enriched his life.
words.ex_cn: 这份新工作使他的生活富裕起来。
words.en: To enrich something means to improve its quality, often by adding something to it.

words.ex: The cat got entangled in the string.
words.ex_cn: 猫被绳子缠住了。
words.en: If something is entangled in something else, it is caught or twisted around it, or mixed with it so that it is difficult to separate the two things.

words.ex: He entreats his friend to help him.
words.ex_cn: 他恳求朋友帮助他。
words.en: To ask someone earnestly or anxiously to do something.

words.ex: The song evokes happy memories of childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌唤起了对童年的美好回忆。
words.en: To evoke a particular memory, idea, emotion, or response means to cause it to occur.

words.ex: The teacher exhorts students to study hard.
words.ex_cn: 老师敦促学生努力学习。
words.en: To strongly encourage or try to persuade someone to do something.

words.tr:
v. 调情；轻率地对待
n. 与多人调情的人
words.ex: He flirts with her at the coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他在咖啡店向她调情。
words.en: If you flirt with someone, you behave as if you are sexually attracted to them, in a playful or not very serious way.

words.ex: He will not forsake his family.
words.ex_cn: 他不会抛弃他的家人。
words.en: If you forsake someone, you leave them when you should have stayed, or you stop helping them or looking after them.

words.ex: The puppy frisks around the garden.
words.ex_cn: 小狗在花园里活蹦乱跳。
words.en: To frisk someone means to search them for weapons or illegal items by feeling their body with your hands.

words.ex: He is grappled with the math problem for hours.
words.ex_cn: 他花了好几个小时努力解决这道数学题。
words.en: To grapple with something means to try hard to understand or deal with a difficult problem or subject.

words.tr:
v. 阻碍；妨碍
n. （带盖）篮子
words.ex: Rain hampered our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨妨碍了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If something hampers you, it makes it difficult for you to do something.

words.tr:
n. 麻烦；困难；争吵
v. 烦扰；纠缠
words.ex: It's not worth the hassle to change your plans.
words.ex_cn: 改变计划不值得这么麻烦。
words.en: If you describe something as a hassle, you mean that it is inconvenient and annoying. As a verb, to hassle someone means to annoy or trouble them persistently.

words.ex: The crowd began to heckle the speaker during the debate.
words.ex_cn: 在辩论期间，观众开始嘲笑那位演讲者。
words.en: To heckle someone means to interrupt them while they are speaking, especially in a public situation, by shouting out questions or comments, often in order to challenge or embarrass them.

words.ex: The hubbub in the market made it hard to think.
words.ex_cn: 市场里的喧闹让人难以集中思想。
words.en: A hubbub is a loud, confused noise, especially one caused by a large crowd of people.

words.tr:
v. 挤作一团
n. 挤作一团
words.ex: The team huddled together to plan their next move.
words.ex_cn: 团队聚在一起规划下一步行动。
words.en: If people huddle together, they stand, sit, or lie close to each other because they are cold or frightened.

words.ex: The injury impaired his ability to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤损害了他走路的能力。
words.en: If something impairs something such as an ability or the way something works, it damages it or makes it worse.

words.ex: Smoking can imperil your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会危及你的健康。
words.en: To put someone or something at risk of being harmed, damaged, or destroyed.

words.ex: She implored him to stay.
words.ex_cn: 她恳求他留下。
words.en: If you implore someone to do something, you ask them to do it in a forceful, emotional way.

words.ex: The war impoverished many families.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争使许多家庭变得贫困。
words.en: To make someone poor or to reduce the quality, strength, or richness of something.

words.ex: He invoked the law to protect his rights.
words.ex_cn: 他援引法律来保护自己的权利。
words.en: If you invoke a law, rule, or principle, you refer to it as a reason or justification for something.

words.tr:
v. 挤；推；撞；争夺
n. 挤拥；推撞
words.ex: People jostle in the crowded market.
words.ex_cn: 人们在拥挤的市场里推挤。
words.en: To jostle someone means to push or knock against them, usually in a crowd.

words.ex: She tries to juggle her job and caring for her kids.
words.ex_cn: 她努力兼顾工作和照顾孩子。
words.en: If you juggle, you keep several objects in motion in the air at the same time by repeatedly throwing and catching them. Juggle can also mean to deal with several things at the same time, often in a skillful way.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使杂乱
n. 杂乱；混乱
words.ex: He jumbled the letters and could not read the word.
words.ex_cn: 他把字母弄乱了，无法认出这个单词。
words.en: To mix things together in a confused or untidy way.

words.tr: v. 衰弱；凋萎；憔悴；受折磨
words.ex: The prisoner languishes in a dark cell.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯在黑暗的牢房中饱受煎熬。
words.en: If someone languishes somewhere, they are forced to remain and suffer in an unpleasant situation.

words.tr: n. 大笑；笑死我了 (used to express amusement)
words.ex: He told a funny joke and got a big lol.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了个有趣的笑话，引得大家大笑。
words.en: To laugh out loud, especially in response to something humorous.

words.ex: There was a lull in the rain before the storm came back.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨再次来临前，雨下了一阵间歇。
words.en: A lull is a short period of quiet or calm in an otherwise noisy or hectic situation. To lull means to cause someone to feel calm or to fall asleep.

words.tr:
v. 吸引；诱惑；引诱
n. 诱惑；诱饵；吸引力
words.ex: The bright colors lure the birds to the feeder.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的颜色吸引鸟类来到喂食器。
words.en: If you lure someone, you tempt them to do something or to go somewhere, especially by offering some form of reward.

words.ex: The brewery uses fresh mash to make beer.
words.ex_cn: 酿酒厂使用新鲜的麦芽浆来酿造啤酒。
words.en: To crush or smash something into a soft, pulpy mass.

words.ex: He misapprehends the simple instructions.
words.ex_cn: 他误解了简单的指示。
words.en: To misunderstand or misinterpret something or someone.

words.ex: He was arrested for molesting a child.
words.ex_cn: 他因骚扰儿童而被逮捕。
words.en: To molest someone means to assault or harass them, especially sexually.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使糊涂；胡乱应付
n. 混乱；糊涂
words.ex: He muddled the instructions and got confused.
words.ex_cn: 他把说明搞混了，感到困惑。
words.en: If you muddle things or people, you get them mixed up, so that you do not know which is which.

words.ex: He felt nostalgia when he saw his old toy.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到自己的旧玩具时，感到怀旧。
words.en: A sentimental longing or wistful affection for the past, typically for a period or place with happy personal associations.

words.tr:
v. 轻推；轻触；劝说；鼓动
n. 轻推；轻触；劝说；鼓动
words.ex: He gave me a nudge to start the project.
words.ex_cn: 他轻轻推了我一下，让我开始这个项目。
words.en: If you nudge someone, you push them gently, usually with your elbow, in order to draw their attention to something.

words.tr: v. 消灭；毁掉；清除；抹除
words.ex: The bomb will obliterate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To obliterate something means to remove all signs of it or to destroy it completely.

words.ex: He obsesses over small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他 obsesses 于微小的错误。
words.en: If something or someone obsesses you, you think or worry about them all the time and you cannot think about anything else.

words.ex: She pampered her baby with warm baths and soft blankets.
words.ex_cn: 她用温水浴和柔软的毯子细心照顾她的婴儿。
words.en: To treat someone very kindly, often too kindly, by letting them have or do whatever they want.

words.tr:
v. 偷看；窥视
n. 偷看；窥见
words.ex: He peeked through the keyhole.
words.ex_cn: 他从钥匙孔里偷看。
words.en: To peek means to look at something quickly and secretly, especially through a small opening or from behind something.

words.ex: The riddle perplexed the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个谜语让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If something perplexes you, it confuses and worries you because you do not understand it or because it causes you difficulty.

words.tr: v. 使焦虑；使不安；扰乱
words.ex: The noise perturbs the baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音让婴儿不安。
words.en: If something perturbs you, it makes you feel anxious or worried.

words.tr: v. 不断打扰；纠缠；烦扰
words.ex: The child keeps pestering his mom for candy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子不停地缠着妈妈要糖果。
words.en: If you say that someone is pestering you, you mean that they keep asking you to do something, or keep talking to you, and you find this annoying.

words.ex: He gave her a light pinch on the arm.
words.ex_cn: 他轻轻捏了她的胳膊一下。
words.en: To pinch someone or something means to squeeze them tightly between your thumb and finger, or between two surfaces, especially in a way that causes pain.

words.tr:
v. 猛扑；突袭；抓住
n. 猛扑
words.ex: The cat will pounce on the mouse.
words.ex_cn: 猫会扑向老鼠。
words.en: If someone pounces on you, they come up towards you suddenly and take hold of you.

words.tr:
v. 加速（坏事的发生）
n. 沉淀物；冷凝物
adj. 轻率的；仓促的
words.ex: The scandal precipitated the politician's resignation.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻加速了这位政治家的辞职。
words.en: To cause something to happen suddenly or unexpectedly; to cause a substance to be deposited in solid form from a solution.

words.ex: The rain precludes a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 下雨阻止了野餐。
words.en: If something precludes an event or action, it prevents it from happening.

words.ex: The school prohibits students from using phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止学生在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: If a law or someone in authority prohibits something, they forbid it or make it illegal.

words.tr: v. 熄灭；平息；抑制（欲望）；用水冷却
words.ex: He quenched the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水熄灭了火。
words.en: To satisfy one's thirst or to extinguish a fire or to suppress a feeling or desire.

words.tr:
n. 遁词；狡辩；支吾以对；争论的小问题
v. 使用遁词；含糊其辞；吹毛求疵
words.ex: His excuse was just a quibble to avoid blame.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口只是逃避责任的遁词。
words.en: To argue or raise objections about a trivial matter or minor detail.

words.tr: v. 回报；报答；往复；来回
words.ex: She helped me, and I will reciprocate.
words.ex_cn: 她帮了我，我会回报她。
words.en: If your feelings or actions towards someone are reciprocated, the other person feels or behaves in the same way towards you as you have felt or behaved towards them.

words.ex: He had no recourse but to ask for help.
words.ex_cn: 他别无依靠，只能求助。
words.en: If you have recourse to a particular course of action, you use it when you are in a difficult situation or when you need to achieve something.

words.tr:
n. 经常重复的评价（或抱怨）；叠句；
v. 克制；
words.ex: His constant refrain is that the food is too expensive.
words.ex_cn: 他经常抱怨食物太贵。
words.en: If you refrain from doing something, you deliberately do not do it.

words.ex: He reject the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这份工作邀请。
words.en: If you reject something such as a proposal, a request, or an offer, you do not accept it or you do not agree to it.

words.ex: He had to relinquish his seat to an old man.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不把座位让给一位老人。
words.en: If you relinquish something, such as power or control, you give it up, often unwillingly.

words.tr: n. 报复；报仇；报复性劫掠
words.ex: He feared reprisal after speaking out against the boss.
words.ex_cn: 他因公开反对老板而害怕遭到报复。
words.en: An act of retaliation for a wrong or injury.

words.tr: n. 归还；赔偿；恢复原状
words.ex: The court ordered restitution for the damaged property.
words.ex_cn: 法院命令对受损财产进行赔偿。
words.en: The act of restoring something to its original state or the act of compensating for loss or damage.

words.ex: The law restricts driving after drinking.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制酒后驾驶。
words.en: to limit the movements or actions of someone, or to limit something and reduce its size or prevent it from increasing

words.ex: He tried to retaliate by spreading rumors.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过散布谣言来报复。
words.en: If you retaliate when someone harms or annoys you, you do something which harms or annoys them in return.

words.ex: The sweater shrinks in hot water.
words.ex_cn: 这件毛衣在热水中会收缩。
words.en: If something shrinks or you shrink it, it becomes smaller.

words.tr:
n. 寿衣；裹尸布；覆盖物
v. 覆盖；遮蔽
words.ex: The body was wrapped in a white shroud.
words.ex_cn: 遗体被裹在一件白色的寿衣里。
words.en: A shroud is a cloth which is used for wrapping a dead body. It can also refer to something that covers, hides, or protects.

words.tr: v. “stand”的现在分词；站立； adj. 直立的；常设的； n. 地位；
words.ex: He is standing by the door.
words.ex_cn: 他正站在门边。
words.en: Your standing is your status or reputation.

words.tr:
n. 破烂的衣服；千疮百孔
n. 破布；碎纸片；“tatter”的复数
words.ex: His clothes were in tatters after the long journey.
words.ex_cn: 长途旅行后，他的衣服破烂不堪。
words.en: Pieces of cloth that are old and torn.

words.tr:
n. 琐事；少量
v. 玩弄；轻视
words.ex: He threw away a trifle of money on candy.
words.ex_cn: 他花了一点钱买糖果。
words.en: A trifle is something that is considered to have little importance, value, or significance. It can also refer to a small amount of something. As a verb, to trifle means to treat someone or something without seriousness or respect.

words.tr:
n. 流浪汉；漂泊者；乞丐
adj. 流浪的；漂泊的
words.ex: The vagrant slept on the park bench.
words.ex_cn: 那个流浪汉睡在公园的长椅上。
words.en: A vagrant is someone who moves from place to place and does not have a permanent home or job.

words.tr:
n. （男子的）贴身男仆；（洗衣或停车的）男服务员
v. （受雇）洗（车）；伺候
words.ex: The valet parked his car.
words.ex_cn: 停车场服务员停了他的车。
words.en: A valet is a man's personal male attendant, responsible for his clothes and appearance. In some contexts, it also refers to a person employed to park cars.

words.tr: adj. 复仇心重的；报复的
words.ex: He was vengeful after his friend lied to him.
words.ex_cn: 他的朋友骗了他之后，他变得报复心很强。
words.en: If you describe someone as vengeful, you are critical of them because they feel a great desire for revenge.

words.ex: He decided to waive the fee.
words.ex_cn: 他决定放弃这笔费用。
words.en: If you waive a right, claim, or privilege, you do not insist on it or do not use it.

words.tr: v. 求爱；求婚；寻求支持
words.ex: He tried to woo her with flowers and chocolates.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用鲜花和巧克力追求她。
words.en: If you woo someone, you try to persuade them to marry you or to have a relationship with you, or you try to gain their support or favor.

chapters.name: 全球风云 社会生活 认知词

words.ex: The coroner examined the body to find the cause of death.
words.ex_cn: 法医检查了尸体以确定死因。
words.en: A coroner is an official who is responsible for investigating the deaths of people who have died in a sudden, violent, or unusual way.

words.ex: His sudden win in the race was a real coup.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中突然获胜，真是了不起的成就。
words.en: A coup is a sudden, violent, and illegal seizure of power from a government.

words.tr:
n. 裂缝；噼啪声；
v. 破裂；
words.ex: There is a small crack in the wall.
words.ex_cn: 墙上有一条小裂缝。
words.en: If something hard cracks, or if you crack it, it becomes slightly damaged, with lines appearing on its surface.

words.ex: He requested that his body be cremated after death.
words.ex_cn: 他要求死后将他的遗体火化。
words.en: To cremate a dead person's body means to burn it, usually as part of a funeral ceremony.

words.ex: The crematorium is near the church.
words.ex_cn: 火葬场在教堂附近。
words.en: A crematorium is a place where the bodies of dead people are burned.

words.tr:
v. 轻拍；轻触；轻敷
n. 轻拍；少量；能手；比目鱼
words.ex: He dabbed paint on the wall with a brush.
words.ex_cn: 他用刷子在墙上点了一些颜料。
words.en: To dab means to touch something lightly and quickly, often with a cloth or your fingers, in order to clean it, dry it, or apply something to it.

words.ex: The knight saved the damsel from the dragon.
words.ex_cn: 骑士从龙手中救出了少女。
words.en: A damsel is a young, unmarried woman, often portrayed as being in need of rescue or protection.

words.tr:
n. 花花公子；好打扮的男人
adj. 服装华丽的；极好的
words.ex: He is a dandy who wears fancy clothes every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是个时髦男子，每天都穿华丽的衣服。
words.en: A dandy is a man who places particular importance upon physical appearance, refined language, and leisurely hobbies, pursued with the appearance of nonchalance in a cult of self.

words.ex: The keys dangle from his belt.
words.ex_cn: 钥匙挂在他的腰带上。
words.en: If something dangles from somewhere or if you dangle it somewhere, it hangs or swings loosely.

words.tr:
n. 死亡
v. 死；死亡
words.ex: His decease was sudden and unexpected.
words.ex_cn: 他的去世突然且意外。
words.en: The death of a person.

words.ex: His calm demeanor made everyone feel safe.
words.ex_cn: 他平静的举止让每个人都感到安心。
words.en: The way in which a person behaves towards others; outward behavior or bearing.

words.ex: His calm demeanour surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他冷静的举止让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Demeanour refers to the way in which a person behaves towards others; their outward behaviour or bearing.

words.ex: The war caused the village to depopulate.
words.ex_cn: 战争导致村庄人口减少。
words.en: To reduce the population of an area, especially by violence, disease, or lack of food.

words.ex: The dignitary gave a speech at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 这位显要人物在仪式上发表了演讲。
words.en: A dignitary is a person who has an important position in a society or an organization.

words.tr:
n. 嘈杂声；喧闹声
v. 喧闹；喋喋不休地说
words.ex: The children made a loud din in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在教室里发出很大的嘈杂声。
words.en: A din is a loud, unpleasant, and prolonged noise.

words.tr:
v. 弄乱；使混乱
n. 无秩序；混乱；衣冠不整
words.ex: The storm disarrayed the books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 风暴把书架上的书弄乱了。
words.en: a state of disorganization or untidiness

words.ex: There is a disparity in pay between men and women.
words.ex_cn: 男女之间的工资存在差异。
words.en: A disparity between two or more things is a noticeable difference between them.

words.ex: There is a dissonance between his words and actions.
words.ex_cn: 他的言行不一致。
words.en: A lack of harmony or agreement between people or things.

words.tr:
n. 施舍品；失业救济金
v. 发放救济
words.ex: The government gives dole to the unemployed.
words.ex_cn: 政府向失业者提供救济金。
words.en: Money or food given by a government to people who are poor and have no other way of getting money or food.

words.ex: The donor gave money to the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 捐赠者向医院捐了钱。
words.en: A donor is a person or organization that gives something, especially money, to a charity or other organization.

words.tr: n. 孀居贵妇；老年贵妇
words.ex: The dowager lived in a big house with gardens.
words.ex_cn: 这位寡居的贵妇住在一座带花园的大房子里。
words.en: A dowager is a woman of high social rank whose husband is dead and who has a title or property because of her marriage.

words.tr:
n. 穷困潦倒的人
adj. 穷困潦倒的；被击倒的
words.ex: He is a down-and-out man who sleeps on the street.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个睡在街头的落魄之人。
words.en: Someone who is down-and-out has no home, no job, and no money.

words.ex: Her family gave a dowry when she married.
words.ex_cn: 她结婚时，她的家人给了嫁妆。
words.en: A dowry is property or money that a woman brings to her husband when they marry.

words.ex: He drank the dregs of the coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他喝完了咖啡剩下的残渣。
words.en: The remnants of a liquid left in a container, together with any sediment or grounds.

words.ex: She wore a white pearl necklace.
words.ex_cn: 她戴着一条白色的珍珠项链。
words.en: A pearl is a hard, rounded object formed within the shell of a pearl oyster or similar mollusk, highly prized as a gemstone.

words.ex: He tried to eavesdrop on their conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他试图偷听他们的对话。
words.en: To eavesdrop means to listen secretly to other people's conversations.

words.tr: v. 擦去；忘却；不抛头露面；使（自己）不受人注意
words.ex: He tried to efface the mark with an eraser.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用橡皮擦掉那个痕迹。
words.en: To efface something means to remove it completely so that it no longer exists or is no longer noticeable.

words.tr:
v. 逝去；过去
n. （光阴）逝去
words.ex: Two hours elapsed while he waited for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他等公交车时，两个小时过去了。
words.en: If time elapses, it passes.

words.tr: v. 使成贵族；使高贵；使受尊敬
words.ex: The king will ennoble the brave soldier.
words.ex_cn: 国王将封赏这位勇敢的士兵。
words.en: To ennoble someone means to make them a member of the nobility, or to make them seem morally or socially superior.

words.tr: adj. 性欲的；性爱的；色情的
words.ex: The movie contains erotic scenes that are not suitable for children.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影包含不适合儿童的色情场景。
words.en: Relating to or tending to arouse sexual desire or excitement.

words.ex: The company follows ethical practices in hiring.
words.ex_cn: 该公司在招聘中遵循伦理规范。
words.en: Relating to moral principles or the branch of knowledge dealing with these.

words.ex: The school's ethos is respect for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校的社會精神特质是尊重每一个人。
words.en: The fundamental character or spirit of a culture; the underlying sentiment that informs the beliefs, customs, or practices of a group or society.

words.ex: He knows good etiquette at dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他知道晚餐时的礼貌规矩。
words.en: Etiquette refers to the customary code of polite behavior in society or among members of a particular profession or group.

words.ex: The footman opened the door for the guests.
words.ex_cn: 男仆为客人打开了门。
words.en: A footman is a male servant, especially one who works in a large household and who helps the butler.

words.tr:
n. 怪诞行为；
adj. 不正常的；怪异的；
words.ex: His freak of wearing socks with sandals surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他穿袜子配凉鞋的怪诞行为让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A freak is a person who is considered to be unusual because of their behaviour or interests, or a sudden and unexpected event or situation.

words.tr:
n. 花环
v. 给…戴上花环
words.ex: She put a garland on the door for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对在门上挂了一个花环。
words.en: A garland is a circular decoration made from flowers and leaves, which is worn on the head or hung up as a decoration.

words.ex: The ad used a cheap gimmick to attract customers.
words.ex_cn: 这个广告用了一个廉价的噱头来吸引顾客。
words.en: A gimmick is a trick or device intended to attract attention, publicity, or trade.

words.tr: v. 使协调一致；使和谐；配上和音
words.ex: The two singers try to harmonize their voices.
words.ex_cn: 两位歌手试图让他们的声音和谐。
words.en: If two or more things harmonize, they combine in a pleasing way, or if you harmonize them, you make them combine in a pleasing way.

words.ex: The flowers are on the headstone.
words.ex_cn: 花放在墓碑上。
words.en: A headstone is a large stone which is placed at one end of a grave, usually with the name of the dead person carved on it.

words.tr: n. 传闻；谣传；道听途说
words.ex: He believed the hearsay without checking the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他没有核实事实就相信了这些流言。
words.en: Information received from other people that one cannot adequately substantiate; rumor.

words.ex: The hearse drove slowly down the street.
words.ex_cn: 灵车缓缓驶过街道。
words.en: A hearse is a vehicle used to carry a coffin to a cemetery or crematorium.

words.ex: With hindsight, I should have saved more money.
words.ex_cn: 事后看来，我本该多存些钱。
words.en: The understanding of a situation or event only after it has happened or developed.

words.tr:
adj. 同性恋的
n. 同性恋者
words.ex: He is homosexual and loves his partner.
words.ex_cn: 他是同性恋，爱他的伴侣。
words.en: A homosexual is someone who is sexually attracted to people of the same sex.

words.ex: A horde of children ran to the ice cream truck.
words.ex_cn: 一群孩子跑向冰淇淋车。
words.en: A horde is a large group of people or animals, especially one that is moving or acting together.

words.tr: n. 人道主义； 人文主义
words.ex: He believes in humanism and values people over rules.
words.ex_cn: 他相信人文主义，重视人而非规则。
words.en: Humanism is a philosophical stance that emphasizes the value and agency of human beings, individually and collectively, and generally prefers critical thinking and evidence (rationalism, empiricism) over acceptance of dogma or superstition.

words.tr: adj. 人道主义的；慈善的；
words.ex: The humanitarian aid helped the hungry children.
words.ex_cn: 人道主义援助帮助了饥饿的孩子们。
words.en: A humanitarian is someone who is involved in or connected with improving people's lives and reducing suffering.

words.tr: n. 偶像崇拜；盲目崇拜
words.ex: He worships the pop star like idolatry.
words.ex_cn: 他像崇拜偶像一样崇拜这位流行歌手。
words.en: The worship of idols or excessive admiration for someone or something.

words.tr: v. 偶像化；过分崇拜；奉为神圣
words.ex: He idolizes his older brother.
words.ex_cn: 他崇拜他的哥哥。
words.en: If you idolize someone, you admire them very much.

words.ex: He told the story about incest in the old family.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了那个关于家族乱伦的旧事。
words.en: Incest is sexual activity between family members or close relatives.

words.tr: v. 焚化；焚毁；把…烧成灰烬
words.ex: The city will incinerate the trash tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市明天将焚烧垃圾。
words.en: To incinerate something means to burn it until it is reduced to ash.

words.tr: n. 闯入者；干涉他人事务者
words.ex: The interloper walked into the meeting without permission.
words.ex_cn: 那个闯入者未经允许走进了会议。
words.en: An interloper is someone who becomes involved in a situation or place where they are not wanted or are considered not to belong.

words.ex: The interment took place at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 葬礼在日出时举行。
words.en: The act or ceremony of burying a dead body.

words.ex: He spent the evening in introspection.
words.ex_cn: 他整个晚上都在反省。
words.en: The examination of one's own thoughts, feelings, and sensations; self-examination.

words.tr: n. 突然冲入；急速增加
words.ex: The irruption of birds scared the children.
words.ex_cn: 鸟群的突然涌入吓到了孩子们。
words.en: An irruption is a sudden, violent, or forcible entry or invasion.

words.tr: n. 万事通；杂而不精的人
words.ex: He is a jack-of-all-trades who fixes cars, cooks meals, and teaches kids.
words.ex_cn: 他是个万能的人，会修车、做饭和教孩子。
words.en: A person who can do many different types of work but who perhaps does not do any of them very well.

words.tr:
n. 女同性恋者
adj. 女同性恋的
words.ex: She is a lesbian and loves her partner.
words.ex_cn: 她是一名女同性恋者，深爱着她的伴侣。
words.en: A lesbian is a woman who is sexually attracted to other women.

words.ex: Eating healthy food helps with longevity.
words.ex_cn: 健康饮食有助于长寿。
words.en: Longevity refers to the length or duration of an individual's life, especially when it is unusually long.

words.tr: n. 巨头；大亨；大资本家
words.ex: The magnate owns many hotels and airlines.
words.ex_cn: 这位大亨拥有许多酒店和航空公司。
words.en: A magnate is a person who is very rich and powerful, especially in a particular industry.

words.tr: n. 骚动；破坏；故意的伤害罪
words.ex: The storm caused mayhem in the city.
words.ex_cn: 风暴在城市中造成了混乱。
words.en: Violent or extreme disorder; chaos.

words.ex: He believes in monogamy and stays with one partner.
words.ex_cn: 他相信一夫一妻制，并且只与一个伴侣在一起。
words.en: The practice or condition of having a single sexual partner during a period of time.

words.ex: The mortuary was filled with the bodies of the victims.
words.ex_cn: 停尸房里堆满了受害者的尸体。
words.en: A mortuary is a building or a room in a hospital where dead bodies are kept before they are buried or cremated.

words.ex: The nobility lived in large castles and owned much land.
words.ex_cn: 贵族住在大城堡里，拥有大量土地。
words.en: The quality of being noble in character, mind, birth, or rank.

words.ex: The newspaper published his obituary yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 报纸昨天刊登了他的讣告。
words.en: An obituary is a notice of a person's death, especially in a newspaper, often with a brief biography of the deceased.

words.tr: n. 孤儿；失去生母的幼小动物
words.ex: The boy lives with his uncle because he is an orphan.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩和叔叔住在一起，因为他是个孤儿。
words.en: An orphan is a child whose parents are dead.

words.ex: The boy lives in an orphanage.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩住在孤儿院。
words.en: An orphanage is a place where children who have lost their parents or who have been abandoned by them are cared for and live.

words.ex: The company received patronage from a local businessman.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司收到了一位本地商人的赞助。
words.en: The support, encouragement, privilege, or financial aid that an organization or individual bestows to another.

words.tr: v. 惠顾；资助；屈尊俯就
words.ex: He often patronizes the local bakery.
words.ex_cn: 他经常光顾这家本地面包店。
words.en: If someone patronizes you, they speak or behave towards you in a way which seems friendly, but which shows that they think they are superior to you in some way.

words.tr: n. 领取退休、养老金或抚恤金的人；
words.ex: The pensioner walks his dog every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这位领取养老金的人每天早上都遛狗。
words.en: A pensioner is someone who receives a pension, especially a retirement pension.

words.tr: n. 名人；要人；人物；角色
words.ex: The personage gave a speech at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 这位人物在仪式上发表了演讲。
words.en: A personage is a person, especially someone who is famous or important in some way.

words.tr: v. 使通俗化；宣传；推广；使普及
words.ex: He wants to popularize science among children.
words.ex_cn: 他想在儿童中普及科学。
words.en: To make something known or liked by many people.

words.ex: The two countries signed a protocol to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项停止战争的协议。
words.en: A protocol is a set of rules or a system of rules about the correct way to act in formal situations.

words.ex: He is the recipient of the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个奖项的接受者。
words.en: A recipient is a person who receives something.

words.tr: n. 弹回；反响；后果；反射
words.ex: The ball showed a clear repercussion off the wall.
words.ex_cn: 球从墙上明显地弹回。
words.en: The effect that an action, event, or decision has on something, especially a bad effect.

words.ex: He was eager to regain his lost respectability.
words.ex_cn: 他急切地想要恢复失去的名望。
words.en: The quality of being socially acceptable or respectable.

words.ex: The kids made a ruckus in the living room.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在客厅里闹出了很大的动静。
words.en: A ruckus is a noisy situation or argument.

words.tr: n. 散布骇人谣言的人；危言耸听者
words.ex: The newspaper was accused of scaremongering about the economic crisis.
words.ex_cn: 这家报纸被指控在经济危机问题上散布恐慌。
words.en: A scaremonger is a person who spreads alarming or frightening rumors, often without evidence, to cause fear or anxiety among the public.

words.ex: She scoured the pan until it was clean.
words.ex_cn: 她把锅擦得干干净净。
words.en: If you scour something, you clean it by rubbing it hard with something rough.

words.tr: adj. 感官的；肉欲的；愉悦感官的；耽于肉欲的
words.ex: The sensual smell of fresh bread made her hungry.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜面包的感官香味让她感到饥饿。
words.en: Relating to or involving gratification of the senses and physical, especially sexual, pleasure.

words.tr:
n. 墓室；冢
v. 埋葬
words.ex: The ancient sepulchre was discovered by archaeologists.
words.ex_cn: 考古学家发现了这座古老的坟墓。
words.en: A sepulchre is a tomb or burial chamber, especially one that is large and imposing.

words.ex: He was fired for showing sexism at work.
words.ex_cn: 他因在工作中表现出性别歧视而被解雇。
words.en: Sexism is the belief that the members of one sex are less intelligent, able, skillful, etc. than the members of the other sex, especially that women are less able than men.

words.tr:
n. 性别歧视者
adj. 性别歧视的
words.ex: He made a sexist comment about women drivers.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了关于女司机的性别歧视言论。
words.en: A sexist person shows prejudice or discrimination based on a person's sex, especially against women.

words.ex: The old engine spluttered and then stopped.
words.ex_cn: 那台旧引擎发出劈啪声，然后熄火了。
words.en: If someone splutters, they make short sounds and have difficulty speaking clearly, for example because they are embarrassed or angry.

words.tr:
n. 争吵
v. 争吵
words.ex: The two boys squabble over toys every day.
words.ex_cn: 这两个男孩每天为玩具争吵。
words.en: A squabble is a noisy disagreement about something unimportant.

words.ex: He dreams of stardom after winning the talent show.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得才艺比赛后梦想着成名。
words.en: The status of being a very famous or popular performer, especially in the entertainment industry.

words.tr: n. 求婚者；起诉者；有意收购另一公司的机构
words.ex: He is a suitor who brings flowers every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位每天送花的追求者。
words.en: A suitor is a man who wants to marry a particular woman.

words.tr: adj. 不拘礼仪的；随意的；无礼的；唐突的
words.ex: He left the meeting in an unceremonious way.
words.ex_cn: 他以一种不拘礼节的方式离开了会议。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as unceremonious, you mean it is done in a sudden, rude, or informal way without any regard for formalities or politeness.

words.ex: He told an untruth to avoid trouble.
words.ex_cn: 他说了个不实之词来避免麻烦。
words.en: An untruth is a statement that is not true; a lie.

words.ex: The viscount lives in a big castle.
words.ex_cn: 子爵住在一座大城堡里。
words.en: A viscount is a British nobleman ranking above a baron and below an earl.

chapters.name: 描述类词汇 人物正面描述 重点词

words.ex: He has business acumen and makes smart decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他有商业洞察力，能做出明智的决定。
words.en: The ability to make good judgments and quick decisions, typically in a particular domain.

words.ex: He is adroit at fixing broken machines.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长修理坏掉的机器。
words.en: Someone who is adroit is quick and skillful in their thoughts, behavior, or actions.

words.tr: adj. 和蔼可亲的；亲切友好的
words.ex: He is an amiable man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Someone who is amiable is friendly and pleasant to be with.

words.ex: They had an amicable talk after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 争吵之后，他们进行了一次友好的交谈。
words.en: When people have an amicable relationship, they are pleasant towards each other and solve their problems without arguing.

words.ex: He was born in August.
words.ex_cn: 他出生在八月。
words.en: August is the eighth month of the Gregorian calendar, following July and preceding September.

words.tr: adj. 坦率的；坦诚的；偷拍的
words.ex: He gave a candid answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了坦率的回答。
words.en: If you are candid, you are honest and say what you really think.

words.tr: adj. 精明的；老谋深算的
words.ex: He is a canny trader who always makes smart choices.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精明的交易员，总是做出明智的选择。
words.en: A canny person is clever and able to think quickly, especially in business or politics.

words.tr: adj. 有同情心的；表示怜悯的；
words.ex: She is a compassionate teacher who helps struggling students.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位有同情心的老师，帮助学习困难的学生。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as compassionate, you mean that they feel or show pity, sympathy, and understanding for people who are suffering.

words.ex: He kept his composure during the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他在面试中保持了冷静。
words.en: The state of being calm and in control of your emotions.

words.tr: adj. 考虑周到的；体贴的；
words.ex: He is considerate and always asks if others need help.
words.ex_cn: 他很体贴，总是问别人是否需要帮助。
words.en: Someone who is considerate pays attention to the needs, wishes, or feelings of other people.

words.ex: He was courteous to everyone he met.
words.ex_cn: 他对遇到的每个人都很有礼貌。
words.en: Someone who is courteous is polite and respectful to other people.

words.ex: The movie was incredible.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影太棒了。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as incredible, you like them very much or are impressed by them, because they are extremely or unusually good.

words.ex: His decisive action saved the team.
words.ex_cn: 他果断的行动拯救了团队。
words.en: If a fact, action, or event is decisive, it makes it certain that there will be a particular result.

words.ex: The chef made a deft cut with the knife.
words.ex_cn: 厨师用刀熟练地切了一下。
words.en: A deft action is skilful and often quick.

words.ex: The surgeon's dexterity saved the patient's life.
words.ex_cn: 外科医生的灵巧救了病人的命。
words.en: Skill and grace in physical movement, especially in the use of the hands; adroitness.

words.tr: adj. 有辨别力的；能洞悉的；眼光敏锐的； v. “discern”的现在分词；
words.ex: She is a discerning shopper who always finds the best quality.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有辨别力的购物者，总是能找到最好的质量。
words.en: If you describe someone as discerning, you mean that they are able to judge which things of a particular kind are good and which are bad.

words.ex: The judge was disinterested in the case.
words.ex_cn: 法官对这个案件持客观态度。
words.en: If someone is disinterested in something, they have no personal involvement or investment in it and are therefore able to judge it fairly.

words.ex: He is downright lazy.
words.ex_cn: 他完全懒惰。
words.en: You use downright to emphasize that something is completely the case, especially when you are describing something bad or negative.

words.ex: She wore an elegant dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条优雅的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe a person or thing as elegant, you mean that they are pleasing and graceful in appearance or style.

words.tr: adj. 雄辩的；有口才的；有说服力的
words.ex: He gave an eloquent speech at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上发表了富有感染力的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as eloquent, you mean that they are able to express their ideas and opinions well, so that other people understand them and are influenced by them.

words.tr: adj. 令人羡慕的；引起妒忌的；
words.ex: His perfect vacation looks enviable.
words.ex_cn: 他完美的假期看起来令人羡慕。
words.en: If you describe something such as a quality or ability as enviable, you mean that someone has it to a degree that other people admire or feel jealous of.

words.tr: adj. 可估量的；值得尊重的
words.ex: The cost of the project is estimable with current data.
words.ex_cn: 根据当前数据，这个项目的成本是可以估量的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as estimable, you mean that they deserve admiration because they are extremely good or have a very good quality.

words.tr: adj. 典范的；可做模范的；惩戒性的
words.ex: He is an exemplary student who always finishes his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名模范学生，总是完成作业。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as exemplary, you think they are extremely good and suitable to be copied by other people.

words.ex: He is farsighted and needs glasses to read books.
words.ex_cn: 他有远视，读书时需要戴眼镜。
words.en: Having the ability to anticipate and plan for the future; having good judgment about what will be needed in the future.

words.ex: He showed filial love by taking care of his old parents.
words.ex_cn: 他通过照顾年迈的父母表现出子女的孝心。
words.en: Filial is used to describe the relationship between children and their parents, especially emphasizing the duty and respect that children should show towards their parents.

words.tr: adj. 直截了当的；直率的；坦白的
words.ex: He is forthright about his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他坦率地承认自己的错误。
words.en: If you describe someone as forthright, you admire them because they show clearly and strongly what they think and feel.

words.ex: The twin boys are fraternal twins.
words.ex_cn: 这两个男孩是异卵双胞胎。
words.en: Fraternal is used to describe feelings or actions that are like those of a brother towards his brothers or sisters.

words.ex: The gallant soldier saved his comrades in battle.
words.ex_cn: 这位英勇的士兵在战斗中救了他的战友们。
words.en: If someone is gallant, they behave bravely and honorably in a dangerous or difficult situation. It can also describe someone who is very polite and kind towards women.

words.tr: adj. 亲切的；和蔼的；温暖的
words.ex: He is a genial man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Friendly and cheerful.

words.tr: adj. 文雅的；有教养的；上流社会的；装绅士派头的
words.ex: She spoke in a genteel way at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 她在晚宴上说话很文雅。
words.en: Someone who is genteel behaves in a polite and refined way, often in a manner that is considered typical of someone from a high social class.

words.ex: This is a genuine diamond.
words.ex_cn: 这是一颗真正的钻石。
words.en: If something is genuine, it is real and exactly what it appears to be.

words.tr:
adj. 健壮的；硬朗的
v. 强拉硬拖
words.ex: He is still hale at age 80.
words.ex_cn: 他80岁了依然身体健康。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially an old person, as hale, you mean that they are healthy.

words.ex: She hankers after a simpler life.
words.ex_cn: 她向往一种更简单的生活。
words.en: If you hanker after something, you have a strong desire for it.

words.ex: He carried a hefty bag full of books.
words.ex_cn: 他提着一个异常大的装满书的包。
words.en: Something that is hefty is large in size, weight, or amount.

words.tr: adj. 热血的；易激动的；感情冲动的
words.ex: He was a hot-blooded young man, always ready for a fight.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热血青年，随时准备打架。
words.en: If you describe someone as hot-blooded, you mean that they are very quick to express their emotions, especially anger and love.

words.ex: He showed humility after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得奖品后表现出了谦逊。
words.en: Humility is the quality of being humble and not thinking that you are better than other people.

words.ex: He is an illustrious scientist who won many awards.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位杰出的科学家，获得过许多奖项。
words.en: If you describe someone as illustrious, you mean that they are very well known because they have a high position in society or they have done something impressive.

words.tr: adj. 天生的；先天的；天赋的
words.ex: He has an inborn talent for music.
words.ex_cn: 他天生就有音乐才能。
words.en: An inborn quality or ability is one that you have had naturally since birth.

words.ex: His incisive comment solved the problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他一针见血的评论迅速解决了问题。
words.en: An incisive remark, question, or piece of writing is very clear and direct, and shows that the person understands something very well.

words.ex: The pope is considered infallible in matters of faith by some Catholics.
words.ex_cn: 一些天主教徒认为教皇在信仰问题上是一贯正确的。
words.en: If a person or thing is infallible, they are never wrong or never fail.

words.tr:
adj. 热恋着的；冲昏头脑的；入迷的
v. 使冲昏头脑；使着迷；“infatuate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She was infatuated with the new pop star.
words.ex_cn: 她对这位新晋流行歌手非常着迷。
words.en: If you are infatuated with someone, you have a very strong feeling of love or attraction for them, which usually does not last very long.

words.tr: adj. 有独创性的；巧妙的；
words.ex: The child came up with an ingenious way to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子想出了一个有独创性的方式来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Something that is ingenious is very clever and involves new ideas, methods, or equipment.

words.tr: adj. 单纯的；天真的；坦率的
words.ex: He gave an ingenuous smile when he told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 当他讲真话时，他露出了天真无邪的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as ingenuous, you mean that they are innocent, trusting, and honest, often in a way that seems naive.

words.ex: Babies have an innate ability to cry.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿生来就有哭泣的能力。
words.en: An innate quality or ability is one that you were born with, not one you have learned.

words.ex: The inquisitive child asked many questions about the stars.
words.ex_cn: 这个好奇的孩子问了很多关于星星的问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as inquisitive, you mean that they are interested in a lot of different things and want to find out more about them.

words.tr: adj. 明智的；有见识的；判断正确的
words.ex: He made a judicious choice about which book to buy.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个明智的买书决定。
words.en: If you describe an action or decision as judicious, you approve of it because you think that it shows good judgment and sense.

words.tr: adj. 宽宏大量的；有雅量的
words.ex: He was magnanimous and forgave his enemy.
words.ex_cn: 他宽宏大量，原谅了他的敌人。
words.en: If you are magnanimous, you behave kindly and generously toward someone, especially after defeating them or being treated badly by them.

words.tr: adj. 一丝不苟的；缜密的
words.ex: He is meticulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他仔细检查作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as meticulous, you mean that they do things very carefully and with great attention to detail.

words.tr: adj. 灵活的；敏捷的；机敏的
words.ex: The cat is nimble and jumps over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫很敏捷，跳过了篱笆。
words.en: Someone who is nimble is able to move their fingers, hands, or legs quickly and easily.

words.tr: adj. 观察力敏锐的；谨慎遵守的；
words.ex: She is observant and notices small details.
words.ex_cn: 她观察力敏锐，能注意到细小的细节。
words.en: Someone who is observant pays close attention to things and notices more about them than most people do.

words.tr: adj. 全知的；无所不知的
words.ex: The omniscient narrator knows everything about the characters.
words.ex_cn: 全知的叙述者了解角色的一切。
words.en: Knowing everything; having infinite awareness, understanding, and insight.

words.tr: adj. 外向的；即将离职的；往外去的；
words.ex: He is an outgoing boy who loves talking to new people.
words.ex_cn: 他是个外向的男孩，喜欢和新朋友聊天。
words.en: Someone who is outgoing is very friendly and likes meeting and talking to people.

words.tr:
adv. 彻底地；立刻地；
adj. 完全的；彻底的；
words.ex: He refused the offer outright.
words.ex_cn: 他彻底拒绝了这个提议。
words.en: If something is done outright, it is done completely and without any hesitation or attempt to hide it.

words.tr: adj. 直言无讳的；坦率的；
words.ex: He is an outspoken teacher who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位直言不讳的老师，总是说真话。
words.en: Someone who is outspoken expresses their opinions frankly and honestly, even if they are likely to shock or offend people.

words.ex: The boy is a piano prodigy at age six.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩六岁时就是一位钢琴奇才。
words.en: A prodigy is someone who is unusually young and has a great natural ability in a particular area.

words.tr: adj. 有先见之明的；深谋远虑的
words.ex: He is a provident man who saves money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有远见的人，会为未来存钱。
words.en: Making provision for the future; exercising foresight or forethought.

words.tr: n. 高超的技艺；造诣；英勇；
words.ex: His prowess in basketball amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在篮球方面的高超技艺让所有人都惊叹。
words.en: Exceptional skill or ability in a particular field or activity.

words.tr: adj. 谨慎的；慎重的；精明的
words.ex: He is prudent with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他在花钱时很谨慎。
words.en: If you are prudent, you are careful and avoid taking unnecessary risks.

words.ex: He is a reliable friend who always helps.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个可靠的朋友，总是帮忙。
words.en: Able to be trusted to do or provide what is needed or right.

words.tr: adj. 坚决的；毅然的；有决心的；
words.ex: He was resolute in his decision to quit smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他决心戒烟。
words.en: If you describe someone as resolute, you approve of them because they are very determined not to change their mind or not to give up a course of action.

words.ex: He earned a respectable salary last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年挣了一份可观的薪水。
words.en: Someone or something that is respectable is approved of by society and considered to be morally correct.

words.ex: He showed reverence for his grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他对祖父表示尊敬。
words.en: A feeling of profound respect for someone or something.

words.ex: She added sage to the stuffing for Thanksgiving dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她在感恩节晚餐的填料中加入了鼠尾草。
words.en: A sage is a person who is regarded as being very wise, especially someone who is known for their good judgment and deep understanding of life.

words.tr: adj. 遮遮掩掩的；守口如瓶的；
words.ex: He gave a secretive smile and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他露出一个遮遮掩掩的微笑，然后走开了。
words.en: If you are secretive, you like to have secrets and to keep your knowledge, feelings, or intentions hidden.

words.tr: adj. 明智的；有判断力的；恰当的；合理的；
words.ex: It is sensible to wear a coat in cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 在寒冷的天气里穿外套是明智的。
words.en: A sensible person is able to make good judgments and decisions based on reason rather than emotion.

words.ex: He gave a sincere apology.
words.ex_cn: 他真诚地道歉了。
words.en: If you say that someone is sincere, you approve of them because they really mean the things they say.

words.ex: The car has a sleek design.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车有着流畅的外形。
words.en: Sleek describes something that is smooth, glossy, and streamlined, often implying a sense of elegance and efficiency.

words.tr: adj. 精密复杂的；老练的；
words.ex: The phone has a sophisticated camera.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个精密复杂的摄像头。
words.en: A sophisticated person is intelligent and knows a lot, so that they are able to understand complicated situations. A sophisticated machine, device, or method is more advanced or complex than others.

words.tr:
adj. 忠实的；坚定的
v. 止住（血等的）流出
words.ex: He is a staunch supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的坚定支持者。
words.en: A staunch person is someone who is very loyal and firm in their beliefs or support for someone or something.

words.tr: n. 容许；忍耐；勉强同意
words.ex: He stayed out of pity, out of sufferance.
words.ex_cn: 他留下来是出于同情，出于容忍。
words.en: If you do something on sufferance, you do it because someone allows you to, although they do not really want you to.

words.ex: He answered the question with tact.
words.ex_cn: 他机智地回答了这个问题。
words.en: If you describe what someone says or does as tact, you mean that it is polite, considerate, and shows an understanding of other people's feelings.

words.ex: The weather was tolerable, so we went for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 天气还可以忍受，所以我们去散步了。
words.en: If something is tolerable, it is acceptable or bearable, even though it is not very good or pleasant.

words.ex: You need to pay the upfront fee before the service starts.
words.ex_cn: 你需要在服务开始前支付预付款。
words.en: If you are upfront about something, you are honest and open about it.

words.ex: The venerable teacher has taught for over 40 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位值得尊敬的老师已经教书40多年了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as venerable, you mean that they are old and respected.

words.ex: People venerate the ancient sage for his wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 人们因他的智慧而崇敬这位古代圣人。
words.en: To regard with respect or reverence.

words.ex: He was wary of strangers who offered free gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些提供免费礼物的陌生人保持谨慎。
words.en: If you are wary of something or someone, you are cautious because you do not know much about them and you believe they may be dangerous or cause problems.

chapters.name: 描述类词汇 人物正面描述 认知词

words.ex: He can solve the problem ably.
words.ex_cn: 他能出色地解决这个问题。
words.en: In a competent or capable manner.

words.tr:
adv. 光明正大地
adj. 光明正大的
words.ex: He always plays aboveboard in business.
words.ex_cn: 他在商业中总是光明正大。
words.en: If something is aboveboard, it is done in an honest and open way without any attempt to deceive.

words.ex: He was adamant about not changing his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他坚定不移地不改变主意。
words.en: If someone is adamant about something, they are determined not to change their mind about it.

words.tr: adj. 谦恭有礼的；和蔼可亲的
words.ex: He is an affable man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Someone who is affable is pleasant and friendly.

words.ex: His benevolence helped the poor family.
words.ex_cn: 他的仁慈帮助了这个贫困家庭。
words.en: The quality of being well meaning; kindness.

words.ex: His bravery saved the children from the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他的勇敢救了孩子们于火海之中。
words.en: Bravery is the quality of being brave; courage.

words.ex: He spoke with certitude about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 他对于这个答案说话时充满确信。
words.en: A feeling of being certain or convinced about something.

words.tr: v. 犯罪；做错事；“commit”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 忠诚的；
words.ex: He was committed for stealing a car.
words.ex_cn: 他因偷车而被定罪。
words.en: If you are committed to something, you are willing to give your time and energy to it because you believe in it.

words.tr: n. 坚定不移；持久不变
words.ex: His constancy never changes, even when things are hard.
words.ex_cn: 他的坚定从不改变，即使事情很艰难。
words.en: The quality of being unchanging or unwavering, especially in one's loyalty or affections.

words.ex: The courageous firefighter saved the child from the burning house.
words.ex_cn: 这位勇敢的消防员从着火的房子里救出了孩子。
words.en: Someone who is courageous shows courage.

words.ex: The puppy is cute.
words.ex_cn: 这只小狗很可爱。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as cute, you mean that they are attractive, often in a childlike or youthful way.

words.tr: adj. 勇敢的；无所畏惧的；不屈不挠的
words.ex: The dauntless firefighter ran into the burning building.
words.ex_cn: 这位无畏的消防员冲进了着火的建筑。
words.en: If you describe someone as dauntless, you mean they are not easily frightened or discouraged from doing something.

words.ex: He showed decency by helping the old man.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助那位老人，表现出了礼貌和善良。
words.en: Decency is behaviour that is considered to be polite, moral, and acceptable.

words.tr: adj. 符合礼仪的；得体的；高雅的
words.ex: She behaved in a decorous way at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 她在晚宴上举止得体。
words.en: If you say that something is decorous, you mean that it is dignified, proper, and socially acceptable.

words.tr: n. 礼貌得体；适宜的举止
words.ex: He maintained decorum during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议期间保持了得体的行为。
words.en: Decorum is behavior that is controlled, calm, and polite, especially in formal situations.

words.ex: His devotion to his family is obvious.
words.ex_cn: 他对家庭的献身显而易见。
words.en: Devotion is great love, affection, or admiration for someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；衷心的；诚挚的；
words.ex: He is a devout Christian who goes to church every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名虔诚的基督徒，每周日都去教堂。
words.en: If you describe someone as devout, you mean that they have a deep religious faith.

words.ex: The old man walked with a dignified posture.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人以有尊严的姿态行走。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is dignified, you mean they are calm, impressive and deserve respect.

words.tr: v. 区分；“distinguish”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 卓越的；著名的；
words.ex: He distinguished the fake coin from the real one.
words.ex_cn: 他把假硬币和真硬币区分开来。
words.en: If you describe a person or their work as distinguished, you mean that they have been very successful in their career and have a good reputation.

words.ex: He is a dutiful son who helps his parents every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个孝顺的儿子，每天帮助父母。
words.en: Someone who is dutiful is careful to do the things that they are expected to do.

words.ex: He is an easygoing man who likes to smile.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个随和的人，喜欢微笑。
words.en: Someone who is easygoing is relaxed and not easily upset or worried.

words.ex: His eloquence moved everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他的雄辩打动了房间里每一个人。
words.en: The ability to speak or write in a way that is fluent, persuasive, and expressive.

words.ex: He is a man of great eminence in science.
words.ex_cn: 他在科学界享有很高的声望。
words.en: Eminence refers to a position of great distinction or superiority, especially in a particular field or profession.

words.tr: adj. 有活力的；精力旺盛的；
words.ex: The energetic boy ran around the park all afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 这个有活力的男孩整个下午都在公园里跑来跑去。
words.en: Someone who is energetic is very active and does not tire easily.

words.ex: The erudite professor knows many ancient languages.
words.ex_cn: 这位博学的教授懂得许多古代语言。
words.en: Having or showing great knowledge or learning.

words.ex: He showed excellence in math competitions.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学竞赛中表现出色。
words.en: The quality of being outstanding or extremely good.

words.ex: The expansive desert stretches for miles.
words.ex_cn: 广阔的沙漠延伸数英里。
words.en: If you describe something such as a period of time or a piece of writing as expansive, you mean that it is very long or detailed.

words.ex: Her expressive eyes showed all her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 她富有表情的眼睛展现了她所有的感情。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as expressive, you mean that their behaviour clearly indicates their feelings or intentions.

words.ex: He extols the beauty of nature every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天赞美大自然的美。
words.en: If you extol something or someone, you praise them enthusiastically.

words.tr:
n. 性格外向者；爱交际的人
adj. 外向的
words.ex: He is an extrovert who loves talking to people.
words.ex_cn: 他是个外向的人，喜欢和人交谈。
words.en: An extrovert is someone who is very outgoing, sociable, and enjoys being around other people.

words.ex: He is an extravert who loves talking to people.
words.ex_cn: 他是个外向的人，喜欢和人交谈。
words.en: An extravert is someone who is outgoing and sociable, deriving energy from being around other people.

words.tr: n. 先见；预见；先见之明
words.ex: He showed foresight by saving money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他通过为未来存钱展现了远见。
words.en: The ability to predict or the action of predicting what will happen or be needed in the future.

words.ex: Her forethought in planning the event ensured its success.
words.ex_cn: 她在计划活动时的事先考虑确保了活动的成功。
words.en: If you use forethought, you think carefully before you do something in order to avoid problems or to make sure it is successful.

words.tr:
n. 专长；特长
adv. 用强音
words.ex: His forte is playing the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他的强项是弹钢琴。
words.en: A thing at which someone excels.

words.ex: His generosity helped the poor family.
words.ex_cn: 他的慷慨帮助了那个贫困的家庭。
words.en: Generosity is the quality of being kind and generous.

words.tr: adj. 优雅的；优美的；得体的；
words.ex: The dancer moved in a graceful way.
words.ex_cn: 这位舞者动作优雅。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as graceful, you mean that they move in a smooth, controlled, and attractive way.

words.tr: adj. 亲切的；和蔼的；仁慈的
words.ex: She was gracious and thanked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 她很友善，感谢了每一个人。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially someone you think is superior to you, as gracious, you mean that they are very well-mannered and pleasant.

words.ex: The grandeur of the palace amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿的宏伟让每个人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality of being grand or splendid in appearance or style.

words.ex: Dolphins are gregarious animals that swim in groups.
words.ex_cn: 海豚是群居动物，成群游泳。
words.en: Someone who is gregarious enjoys being with other people.

words.tr: adv. 帅气地；慷慨地；相当优厚地；气派地
words.ex: He rewarded the employee handsomely for his hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他慷慨地奖励了那位辛勤工作的员工。
words.en: In a generous or ample manner; in a way that is attractive or beautiful.

words.tr: adj. 通过经历而变得顽强的；坚毅的；冷酷无情的
words.ex: The hard-bitten soldier never gave up, even in the face of overwhelming odds.
words.ex_cn: 面对压倒性的劣势，这位顽强的士兵也从未放弃。
words.en: If you describe someone as hard-bitten, you mean that they have been through a lot of difficult or unpleasant experiences and are tough as a result.

words.tr: adj. 讲究实际的；头脑清晰的；不感情用事的
words.ex: He is hardheaded and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很固执，不会改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as hardheaded, you mean that they are practical and determined to get what they want, and do not let emotions or other people's opinions affect them.

words.ex: The heroic firefighter saved the child from the burning house.
words.ex_cn: 这位英勇的消防员从着火的房子里救出了孩子。
words.en: If you describe a person or their actions as heroic, you admire them because they show extreme bravery.

words.ex: The film is an homage to old Hollywood movies.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是对老好莱坞电影的致敬。
words.en: Homage is respect shown towards someone or something you admire, or to a person in authority.

words.ex: The climate is hospitable for growing oranges.
words.ex_cn: 这种气候适合种植橙子。
words.en: If someone is hospitable, they are friendly, welcoming, and generous to guests or strangers.

words.ex: The child gave an imaginative story about flying cats.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子讲了一个关于会飞的猫的富有想象力的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone or their ideas as imaginative, you are praising them because they are easily able to think of or create new or exciting things.

words.ex: Legends say that some heroes are immortal.
words.ex_cn: 传说有些英雄是不死的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as immortal, you mean that they are so famous or popular that they will be remembered for a very long time.

words.ex: His speech was very impressive.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲非常令人印象深刻。
words.en: Something that is impressive makes you admire it because it is very good, large, important, etc.

words.ex: His ingenuity solved the problem with a simple tool.
words.ex_cn: 他的独创力用一个简单的工具解决了问题。
words.en: Ingenuity is the ability to think of clever and original ways to solve problems.

words.ex: The intrepid explorer climbed the high mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这位无畏的探险家爬上了高山。
words.en: If you describe someone as intrepid, you mean that they are brave, fearless, and willing to do things that might be dangerous.

words.ex: She kindly helped me with my homework.
words.ex_cn: 她亲切地帮我做作业。
words.en: If someone is kindly, they are friendly and behave in a gentle and caring way.

words.ex: The judge showed leniency toward the first-time offender.
words.ex_cn: 法官对初犯表现出了宽大。
words.en: Leniency is the quality of being more merciful or tolerant than expected.

words.tr: n. 宽大；仁慈；宽大，仁慈( leniency的名词复数 )；
words.ex: The judge showed lenience toward the first-time offender.
words.ex_cn: 法官对初犯表现出了宽大。
words.en: The quality of being more merciful or tolerant than expected.

words.tr: adj. 宽厚的；仁慈的；不严格的；
words.ex: The teacher was lenient with students who were late.
words.ex_cn: 老师对迟到的学生很宽厚。
words.en: If you are lenient with someone, you are not strict in the way you treat them, especially when they have done something wrong.

words.ex: He is loyal to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友忠诚。
words.en: Someone who is loyal remains firm in their friendship or support for a person or thing.

words.ex: His loyalty to his friends never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的忠诚从未改变。
words.en: The quality of being loyal to someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 男子汉气概的；大男子主义的
words.ex: He acts macho to impress his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他为了给朋友留下深刻印象而表现得阳刚。
words.en: If you describe a man as macho, you mean that he behaves in a way that is traditionally associated with men, such as being very strong, brave, or aggressive.

words.tr: adj. 大丈夫气概的；刚毅的；勇敢的
words.ex: He showed a manful determination to overcome his challenges.
words.ex_cn: 他表现出克服挑战的勇敢决心。
words.en: If you describe a man's behaviour as manful, you mean that he behaves in a way which is traditionally considered to be brave and strong.

words.ex: His modesty made everyone like him.
words.ex_cn: 他的谦虚让所有人都喜欢他。
words.en: Modesty is the quality of not being too proud or confident about yourself or your abilities.

words.tr: adj. 慈善的；乐善好施的；
words.ex: He made a philanthropic donation to help poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他捐赠了一笔慈善款项来帮助贫困儿童。
words.en: A philanthropic person or organization freely gives money or other help to people who need it.

words.tr: adj. 享有声望的；声望很高的；
words.ex: He got into a prestigious university.
words.ex_cn: 他进入了一所享有声望的大学。
words.en: A prestigious institution, job, or activity is respected and admired because it is considered to be of very high quality.

words.ex: His rectitude in business dealings was well-known.
words.ex_cn: 他在商业交易中的正直是众所周知的。
words.en: Moral integrity; honesty and correctness of judgement or behaviour.

words.tr: adj. 有声望的；声誉好的
words.ex: He works for a reputable company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家信誉良好的公司工作。
words.en: A reputable person or organization is considered to be good and trustworthy by most people.

words.tr: adj. 尊重人的；表示敬意的
words.ex: He is always respectful to his teachers.
words.ex_cn: 他总是对老师很尊敬。
words.en: If you are respectful, you show respect for someone.

words.tr: adj. 精明练达的；有远见的；有洞察力的
words.ex: He is a sagacious man who always makes wise choices.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个睿智的人，总是做出明智的选择。
words.en: Having or showing keen mental discernment and good judgment; shrewd.

words.ex: Her sagacity in business matters was widely recognized.
words.ex_cn: 她在商业事务上的睿智广为人知。
words.en: The quality of being sagacious; wisdom and good judgment.

words.tr: n. 发出火花；闪烁；才华横溢
words.ex: The scintillation of the stars in the night sky was mesmerizing.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中星星的闪烁令人着迷。
words.en: Scintillation refers to the act of emitting sparks or flashes of light, or to the quality of being brilliantly clever or witty.

words.ex: He is scrupulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他检查作业时一丝不苟。
words.en: If you are scrupulous, you are careful, thorough, and extremely attentive to details.

words.tr: adj. 自我谦避的；不求闻达的
words.ex: She was self-effacing and never sought the limelight.
words.ex_cn: 她为人谦逊，从不追求聚光灯下的生活。
words.en: Someone who is self-effacing does not like to attract attention to themselves or to their abilities or achievements.

words.tr: adj. 有自制力的；沉着的；镇静的
words.ex: She remained self-possessed even when the news shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 即使这个消息让所有人都震惊了，她依然保持冷静自制。
words.en: If you are self-possessed, you are calm and confident and in control of your emotions.

words.tr: adj. 样子好看的；匀称的；线条优美的
words.ex: She has a very shapely figure.
words.ex_cn: 她有着非常匀称的身材。
words.en: Having an attractive shape; well-proportioned.

words.ex: He spoke with sincerity.
words.ex_cn: 他真诚地说话。
words.en: Sincerity is the quality of being free from pretense, deceit, or hypocrisy.

words.tr:
adj. 光滑的；圆滑的；熟练的；华而不实的
n. 浮油层；光滑之处
v. 使平滑
words.ex: The ice on the road was slick.
words.ex_cn: 路上的冰很光滑。
words.en: If something is slick, it is done smoothly and efficiently, often in a way that is intended to be impressive.

words.tr: n. 清醒；镇定；严肃；节制
words.ex: He values sobriety after his accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后重视清醒。
words.en: The state of being sober, especially in terms of not being under the influence of alcohol.

words.tr: n. 运动员精神；运动家的风度
words.ex: He showed good sportsmanship after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在输掉比赛后展现了良好的体育精神。
words.en: Sportsmanship is behaviour and attitudes that show respect for the rules of a game and for the other players.

words.ex: He is a stalwart of the environmental movement.
words.ex_cn: 他是环保运动的坚定分子。
words.en: A stalwart person is someone who is very loyal and committed to a person, belief, or cause and is not likely to change their views or behavior.

words.ex: He is steadfast in his beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己信念坚定不移。
words.en: If someone is steadfast, they are very loyal and constant in their attitudes or actions.

words.ex: The instructions were straightforward and easy to follow.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明很简单，容易遵循。
words.en: If you describe something as straightforward, you approve of it because it is easy to do or understand.

words.tr:
adj. 崇高的；壮丽的；极端的；过分的
v. 变高尚；升华
n. 庄严；崇高；顶点
words.ex: The view from the mountain is sublime.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色是壮丽的。
words.en: If you describe something as sublime, you mean that it has a wonderful quality that affects you deeply.

words.tr: adj. 机智的；圆滑的；得体的
words.ex: He was tactful when he said no to her request.
words.ex_cn: 当他拒绝她的请求时，他很得体。
words.en: If you describe someone as tactful, you approve of them because they are careful not to say or do anything that would offend or upset other people.

words.ex: He is a talented singer.
words.ex_cn: 他是个有才能的歌手。
words.en: Someone who is talented has a natural ability to do something well.

words.ex: He gave a thoughtful answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个深思的答案。
words.en: If you are thoughtful, you are quiet and serious because you are thinking about something.

words.ex: She is thrifty and saves money every week.
words.ex_cn: 她很节约，每周都存钱。
words.en: If you say that someone is thrifty, you are praising them for saving money and not spending it on unnecessary things.

words.ex: The titan built a huge bridge with his hands.
words.ex_cn: 这位巨人用手建造了一座巨大的桥。
words.en: A titan is someone or something that is extremely large, powerful, or important.

words.tr: adj. 不装腔作势的；低调谦逊的；
words.ex: He is an unassuming man who never talks about his achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个不装腔作势的人，从不谈论自己的成就。
words.en: If you describe someone as unassuming, you approve of them because they are quiet and do not try to appear important.

words.tr: adj. 谦逊的；不夸耀的；不矫饰的
words.ex: The house had an unpretentious charm that made it feel welcoming.
words.ex_cn: 这座房子有一种不炫耀的魅力，让人感到宾至如归。
words.en: If you describe a place, person, or thing as unpretentious, you approve of them because they are simple in appearance or character, rather than sophisticated or luxurious.

words.ex: The rain was unremitting all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨一整天都没有停过。
words.en: If you describe someone's effort or activity as unremitting, you mean that it is continued without stopping or becoming less intense.

words.tr: adj. 坚定的；不懈的；始终如一的
words.ex: He has unswerving loyalty to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友有着坚定不移的忠诚。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude, feeling, or way of behaving as unswerving, you mean that it is strong and firm and does not weaken or change.

words.tr: adj. 有男子气概的；阳刚的；强有力的
words.ex: He is a virile man who works hard every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精力充沛的男子，每天努力工作。
words.en: If you describe a man as virile, you mean that he has the qualities that a man is traditionally expected to have, such as strength and sexual power.

words.tr: adj. 品行端正的；品德高的；
words.ex: He is a virtuous man who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个品行端正的人，总是说真话。
words.en: Having or showing high moral standards.

chapters.name: 描述类词汇 人物反面描述 重点词

words.ex: He made an abrupt stop at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 他在红灯前突然停了下来。
words.en: If something happens abruptly, it happens suddenly and unexpectedly.

words.ex: He gave an artful answer to the tricky question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个棘手的问题给出了一个巧妙的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as artful, you mean that they are clever and skillful at achieving what they want, especially by deceiving people.

words.tr: adj. 残暴的；恶劣的；糟透的
words.ex: The dictator committed atrocious acts against his people.
words.ex_cn: 这位独裁者对人民犯下了残暴的罪行。
words.en: If you describe something as atrocious, you are emphasizing that its quality is very bad.

words.tr: adj. 大胆的；鲁莽的；大胆创新的
words.ex: He made an audacious plan to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个大胆的计划，独自攀登那座山。
words.en: If you describe someone as audacious, you mean that they take risks in order to achieve something and show a willingness to challenge conventional ideas.

words.tr: adj. 棒极了；令人敬畏的；令人畏惧的；
words.ex: The concert was awesome!
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会棒极了！
words.en: If you describe someone or something as awesome, you are emphasizing that you think that they are very impressive or extraordinary.

words.ex: He felt awkward when he forgot his friend's name.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记朋友的名字时，他感到很尴尬。
words.en: If you describe a situation as awkward, you mean that it is embarrassing or difficult to deal with.

words.ex: The movie had a banal plot that everyone had seen before.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的剧情平庸得让人看过了无数次。
words.en: If you describe something as banal, you do not like it because you think that it is so ordinary that it is not at all effective or interesting.

words.tr: adj. 离奇的；奇特的；奇怪的；
words.ex: The clown wore a bizarre hat with three eyes.
words.ex_cn: 小丑戴着一顶有三只眼睛的离奇帽子。
words.en: Something that is bizarre is very odd and strange.

words.tr: n. 废弃物（树枝、碎石等）；
words.ex: The workers cleared the brash from the construction site.
words.ex_cn: 工人们清除了建筑工地上的废弃物。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behavior as brash, you disapprove of them because you think that they are too confident and aggressive.

words.tr: adj. 懦弱的；毫无志气的；
words.ex: He was craven and ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他很懦弱，逃跑了。
words.en: If you describe someone as craven, you are criticizing them for being very cowardly.

words.ex: He is credulous and believes every story he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他很轻信，相信他听到的每一个故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as credulous, you have a low opinion of them because they are too ready to believe what people tell them and are easily deceived.

words.tr:
adj. 弯曲的；扭曲的；欺诈的；不老实的
v. （使）弯曲；使成钩状；“crook”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The path was crooked and hard to walk on.
words.ex_cn: 这条路是弯曲的，很难走。
words.en: If you describe something as crooked, especially something that is usually straight, you mean that it is bent or twisted.

words.tr: adj. 匆匆的；粗略的；仓促的
words.ex: He gave the report a cursory look.
words.ex_cn: 他粗略地看了看这份报告。
words.en: A cursory glance or examination is a quick one that is not very thorough.

words.tr: adj. 愚笨的；癫狂的；痴傻的
words.ex: He wore a daft hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶傻气的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as daft, you mean that they are silly, foolish, or crazy.

words.tr: adj. 神志不清的；极度兴奋的；发狂的
words.ex: He was delirious after the fever.
words.ex_cn: 他发烧后神志不清。
words.en: If someone is delirious, they are not able to think or speak in a sensible and reasonable way, usually because they are very ill and have a fever.

words.ex: He was a despicable liar who hurt everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个可鄙的骗子，伤害了所有人。
words.en: If you say that a person or action is despicable, you are emphasizing that they are extremely nasty, cruel, or evil.

words.tr: adj. 不直接的；不正直的；迂回的；
words.ex: He gave a devious answer to avoid telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个不直接的回答，以避免说出真相。
words.en: If you describe someone as devious, you mean that they are dishonest and unfair in the way that they behave, often by using indirect methods to achieve their aims.

words.tr:
n. 伪装；伪装物；
v. 伪装；掩饰；
words.ex: He wore a hat and glasses as a disguise.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了帽子和眼镜作为伪装。
words.en: To disguise means to change your appearance or behavior so that people will not recognize you, or to make something seem different from what it really is.

words.ex: The illness had enfeebled her to the point of immobility.
words.ex_cn: 疾病使她衰弱到几乎不能动弹的地步。
words.en: To make someone or something very weak.

words.tr: adj. 游历的；游离不定的；行为不当的；出轨的
words.ex: The errant knight traveled far across the land.
words.ex_cn: 这位游历的骑士穿越了广袤的土地。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as errant, you mean that they have strayed from the proper course or standards.

words.tr: adj. 不稳定的；飘忽不定的；
words.ex: The weather has been erratic this month.
words.ex_cn: 这个月的天气一直不稳定。
words.en: Something that is erratic does not follow a regular pattern, but happens at unexpected times or moves in unexpected directions.

words.ex: He bought an extravagant car that cost too much money.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆奢侈的车，价格太贵了。
words.en: Spending much more than is necessary or wise; excessively expensive.

words.tr: v. 无法做到；失败；“fail”的现在分词； adj. 减弱中的； n. 失败；
words.ex: He was failing to finish the race.
words.ex_cn: 他没能完成比赛。
words.en: A failing is a fault or a weakness in someone's character or abilities.

words.ex: He is too faint-hearted to speak in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他太胆小了，不敢在全班面前说话。
words.en: Lacking courage or determination; timid.

words.ex: His argument is fallacious because it ignores the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点是错误的，因为它忽略了事实。
words.en: If an idea, argument, or reason is fallacious, it is wrong because it is based on a fallacy.

words.ex: He tried to falsify the report.
words.ex_cn: 他试图篡改报告。
words.en: To falsify means to change something in order to deceive people, or to make a false statement.

words.ex: The child told a fanciful story about flying dragons.
words.ex_cn: 孩子讲了一个关于会飞的龙的富于幻想的故事。
words.en: If you describe an idea as fanciful, you mean that it is imaginative rather than reasonable or practical.

words.tr: adj. 愚昧的；昏庸的；愚笨的
words.ex: His fatuous smile made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他那愚蠢的微笑让每个人都感到不舒服。
